}\n\n    fn published_tool_name(&self, upstream_name: &str) -> String {\n        let raw_name = upstream_name\n            .split_once(':')\n            .map(|(_, name)| name)\n            .unwrap_or(upstream_name);\n\n        let mut normalized = String::with_capacity(raw_name.len());\n        let mut last_was_underscore = false;\n\n        for ch in raw_name.chars() {\n            let ch = ch.to_ascii_lowercase();\n            if ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {\n                normalized.push(ch);\n                last_was_underscore = false;\n            } else if !last_was_underscore {\n                normalized.push('_');\n                last_was_underscore = true;\n            }\n        }\n\n        let normalized = normalized.trim_matches('_');\n        if normalized.is_empty() {\n            raw_name.to_string()\n        } else {\n            normalized.to_string()\n        }\n    }\n}\n\npub async fn register_notebooklm_tools(registry: &ToolRegistry) -> Result<usize> {\n    let config = NotebookLmConfig::from_env();\n    if !config.enabled {\n        tracing::info!(\"NotebookLM MCP bridge disabled\");\n        return Ok(0);\n    }\n\n    let mut client = ExternalMcpClient::new(config.external_config());\n    if let Err(error) = client.start().await {\n        tracing::warn!(\n            error = %error,\n            command = %config.command,\n            args = ?config.args,\n            \"NotebookLM MCP sidecar failed to start; continuing without NotebookLM tools\"\n        );\n        return Ok(0);\n    }\n\n    let upstream_tools = client.get_tools().await;\n    if upstream_tools.is_empty() {\n        tracing::warn!(\"NotebookLM MCP sidecar started but returned no tools\");\n        return Ok(0);\n    }\n\n    let shared_client = Arc::new(Mutex::new(client));\n    let mut registered = 0usize;\n\n    for tool in upstream_tools {\n        let published_name = config.published_tool_name(&tool.name);\n        let wrapper = NotebookLmTool::new(shared_client.clone(), tool, published_name);\n        registry.register(Arc::new(wrapper) as BoxedTool).await?;\n        registered += 1;\n    }\n\n    tracing::info!(registered, \"Registered NotebookLM MCP tools\");\n    Ok(registered)\n}\n\nstruct NotebookLmTool {\n    client: Arc<Mutex<ExternalMcpClient>>,\n    upstream_name: String,\n    name: String,\n    description: String,\n    input_schema: Value,\n}\n\nimpl NotebookLmTool {\n    fn new(client: Arc<Mutex<ExternalMcpClient>>, tool: ExternalTool, name: String) -> Self {\n        let upstream_name = tool\n            .name\n            .split_once(':')\n            .map(|(_, raw_name)| raw_name.to_string())\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| tool.name.clone());\n\n        Self {\n            client,\n            upstream_name,\n            name,\n            description: format!(\"NotebookLM MCP: {}\", tool.description),\n            input_schema: tool.input_schema,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl Tool for NotebookLmTool {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.name\n    }\n\n    fn description(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.description\n    }\n\n    fn input_schema(&self) -> Value {\n        self.input_schema.clone()\n    }\n\n    fn category(&self) -> &str {\n        \"cognitive\"\n    }\n\n    fn namespace(&self) -> &str {\n        \"notebooklm\"\n    }\n\n    fn tags(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        vec![\n            \"notebooklm\".to_string(),\n            \"rag\".to_string(),\n            \"research\".to_string(),\n        ]\n    }\n\n    async fn execute(&self, input: Value) -> Result<Value> {\n        // Robustness: retry with exponential backoff + session rotation\n        // per {\n            if attempt > 0 {\n                let delay = BASE_DELAY_MS * (1 << (attempt - 1));\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    tool = %self.name,\n .description(description);\n\n    if let Some(obj) = state.as_object() {\n        for (key, value) in obj.iter() {\n            builder = builder.field(&key.to_string(), field_from_value(value));\n infer_field_type(value: &Value) -> FieldType {\n    use simd_json::prelude::*;\n\n    if value.is_null() {\n        FieldType::Any\n    } else if value.as_bool().is_some() {\n        FieldType::Boolean\n    } else if value.as_i64().is_some() || value.as_u64().is_some() {\n        FieldType::Integer\n    } else if value.as_f64().is_some() {\n        FieldType::Float\n    } else if value.as_str().is_some() {\n        FieldType::String\n    } else if let Some(arr) = value.as_array() {\n        let inner = arr.first().map(infer_field_type).unwrap_or(FieldType::Any);\n        FieldType::Array(Box::new(inner))\n    } else if let Some(obj) = value.as_object() {\n        let fields = obj\n            .iter()\n            .map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), field_from_value(v)))\n            .collect();\n        FieldType::Object(fields)\n    } else {\n        FieldType::Any\n    }\n}\n\npub(crate) fn any_field(required: bool, description: &str, default: Option<Value>) -> WireGuard interface IP detected at startup (if interface is up)\n//!   4. 0.0.0.0 fallback\n\nuse clap::Parser;\nuse op_cognitive_mcp::CognitiveMcpServer;\nuse op_identity::{write_sled_from_wg, WireGuardIdentity};\nuse tracing::{info, warn, Level};\nuse tracing_subscriber::FmtSubscriber;\n\n#[derive(Parser)]\n#[command(name = \"cognitive-mcp-server\")]\n#[command(about = \"Cognitive MCP Server with memory, NotebookLM bridge, gRPC, and D-Bus\")]\nstruct Cli {\n    /// HTTP/SSE server address (MCP protocol).\n    /// If left at 0.0.0.0 the WireGuard interface IP is used when available.\n    /// Override with COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND env var or this flag.\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND\", default_value = \"0.0.0.0:3003\")]\n    http: String,\n\n    /// gRPC server address (CognitiveToolService).\n    /// If left at 0.0.0.0 the WireGuard interface IP is used when available.\n    /// Override with COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND env var or this flag.\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND\", default_value = \"0.0.0.0:50052\")]\n    grpc: String,\n\n    /// CozoDB database path\n    #[arg(\n        long,\n        env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_DB_PATH\",\n        default_value = \"/var/lib/op-cognitive-mcp/memory.db\"\n    )]\n    db: String,\n\n    /// WireGuard interface to read identity from\n    #[arg(long, env = \"WG_INTERFACE\", default_value = \"netmaker\")]\n    wg_interface: String,\n\n    /// Log level\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_LOG_LEVEL\", default_value = \"info\")]\n    log_level: String,\n\n    /// Disable gRPC server\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_DISABLED\")]\n    no_grpc: bool,\n\n    /// Disable HTTP/SSE server\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_HTTP_DISABLED\")]\n    no_http: bool,\n\n    /// Disable D-Bus registration\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_DBUS_DISABLED\")]\n    no_dbus: bool,\n}\n\n/// Promote an `0.0.0.0:PORT` default address to `<wg_ip>:PORT` when the WG\n/// interface is up.  Explicit addresses (not starting with `0.0.0.0:`) are\n/// returned unchanged so env-var or flag overrides always win.\nfn resolve_bind(addr: &str, wg_ip: Option<&str>) -> String {\n    if let Some(rest) = addr.strip_prefix(\"0.0.0.0:\") {\n        if let Some(ip) = wg_ip {\n            return format!(\"{ip}:{rest}\");\n        }\n    }\n    addr.to_string()\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let cli = Cli::parse();\n\n    let level = match cli.log_level.as_str() {\n        \"trace\" => Level::TRACE,\n        \"debug\" => Level::DEBUG,\n        \"warn\" => Level::WARN,\n        \"error\" => Level::ERROR,\n        _ => Level::INFO,\n    };\n\n    let subscriber = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_max_level(level)\n        .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n        .finish();\n    tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(subscriber)?;\n\n    // ── WireGuard identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // 1. Detect local WG IP for bind address resolution.\n    // 2. \\\n                 set WG_PUBKEY env var to override\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Resolve bind addresses: promote 0.0.0.0 defaults to WG interface IP.\n    let http_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.http, wg_ip.as_deref());\n    let grpc_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.grpc, wg_ip.as_deref());\n\n    info!(\n        http = %http_addr,\n        grpc = %grpc_addr,\n        db = %cli.db,\n        wg_interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n        \"Starting Cognitive MCP Server\"\n    );\n\n    let server = CognitiveMcpServer::new(&cli.db).await?;\n\n    // D-Bus: start first, keep connection alive for the process lifetime.\n    let _dbus_conn = if !cli.no_dbus {\n        match server.start_dbus().await {\n            Ok(conn) => {\n                info!(\"D-Bus registered: org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp\");\n                Some(conn)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                warn!(\"D-Bus registration failed (continuing without it): {e}\");\n                None\n            }\n        }\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n\n    match (cli.no_grpc, cli.no_http) {\n        (true, true) => {\n            eprintln!(\"Error: both --no-grpc and --no-http specified. Nothing to run.\");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n        (true, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE only\");\n            server.start_http_server(&http_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, true) => {\n            info!(\"Running gRPC only\");\n            server.start_grpc_server(&grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE + gRPC\");\n            server.start_dual(&http_addr, &grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n//! .await;\n\n        let socket_addr: std::net::SocketAddr = addr.parse()?;\n        tracing::info!(addr = %socket_addr, \"Cognitive gRPC Server listening\");\n\n        let cors = {"timestamp":"2026-06-14T00:07:51.440Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Implemented the cleaner ZeroClaw-centered version.\n\nWhat changed:\n- Added a ZeroClaw-declared model transcript MCP surface in [zeroclaw.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs) as `model_transcript_mcp`.\n- Added NotebookLM MCP tool prefixing in [notebooklm.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-cognitive-mcp/src/notebooklm.rs), so a ZeroClaw transcript instance exposes names like `zeroclaw_model_transcript_ask_question`.\n- Added the Drive snapshot collector at [op-cli-notebook-log-sync.sh](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/bin/op-cli-notebook-log-sync.sh).\n- Added systemd and s6 deploy units:\n  - [op-cli-notebook-log-sync@.service](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/systemd/op-cli-notebook-log-sync@.service)\n  - [deploy/s6/op-cli-notebook-logger/run](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/s6/op-cli-notebook-logger/run)\n- Added env examples for ZeroClaw discovery and the ZeroClaw transcript NotebookLM MCP instance.\n- Documented the flow in [cli-notebook-log-sync.md](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/docs/op-services/cli-notebook-log-sync.md).\n\nBehavior now:\nZeroClaw owns discovery and writes source specs into `/run/op-dbus/zeroclaw/notebooklm-sources.d/*.env`. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. npx\\nNotebookLM MCP - Access NotebookLM (notebooklm.google.com).\\n\\n**Auth:** If you get authentication errors, run `nlm login` via your Bash/terminal tool. This is the automated authentication method that handles everything. Only use save_auth_tokens as a fallback if the CLI fails.\\n**Account Switching:** To switch Google Accounts for the MCP server, run `nlm login switch <profile>` in Bash. The MCP server instantly uses the active default profile.\\n**Confirmation:** Tools with confirm param require user approval before setting confirm=True.\\n**Studio:** After creating audio/video/infographic/slides, poll studio_status for completion.\\n\\nConsolidated tools:\\n- source_add(source_type=url|text|drive|file, url=..., document_id=..., text=..., file_path=...): Add any source type\\n- studio_create(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Create any artifact type\\n- studio_revise: Revise individual slides in an existing slide deck\\n- download_artifact(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Download any artifact type\\n- note_create/note_list/note_update/note_delete: Manage notes in notebooks\"],\"removedNames\":[]},\"type\":\"attachment\",\"uuid\":\"7327db6c-d92f-4278-9a86-58218f5f84ce\",\"timestamp\":\"2026-06-12T19:34:03.575Z\",\"userType\":\"external\",\"entrypoint\":\"cli\",\"cwd\":\"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\",\"sessionId\":\"0ef14d6e-2b10-4e31-965d-7402203c5317\",\"version\":\"2.1.173\",\"gitBranch\":\"feat/sled-source-port-salt\"}\n{\"parentUuid\":\"7327db6c-d92f-4278-9a86-58218f5f84ce\",\"isSidechain\":false,\"attachment\":{\"type\":\"skill_listing\",\"content\":\"- skills: Reference codebase for Crates. Use this skill when you need to understand the structure, implementation patterns, or code details of the Crates project.\\n- mcp-server-dev:build-mcp-app: This skill should be used when the user wants to build an \\\"MCP app\\\", add \\\"interactive UI\\\" or \\\"widgets\\\" to an MCP server, \\\"render components in chat\\\", build \\\"MCP UI resources\\\", make a tool that shows a \\\"form\\\", \\\"picker\\\", \\\"dashboard\\\" or \\\"confirmation dialog\\\" inline in the conversation, or mentions \\\"apps SDK\\\" in the context of MCP. Use AFTER the build-mcp-server skill has settled the deployment model, or when the user already knows they want UI widgets.\\n- mcp-server-dev:build-mcp-server: This skill should be used when the user asks to \\\"build an MCP server\\\", \\\"create an MCP\\\", \\\"make an MCP integration\\\", \\\"wrap an API for Claude\\\", \\\"expose tools to Claude\\\", \\\"make an MCP app\\\", or discusses building something with the Model Context Protocol. It is the entry point for MCP server development — it interrogates the user about their use case, determines the right deployment model (remote HTTP, MCPB, local stdio), picks a tool-design pattern, and hands off to specialized skills.\\n- mcp-server-dev:build-mcpb: This skill should be used when the user wants to \\\"package an MCP server\\\", \\\"bundle an MCP\\\", \\\"make an MCPB\\\", \\\"ship a local MCP server\\\", \\\"distribute a local MCP\\\", discusses \\\".mcpb files\\\", mentions bundling a Node or Python runtime with their MCP server, or needs an MCP server that interacts with the local filesystem, desktop apps, or OS and must be installable without the user having Node/Python set up.\\n- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\\\"from now on when X\\\", \\\"each time X\\\", \\\"whenever X\\\", \\\"before/after X\\\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\\\"allow X\\\", \\\"add permission\\\", \\\"move permission to\\\"), env vars (\\\"set X=Y\\\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \\\"allow npm commands\\\", \\\"add bq permission to global settings\\\", \\\"move permission to user settings\\\", \\\"set DEBUG=true\\\", \\\"when claude stops show X\\\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \\\"rebind ctrl+s\\\", \\\"add a chord shortcut\\\", \\\"change the submit key\\\", \\\"customize keybindings\\\".\\n- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.\\n- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.\\n- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.\\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \\\"check the deploy every 5 minutes\\\", \\\"keep running /babysit-prs\\\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\\\"run this once at 3pm\\\", \\\"remind me to check X tomorrow\\\").\\n- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.\\nTRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it \\\"looks like a one-liner\\\" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).\\nSKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).\\n- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. The transports are independently toggleable via the `cognitive_mcp` state plugin (`http_enabled` / `grpc_enabled` / `dbus_enabled`, or `COGNITIVE_MCP_HTTP_DISABLED` etc.), so you can turn HTTP/SSE off and leave gRPC + D-Bus up.\n- Enabling an MCP server through the tree is the `mcp` state plugin: apply state with `servers.<name>.enabled = true` plus a transport.\n\n**Three gaps before the CLIs can ride gRPC**\n\n1. `CognitiveToolService` has no generic tool RPCs — it's all domain-specific (notebooks, sources, GeminiQuery…). So gRPC-as-transport means each CLI's config registers a **stdio shim**: a tiny binary the CLI spawns, which translates MCP JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout → gRPC calls to `10.200.0.1:50052` over the grpc-uplink. The foundation is laid; the build is next.\n\n---\n\n## TL;DR\nThe prior session left the stack broken all night. This session found the **two real root\ncauses**, fixed the durable ones, and laid a clean foundation (`array` pool). The remaining\nwork is a **catch-up rebuild on the new pool**, blocked only by a wedge that a (now-safe)\nreboot clears.\n\n---\n\n## Root causes found (this was the breakthrough)\n\n1. **`/run/netmaker` is tmpfs — wiped on every boot.**\n   The proxy devices on `netmaker-mq`/`netmaker-ui` bind host sockets at\n   `/run/netmaker/{mq,mqtts,ui}.sock`. After a reboot the dir is gone → those containers\n   fail to start → **ERROR (`Invalid PID -1`) → they flap RUNNING↔ERROR → hold incusd's\n   write lock → every `incus start`/`move` hangs.** This is the wedge. Reboot used to make\n   it *worse* because it re-wiped the dir. **FIXED** — see below.\n\n2. **The incus pool is a cramped 30 GiB loopback image.**\n   `default` pool driver=btrfs but **source = `/var/lib/incus/disks/default.img`** — a 30 GiB\n   file loop-mounted as `/dev/loop0`. Every container is a subvolume *inside that image*, not\n   native on the disk. It was allocation-locked (30/30 GiB allocated, ~1.4 GiB free) which\n   pressured containers into ERROR. The host disk had room; the pool couldn't see it because\n   the loop image is walled off at 30 GiB.\n\n---\n\n## Fixes applied this session (durable — survive reboot)\n\n- **`/etc/tmpfiles.d/netmaker.conf`** → `d /run/netmaker 0755 root root -`\n  The `tmpfiles-setup` s6 oneshot recreates `/run/netmaker` on every boot. Root cause #1 fixed.\n  Tested live (`systemd-tmpfiles --create` → dir present).\n- **Cleared ~5.4 GB build artifacts** — deleted `target/` in operation-dbus-proto, zbusctl, zbus.\n  (Deployed binaries already live in `/usr/local/bin`, so safe; `target/` rebuilds with cargo.)\n- **`sdb` + `sdc` added to the root btrfs array** (done by user). Root fs is now 3 devices\n  (sda3 185G + sdc 100G + sdb 201G = 486 G total, **~324 GB free**). sdb/sdc were dead disks,\n  wiped and absorbed for raw capacity. btrfs multi-device = no \"grow\" needed; space just appears.\n- **Created `array` incus pool** = native btrfs subvolume on the array:\n  `incus storage create array btrfs source=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/array`\n  Verified: `/dev/sda3[/@/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/array]`, subvol ID 273 — NOT a loop image.\n  This pool draws from the full 324 GB automatically.\n- **`/home/jeremy/bringup-stack.sh`** — idempotent post-reboot bring-up of the stack (wg-xray →\n  mq → netmaker → ui, opdbus egress iptables, sets boot.autostart). PSK rides WireGuard's built-in `PresharedKey` slot. DB stores: WG **public** key (canonical identity anchor), MCP token = `UUID v5(pubkey)`, and `blake3(psk)` **only** (never raw PSK). Car Geeks\", \"Log File Analysis\",\n    \"Linux and Windows Systems Administration Guide\", \"Microsoft Presidio Project Documentation\",\n    \"Gemini Enterprise CLI Transition and Billing Audit Summary\",\n    \"Gemini Enterprise Billing Rebuttal and Technical Audit Case 66825975\",\n    \"Gemini Chats\", \"Claude\"\n  ]\n}\n### knowledge/upload-to-notebook.sh\n#!/bin/bash\n# Upload the Ghostbridge Live! knowledge corpus into the master NotebookLM notebook.\n# Run this LAPTOP-SIDE (live browser session) or right after a fresh `nlm login` —\n# the static-cookie sessions on the server die in minutes, which is why this is a script.\n#\n# Usage:  ./knowledge/upload-to-notebook.sh\n# Prereq: nlm authenticated (nlm notebook list should work first)\n\nset -u\nMASTER=\"${1:-01b00e9c-033a-4bc9-965f-3257360ff4a8}\"   # Ghostbridge Live!\ncd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" || exit 1\n\n# fail fast if auth is dead\nif ! nlm notebook list >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n  echo \"ERROR: nlm not authenticated. Run 'nlm login' (laptop) or re-import cookies, then retry.\"\n  exit 1\nfi\n\nn=0\nadd() {  # add <file> <title>\n  if nlm source add \"$MASTER\" --file \"$1\" --title \"$2\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    n=$((n+1)); echo \"+[$n] $2\"\n  else\n    echo \"FAIL $2 (auth may have expired — re-login and re-run; dups are fine)\"\n  fi\n}\n\necho \"=== distilled knowledge ===\"\nadd WISHLIST.md                       \"Ghostbridge Live! — Task Board\"\nadd SIGNALS.md                        \"Ghostbridge Live! — Model Signals & Decisions\"\nadd knowledge/notebooks.manifest.json \"Knowledge Corpus Manifest\"\n\necho \"=== core memory ===\"\nfor m in \"$HOME\"/.claude/projects/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/memory/*.md; do\n  add \"$m\" \"memory-$(basename \"$m\" .md)\"\ndone\n\necho \"=== full transcripts (the reasoning) ===\"\nfor f in knowledge/transcripts/*.md; do\n  add \"$f\" \"transcript-$(basename \"$f\" .md)\"\ndone\n\necho \"=== done: $n sources uploaded to $MASTER ===\"\necho \"If it died partway, just re-run — NotebookLM dedups by you, dups are harmless.\"\n### deploy/netmaker/rumqttd.toml\n# rumqttd — host MQTT broker, replaces the no-NIC netmaker-mq container.\n# Plaintext on loopback; xray terminates TLS upstream (matches stack).\nid = 0\n\n[router]\nmax_connections = 10010\nmax_outgoing_packet_count = 200\nmax_segment_size = 104857600\nmax_segment_count = 10\n\n# MQTT 3.1.1 (v4) — netmaker speaks this\n[v4.1]\nname = \"v4-1883\"\nlisten = \"127.0.0.1:1883\"\nnext_connection_delay_ms = 1\n[v4.1.connections]\nconnection_timeout_ms = 60000\nmax_payload_size = 20480\nmax_inflight_count = 500\n[v4.1.connections.auth]\nnetmaker = \"3f48f4cbbf54ae2fbfdf5c4fce64caf2\"\n\n# second loopback listener mirroring mosquitto's 8883 (plaintext; xray does TLS)\n[v4.2]\nname = \"v4-8883\"\nlisten = \"127.0.0.1:8883\"\nnext_connection_delay_ms = 1\n[v4.2.connections]\nconnection_timeout_ms = 60000\nmax_payload_size = 20480\nmax_inflight_count = 500\n[v4.2.connections.auth]\nnetmaker = \"3f48f4cbbf54ae2fbfdf5c4fce64caf2\"\n\n[console]\nlisten = \"127.0.0.1:3030\"\n### deploy/config/zeroclaw-model-transcript-mcp.env.example\n# ZeroClaw-owned NotebookLM MCP instance for model transcript research.\n# This is intentionally a separate NotebookLM MCP profile/server name so its\n# tools can be exposed without colliding with the default NotebookLM bridge.\n\nCOGNITIVE_MCP_NOTEBOOKLM_ENABLED=1\nCOGNITIVE_MCP_NOTEBOOKLM_COMMAND=npx\nCOGNITIVE_MCP_NOTEBOOKLM_ARGS=-y notebooklm-mcp@latest\nCOGNITIVE_MCP_NOTEBOOKLM_SERVER_NAME=zeroclaw-model-transcripts\nCOGNITIVE_MCP_NOTEBOOKLM_PROFILE=model-transcripts\nCOGNITIVE_MCP_NOTEBOOKLM_TOOL_PREFIX=zeroclaw_model_transcript\n\nZEROCLAW_MODEL_TRANSCRIPT_SOURCE_DIR=/run/op-dbus/zeroclaw/notebooklm-sources.d\nZEROCLAW_MODEL_TRANSCRIPT_DRIVE_ROOT=gdrive:NotebookLM/op-dbus/model-transcripts\n### docs/op-services/cli-notebook-log-sync.md\n# CLI NotebookLM Log Sync\n\n## Requirements\n\n- `OP_NOTEBOOK_ID` is required for every discovered source.\n- Each ZeroClaw-declared CLI/model pair writes one stable Google Drive file.\n- Add that Drive file to the matching NotebookLM notebook once.\n- The service overwrites the Drive file; it does not add new NotebookLM sources.\n- ZeroClaw owns discovery. The sync service only consumes declared source specs.\n\n## Design\n\nNotebookLM has source limits, so this service treats Google Drive as the stable source of truth. ZeroClaw discovers clients/models/sessions through its plugin schema and publishes source specs under:\n\n```text\n/run/op-dbus/zeroclaw/notebooklm-sources.d/*.env\n```\n\nEach spec maps one CLI/model/session stream to one stable Drive file and one NotebookLM notebook id.\nNotebookLM should contain that Drive file as a source. When the service updates the file, refresh/sync the existing Drive source in NotebookLM instead of adding another source.\n\nThe service deliberately does not hardcode VS Code, Antigravity, OpenCode, or model paths. Those details belong in ZeroClaw's D-Bus/MCP projection because `PluginSchema` is the interface contract.\n\nZeroClaw also declares a dedicated NotebookLM MCP instance for model transcript research:\n\n```text\nserver_name: zeroclaw-model-transcripts\nprofile: model-transcripts\ntool_prefix: zeroclaw_model_transcript\nsubid: exp.service.zeroclaw-model-transcripts.mcp@v1\n```\n\nThat gives the chatbot/MCP surface a separate transcript research namespace while still using the regular NotebookLM MCP sidecar under cognitive-mcp. The transcript MCP reads the NotebookLM notebook whose sources are the stable Drive files maintained by this sync service.\n\n## Code Implementation\n\nInstall the runner:\n\n```sh\ninstall -m 0755 deploy/bin/op-cli-notebook-log-sync.sh /usr/local/sbin/op-cli-notebook-log-sync.sh\n```\n\nSystemd instance:\n\n```sh\ninstall -d -m 0755 /etc/op-dbus/cli-notebook-logger\ninstall -m 0644 deploy/config/cli-notebook-logger/zeroclaw-discovery.env.example \\\n  /etc/op-dbus/cli-notebook-logger/zeroclaw-discovery.env\ninstall -m 0644 deploy/systemd/op-cli-notebook-log-sync@.service /etc/systemd/system/\nsystemctl daemon-reload\nsystemctl enable --now op-cli-notebook-log-sync@zeroclaw-discovery.service\n```\n\ns6 instance:\n\n```sh\ninstall -d -m 0755 /etc/s6/sv/op-cli-notebook-logger/env\ncp -a deploy/s6/op-cli-notebook-logger/. /etc/s6/sv/op-cli-notebook-logger/\ncp -a deploy/s6/op-cli-notebook-logger-log /etc/s6/sv/op-cli-notebook-logger-log\n```\n\nFor s6 envdir, create one file per variable under the service `env/` directory.\n"}}

With that, the DNS layer is fully specified and it's coherent with everything else:\\n\\n## DNS architecture (final)\\n\\n**NextDNS resolves everything except domains we own**, and the NextDNS profile is **injected per-identity via the ghostbridge header** — so DNS is part of the same accountability loop as the rest of the stack, not a flat host resolver. That's already half-wired: `NEXTDNS_PROFILE_ID` flows into the generated xray config next to the footprint/trace headers in `schema_bridge.rs`. Base device profile is `689ec7`; NextDNS listens on `localhost:53` and `10.200.0.2:53` and resolves correctly (verified).\\n\\nThe resolution chain becomes:\\n\\n```\\nclient/host → split-horizon forwarder\\n                ├─ *.ghostbridge.tech (owned)  → Gemma/xray → internal / wg-xray addr   (never public, never decoy)\\n                └─ everything else             → NextDNS (127.0.0.1), per-identity profile from header → upstream\\n```\\n\\n**The concrete bug:** the host's `/etc/resolv.conf` is `nameserver 1.1.1.1` (written Jun 8; the \\\"injected via nextdns-srv\\\" comment is stale — the s6 run script doesn't actually write it). So the host bypasses local NextDNS entirely *and* sends owned domains to public DNS → the decoy. Both wrong.\\n\\n**Safe fix order** (I won't flip live until the carve-out exists, or owned domains would keep hitting the decoy):\\n1. Stand up the split-horizon forwarder rule — owned domains → local (Gemma/xray or dnsmasq `server=/ghostbridge.tech/<local>`), default → `127.0.0.1` (NextDNS). dnsmasq on `10.200.0.2:53` is the natural home for this.\\n2. Repoint `/etc/resolv.conf` at that forwarder, and find/fix whatever wrote `1.1.1.1` so it doesn't get clobbered back.\\n3. Owned-domain answers ultimately come from Gemma's generated map (same artifact as subid + tag routing).\\n\\n## Still need your call before I cut into live infra\\n\\n1. **xray daemon → plugin refactor** (fold start/stop into `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/xray`, delete the rogue `opdbus.v1` name) — go?\\n2. **netmaker server** — relocate to hypervisor or stay on the decoy?\\n3. **DNS** — want me to start with step 1 (the split-horizon forwarder in dnsmasq, non-disruptive, additive) so the carve-out is ready before any resolv.conf flip?\\n\\nAll three are staged and ready; I just don't want to repoint the live router's launch path, control plane, or resolver without your nod on each.\"}],\"stop_reason\":\"end_turn\",\"stop_sequence\":null,\"stop_details\":null,\"usage\":{\"input_tokens\":2,\"cache_creation_input_tokens\":732,\"cache_read_input_tokens\":143890,\"output_tokens\":1777,\"server_tool_use\":{\"web_search_requests\":0,\"web_fetch_requests\":0},\"service_tier\":\"standard\",\"cache_creation\":{\"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens\":732,\"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens\":0},\"inference_geo\":\"not_available\",\"iterations\":[{\"input_tokens\":2,\"output_tokens\":1777,\"cache_read_input_tokens\":143890,\"cache_creation_input_tokens\":732,\"cache_creation\":{\"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens\":0,\"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens\":732},\"type\":\"message\"}],\"speed\":\"standard\"},\"diagnostics\":null},\"requestId\":\"req_011Cbz12sixco9NEwLyPKBjH\",\"type\":\"assistant\",\"uuid\":\"5b06da7b-85c9-4eba-8246-b9e54632797d\",\"timestamp\":\"2026-06-12T20:32:12.216Z\",\"userType\":\"external\",\"entrypoint\":\"cli\",\"cwd\":\"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\",\"sessionId\":\"0ef14d6e-2b10-4e31-965d-7402203c5317\",\"version\":\"2.1.173\",\"gitBranch\":\"feat/sled-source-port-salt\"}\n"}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-14</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T22:02:12.651Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_53ENx1TNBU1xycPfoBfXn9Uo","output":"Chunk ID: d6d74a\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1958\nOutput:\n---\nname: audit-context-building\ndescription: Enables ultra-granular, line-by-line code analysis to build deep architectural context before vulnerability or bug finding.\nrisk: unknown\nsource: community\n---\n\n# Deep Context Builder Skill (Ultra-Granular Pure Context Mode)\n\n## 1. Purpose\n\nThis skill governs **how Claude thinks** during the context-building phase of an audit.\n\nWhen active, Claude will:\n- Perform **line-by-line / block-by-block** code analysis by default.\n- Apply **First Principles**, **5 Whys**, and **5 Hows** at micro scale.\n- Continuously link insights → functions → modules → entire system.\n- Maintain a stable, explicit mental model that evolves with new evidence.\n- Identify invariants, assumptions, flows, and reasoning hazards.\n\nThis skill defines a structured analysis format (see Example: Function Micro-Analysis below) and runs **before** the vulnerability-hunting phase.\n\n---\n\n## When to Use\nUse when:\n- Deep comprehension is needed before bug or vulnerability discovery.\n- You want bottom-up understanding instead of high-level guessing.\n- Reducing hallucinations, contradictions, and context loss is critical.\n- Preparing for security auditing, architecture review, or threat modeling.\n\nDo **not** use for:\n- Vulnerability findings\n- Fix recommendations\n- Exploit reasoning\n- Severity/impact rating\n\n---\n\n## 2. How This Skill Behaves\n\nWhen active, Claude will:\n- Default to **ultra-granular analysis** of each block and line.\n- Apply micro-level First Principles, 5 Whys, and 5 Hows.\n- Build and refine a persistent global mental model.\n- Update earlier assumptions when contradicted (\"Earlier I thought X; now Y.\").\n- Periodically anchor summaries to maintain stable context.\n- Avoid speculation; express uncertainty explicitly when needed.\n\nGoal: **deep, accurate understanding**, not conclusions.\n\n---\n\n## Rationalizations (Do Not Skip)\n\n| Rationalization | Why It's Wrong | Required Action |\n|-----------------|----------------|-----------------|\n| \"I get the gist\" | Gist-level understanding misses edge cases | Line-by-line analysis required |\n| \"This function is simple\" | Simple functions compose into complex bugs | Apply 5 Whys anyway |\n| \"I'll remember this invariant\" | You won't. Context degrades. | Write it down explicitly |\n| \"External call is probably fine\" | External = adversarial until proven otherwise | Jump into code or model as hostile |\n| \"I can skip this helper\" | Helpers contain assumptions that propagate | Trace the full call chain |\n| \"This is taking too long\" | Rushed context = hallucinated vulnerabilities later | Slow is fast |\n\n---\n\n## 3. Phase 1 — Initial Orientation (Bottom-Up Scan)\n\nBefore deep analysis, Claude performs a minimal mapping:\n\n1. Identify major modules/files/contracts.\n2. Note obvious public/external entrypoints.\n3. Identify likely actors (users, owners, relayers, oracles, other contracts).\n4. Identify important storage variables, dicts, state structs, or cells.\n5. Build a preliminary structure without assuming behavior.\n\nThis establishes anchors for detailed analysis.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Phase 2 — Ultra-Granular Function Analysis (Default Mode)\n\nEvery non-trivial function receives full micro analysis.\n\n### 5.1 Per-Function Microstructure Checklist\n\nFor each function:\n\n1. **Purpose**\n   - Why the function exists and its role in the system.\n\n2. **Inputs & Assumptions**\n   - Parameters and implicit inputs (state, sender, env).\n   - Preconditions and constraints.\n\n3. **Outputs & Effects**\n   - Return values.\n   - State/storage writes.\n   - Events/messages.\n   - External interactions.\n\n4. **Block-by-Block / Line-by-Line Analysis**\n   For each logical block:\n   - What it does.\n   - Why it appears here (ordering logic).\n   - What assumptions it relies on.\n   - What invariants it establishes or maintains.\n   - What later logic depends on it.\n\n   Apply per-block:\n   - **First Principles**\n   - **5 Whys**\n   - **5 Hows**\n\n---\n\n### 5.2 Cross-Function & External Flow Analysis\n*(Full Integration of Jump-Into-External-Code Rule)*\n\nWhen encountering calls, **continue the same micro-first analysis across boundaries.**\n\n#### Internal Calls\n- Jump into the callee immediately.\n- Perform block-by-block analysis of relevant code.\n- Track flow of data, assumptions, and invariants:\n  caller → callee → return → caller.\n- Note if callee logic behaves differently in this specific call context.\n\n#### External Calls — Two Cases\n\n**Case A — External Call to a Contract Whose Code Exists in the Codebase**\nTreat as an internal call:\n- Jump into the target contract/function.\n- Continue block-by-block micro-analysis.\n- Propagate invariants and assumptions seamlessly.\n- Consider edge cases based on the *actual* code, not a black-box guess.\n\n**Case B — External Call Without Available Code (True External / Black Box)**\nAnalyze as adversarial:\n- Describe payload/value/gas or parameters sent.\n- Identify assumptions about the target.\n- Consider all outcomes:\n  - revert\n  - incorrect/strange return values\n  - unexpected state changes\n  - misbehavior\n  - reentrancy (if applicable)\n\n#### Continuity Rule\nTreat the entire call chain as **one continuous execution flow**.\nNever reset context.\nAll invariants, assumptions, and data dependencies must propagate across calls.\n\n---\n\n### 5.3 Complete Analysis Example\n\nSee FUNCTION_MICRO_ANALYSIS_EXAMPLE.md for a complete walkthrough demonstrating:\n- Full micro-analysis of a DEX swap function\n- Application of First Principles, 5 Whys, and 5 Hows\n- Block-by-block analysis with invariants and assumptions\n- Cross-function dependency mapping\n- Risk analysis for external interactions\n\nThis example demonstrates the level of depth and structure required for all analyzed functions.\n\n---\n\n### 5.4 Output Requirements\n\nWhen performing ultra-granular analysis, Claude MUST structure output following the format defined in OUTPUT_REQUIREMENTS.md.\n\nKey requirements:\n- **Purpose** (2-3 sentences minimum)\n- **Inputs & Assumptions** (all parameters, preconditions, trust assumptions)\n- **Outputs & Effects** (returns, state writes, external calls, events, postconditions)\n- **Block-by-Block Analysis** (What, Why here, Assumptions, First Principles/5 Whys/5 Hows)\n- **Cross-Function Dependencies** (internal calls, external calls with risk analysis, shared state)\n\nQuality thresholds:\n- Minimum 3 invariants per function\n- Minimum 5 assumptions documented\n- Minimum 3 risk considerations for external interactions\n- At least 1 First Principles application\n- At least 3 combined 5 Whys/5 Hows applications\n\n---\n\n### 5.5 Completeness Checklist\n\nBefore concluding micro-analysis of a function, verify against the COMPLETENESS_CHECKLIST.md:\n\n- **Structural Completeness**: All required sections present (Purpose, Inputs, Outputs, Block-by-Block, Dependencies)\n- **Content Depth**: Minimum thresholds met (invariants, assumptions, risk analysis, First Principles)\n- **Continuity & Integration**: Cross-references, propagated assumptions, invariant couplings\n- **Anti-Hallucination**: Line number citations, no vague statements, evidence-based claims\n\nAnalysis is complete when all checklist items are satisfied and no unresolved \"unclear\" items remain.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Phase 3 — Global System Understanding\n\nAfter sufficient micro-analysis:\n\n1. **State & Invariant Reconstruction**\n   - Map reads/writes of each state variable.\n   - Derive multi-function and multi-module invariants.\n\n2. **Workflow Reconstruction**\n   - Identify end-to-end flows (deposit, withdraw, lifecycle, upgrades).\n   - Track how state transforms across these flows.\n   - Record assumptions that persist across steps.\n\n3. **Trust Boundary Mapping**\n   - Actor → entrypoint → behavior.\n   - Identify untrusted input paths.\n   - Privilege changes and implicit role expectations.\n\n4. **Complexity & Fragility Clustering**\n"}}

That's exactly why the \\\"egress to 10.0.0.2\\\" question resolves the way it does below.\\n\\nHere's the full state of everything from this session:\\n\\n## Shim: built, installed, working end-to-end ✅\\n\\n- New crate `crates/op-mcp-shim` → installed at `/usr/local/bin/op-mcp-shim`. It's a stdio MCP server that does **gRPC reflection** against cognitive-mcp, projects every unary RPC as an MCP tool (JSON schemas generated from the proto descriptors), and dispatches `tools/call` via `prost-reflect` DynamicMessage — zero compiled-in stubs, so new RPCs in `cognitive.proto` appear as tools automatically.\\n- Verified live: 18 tools discovered, and `CognitiveToolService_GetHealth` returned `healthy: true` through the full path.\\n- Registered as `cognitive-grpc` in all three clients: repo `.mcp.json` (claude-code — replacing the stale `127.0.0.1:3003` HTTP entry), `~/.factory/mcp.json`, and `~/.gemini/settings.json`. Restart each CLI to pick it up.\\n- On your \\\"shim being tonic-web?\\\" question: the shim dials **native gRPC** on the same port — tonic-web's value is that browsers/HTTP-1 clients share that one listener; native clients don't need the gRPC-web framing.\\n\\nTwo things you should know:\\n1. **The gRPC listener binds 100.90.37.1:50052 (netmaker IP), not the 10.200.0.x uplink** — the configs point there because that's where it actually listens.\\n2. The ghostbridge interceptor only checks header *presence* — my test call passed with dummy values. Fine under your zero-trust model (the WG path is the real gate), but it means anything on the netmaker mesh can call tools.\\n\\n## Netmaker / egress to 10.0.0.2: yes, an egress is in order\\n\\n- Mesh is up (fresh handshakes), and the control plane is reachable — `api.ghostbridge.tech` → **129.153.134.63 (the decoy VPS)**, health returns 200. The local `netmaker` Incus container is STOPPED, which explains the dashboard connection-refused you saw in factory; the API works anyway, so the server is being fronted via the decoy now.\\n- **No egress exists**: no NAT/FORWARD rules for 10.0.0.0/24, mesh peers only have /32 allowed-IPs. Since the hypervisor owns 10.0.0.2 on `opdbus`, create the egress on the **hypervisor** node in the dashboard: range `10.0.0.2/32` (or `10.0.0.0/24` if peers should reach the whole opdbus net), NAT on. Here's the full picture of what was done:\\n\\n**Data flow:**\\n```\\nExternal TCP (148.113.204.83:8081)\\n  → xray dokodemo-door inbound (netmaker-api-in)\\n  → xray routing rule → netmaker-api-out (freedom redirect 127.0.0.1:18081)\\n  → incus proxy device on wg-xray (bind=container, listen=127.0.0.1:18081 → unix:/run/netmaker/api.sock on host)\\n  → incus proxy device on netmaker container (listen=unix:/run/netmaker/api.sock → connect=tcp:127.0.0.1:8081)\\n  → netmaker API (loopback only, no NIC)\\n```\\n\\n**What changed:**\\n- `plugin_schema_defs.rs` — `unix_socket_plugin_schema()` example now declares all 4 netmaker sockets; `incus_plugin_schema()` example declares all 3 netmaker containers (no NIC, proxy devices only) and the updated `wg-xray` definition with `netmaker-socks` disk + 4 TCP proxy devices\\n- `default_registry.rs` — `netmaker` added to `default_auto_load`\\n- `/etc/xray/config.json` — 4 new inbounds + 4 new TCP-redirect outbounds + routing rules, validated OK\\n- `wg-xray` container — `netmaker-socks` disk device + 4 container-side TCP proxy devices applied live\\n\\nThe `IncusPlugin.apply_state` will call `sync_devices` to install proxy devices on the netmaker containers when they're created. The `UnixSocketPlugin` reads the schema example from `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` and reconciles the socket files, which is what shows up in the control panel GUI.\"}]\n146:[{\"type\":\"tool_use\",\"id\":\"toolu_01KnH6gDGn4xizr3FFNGnvJE\",\"name\":\"Write\",\"input\":{\"file_path\":\"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/netmaker/install.sh\",\"content\":\"#!/bin/bash\\nset -euo pipefail\\n\\nSCRIPT_DIR=\\\"$(cd \\\"$(dirname \\\"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\\\")\\\" && pwd)\\\"\\n…43939 tokens truncated…erceptor(mut req: Request<()>) -> Result<Request<()>, Status> {\\n    // 1. Extract the Xray-injected Identity Headers (The Accountability Loop)\\n    //    Clone header values upfront to release the immutable borrow on `req`,\\n    //    allowing the mutable `extensions_mut()` call downstream.\\n    let footprint_value = req.metadata().get(\\\"x-ghostbridge-footprint\\\").cloned();\\n    let trace_value = req.metadata().get(\\\"x-ghostbridge-trace-id\\\").cloned();\\n\\n    if footprint_value.is_none() || trace_value.is_none() {\\n        return Err(Status::unauthenticated(\\n            \\\"A.N.N.A. Scribe: Missing Ghostbridge Identity Sled. Connection Dropped.\\\",\\n        ));\\n    }\\n\\n    // 2. 1:1 Direct Read from the SchemaEngine's shared memory (No SQL, No Polling)\\n    let (sled_ptr, _mmap) = op_identity::read_sled()\\n        .map_err(|_| Status::internal(\\\"SchemaEngine Memory Unreachable\\\"))?;\\n    let sled = unsafe { &*sled_ptr };\\n\\n    // The Absolute Base: No valid schema, it does not exist.\\n    if !is_sled_valid(sled) {\\n        return Err(Status::failed_precondition(\\n            \\\"A.N.N.A. Scribe: Invalid Schema State. Cease and Desist.\\\",\\n        ));\\n    }\\n\\n    let current_footprint = sled.hashed_footprint;\\n\\n    // 3. The Strike/Etch Validation: Check if the payload is in sync with Btrfs.\\n    //    If a Btrfs mutation has occurred and the client's footprint is stale,\\n    //    the connection is dropped without consuming any NVMe I/O.\\n    let request_footprint = footprint_value\\n        .as_ref()\\n        .unwrap()\\n        .to_str()\\n        .map_err(|_| Status::invalid_argument(\\\"Invalid footprint header encoding\\\"))?;\\n    let expected_footprint = hex::encode(current_footprint);\\n\\n    if request_footprint != expected_footprint {\\n        return Err(Status::permission_denied(\\n            \\\"A.N.N.A. Scribe: Missing Ghostbridge Identity Sled. Connection Dropped.\\\",\\n        ));\\n    }\\n\\n    // 2. 1:1 Direct Read from the SchemaEngine's shared memory (No SQL, No Polling)\\n    let (sled_ptr, _mmap) = op_identity::read_sled()\\n        .map_err(|_| Status::internal(\\\"SchemaEngine Memory Unreachable\\\"))?;\\n    let sled = unsafe { &*sled_ptr };\\n\\n    // The Absolute Base: No valid schema, it does not exist.\\n    if !is_sled_valid(sled) {\\n        return Err(Status::failed_precondition(\\n            \\\"A.N.N.A. Scribe: Invalid Schema State. Cease and Desist.\\\",\\n        ));\\n    }\\n\\n    let current_footprint = sled.hashed_footprint;\\n\\n    // 3. The Strike/Etch Validation: Check if the payload is in sync with Btrfs.\\n    //    If a Btrfs mutation has occurred and the client's footprint is stale,\\n    //    the connection is dropped without consuming any NVMe I/O.\\n    let request_footprint = footprint_value\\n        .as_ref()\\n        .unwrap()\\n        .to_str()\\n        .map_err(|_| Status::invalid_argument(\\\"Invalid footprint header encoding\\\"))?;\\n    let expected_footprint = hex::encode(current_footprint);\\n\\n    if request_footprint != expected_footprint {\\n        return Err(Status::permission_denied(\\n            \\\"A.N.N.A. Scribe: Temporal Hash Mismatch. \\\\\\n             Session footprint is out of sync with current Btrfs mutation.\\\",\\n        ));\\n    }\\n\\n    // 4. Pass the Trace ID downstream into the gRPC context for the React GUI.\\n    if let Some(trace_val) = trace_value {\\n        req.extensions_mut().insert(trace_val);\\n    }\\n\\n    Ok(req)\\n}\\n\\n#[cfg(test)]\\nmod tests {\\n    use super::*;\\n    use tonic::metadata::MetadataValue;\\n\\n    #[test]\\n    fn test_rejects_missing_footprint_header() {\\n        let req = Request::new(());\\n        let result = ghostbridge_interceptor(req);\\n        assert!(result.is_err());\\n        let status = result.unwrap_err();\\n        assert_eq!(status.code(), tonic::Code::Unauthenticated);\\n        assert!(status.message().contains(\\\"Missing Ghostbridge Identity Sled\\\"));\\n    }\\n\\n    #[test]\\n    fn test_rejects_missing_trace_header() {\\n        let mut req = Request::new(());\\n        req.metadata_mut().insert(\\n            \\\"x-ghostbridge-footprint\\\",\\n            MetadataValue::from_static(\\\"deadbeef\\\"),\\n        );\\n        let result = ghostbridge_interceptor(req);\\n        assert!(result.is_err());\\n        assert_eq!(result.unwrap_err().code(), tonic::Code::Unauthenticated);\\n    }\\n\\n    #[test]\\n    fn test_rejects_missing_footprint_with_trace_only() {\\n        let mut req = Request::new(());\\n        req.metadata_mut().insert(\\n            \\\"x-ghostbridge-trace-id\\\",\\n            MetadataValue::from_static(\\\"trace-abc\\\"),\\n        );\\n        let result = ghostbridge_interceptor(req);\\n        assert!(result.is_err());\\n        assert_eq!(result.unwrap_err().code(), tonic::Code::Unauthenticated);\\n    }\\n\\n    #[test]\\n    fn test_identity_sled_repr_c_layout() {\\n        let size = std::mem::size_of::<IdentitySled>();\\n        assert_eq!(\\n            size, 152,\\n            \\\"IdentitySled must be exactly 152 bytes per spec, got {} bytes\\\",\\n            size\\n        );\\n    }\\n\\n    #[test]\\n    fn test_footprint_mismatch_detection() {\\n        let sled_footprint: [u8;
