TypeScript\\n\\n> **Bindings not shown here:** This README covers the most common managed-agents flows for TypeScript. If you need a class, method, namespace, field, or behavior that isn't shown, WebFetch the TypeScript SDK repo **or the relevant docs page** from `shared/live-sources.md` rather than guess. Do not extrapolate from cURL shapes or another language's SDK.\\n\\n> **Agents are persistent — create once, reference by ID.** Store the agent ID returned by `agents.create` and pass it to every subsequent `sessions.create`; do not call `agents.create` in the request path. The Anthropic CLI is one convenient way to create agents and environments from version-controlled YAML — its URL is in `shared/live-sources.md`. The examples below show in-code creation for completeness; in production the create call belongs in setup, not in the request path.\\n\\n## Installation\\n\\n```bash\\nnpm install @anthropic-ai/sdk\\n```\\n\\n## Client Initialization\\n\\n```typescript\\nimport Anthropic from \\\"@anthropic-ai/sdk\\\";\\n\\n// Default (uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var)\\nconst client = new Anthropic();\\n\\n// Explicit API key\\nconst client = new Anthropic({ apiKey: \\\"your-api-key\\\" });\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Create an Environment\\n\\n```typescript\\nconst environment = await client.beta.environments.create(\\n  {\\n    name: \\\"my-dev-env\\\",\\n    config: {\\n      type: \\\"cloud\\\",\\n      networking: { type: \\\"unrestricted\\\" },\\n    },\\n  },\\n);\\nconsole.log(environment.id); // env_...\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Create an Agent (required first step)\\n\\n> ⚠️ **There is no inline agent config.** `model`/`system`/`tools` live on the agent object, not the session. Always start with `agents.create()` — the session only takes `agent: { type: \\\"agent\\\", id: agent.id }`.\\n\\n### Minimal\\n\\n```typescript\\n// 1. Create the agent (reusable, versioned)\\nconst agent = await client.beta.agents.create(\\n  {\\n    name: \\\"Coding Assistant\\\",\\n    model: \\\"claude-opus-4-7\\\",\\n    tools: [{ type: \\\"agent_toolset_20260401\\\", default_config: { enabled: true } }],\\n  },\\n);\\n\\n// 2. Start a session\\nconst session = await client.beta.sessions.create(\\n  {\\n    agent: { type: \\\"agent\\\", id: agent.id, version: agent.version },\\n    environment_id: environment.id,\\n  },\\n);\\nconsole.log(session.id, session.status);\\n```\\n\\n### With system prompt and custom tools\\n\\n```typescript\\nconst agent = await client.beta.agents.create(\\n  {\\n    name: \\\"Code Reviewer\\\",\\n    model: \\\"claude-opus-4-7\\\",\\n    system: \\\"You are a senior code reviewer.\\\",\\n    tools: [\\n      { type: \\\"agent_toolset_20260401\\\", default_config: { enabled: true } },\\n      {\\n        type: \\\"custom\\\",\\n        name: \\\"run_tests\\\",\\n        description: \\\"Run the test suite\\\",\\n        input_schema: {\\n          type: \\\"object\\\",\\n          properties: {\\n            test_path: { type: \\\"string\\\", description: \\\"Path to test file\\\" },\\n          },\\n          required: [\\\"test_path\\\"],\\n        },\\n      },\\n    ],\\n  },\\n);\\n\\nconst session = await client.beta.sessions.create(\\n  {\\n    agent: { type: \\\"agent\\\", id: agent.id, version: agent.version },\\n    environment_id: environment.id,\\n    title: \\\"Code review session\\\",\\n    resources: [\\n      {\\n        type: \\\"github_repository\\\",\\n        url: \\\"https://github.com/owner/repo\\\",\\n        mount_path: \\\"/workspace/repo\\\",\\n        authorization_token: process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN,\\n        branch: \\\"main\\\",\\n      },\\n    ],\\n  },\\n);\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Send a User Message\\n\\n```typescript\\nawait client.beta.sessions.events.send(\\n  session.id,\\n  {\\n    events: [\\n      {\\n        type: \\\"user.message\\\",\\n        content: [{ type: \\\"text\\\", text: \\\"Review the auth module\\\" }],\\n      },\\n    ],\\n  },\\n);\\n```\\n\\n> 💡 **Stream-first:** Open the stream *before* (or concurrently with) sending the message. The stream only delivers events that occur after it opens — stream-after-send means early events arrive buffered in one batch. See [Steering Patterns](../../shared/managed-agents-events.md#steering-patterns).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Stream Events (SSE)\\n\\n```typescript\\n// Stream-first: open stream and send concurrently\\nconst [events] = await Promise.all([\\n  collectStream(session.id),\\n  client.beta.sessions.events.send(\\n    session.id,\\n    { events: [{ type: \\\"user.message\\\", content: [{ type: \\\"text\\\", text: \\\"...\\\" }] }] },\\n  ),\\n]);\\n\\n// Standalone stream iteration:\\nconst stream = await client.beta.sessions.events.stream(\\n  session.id,\\n);\\n\\nfor await (const event of stream) {\\n  switch (event.type) {\\n    case \\\"agent.message\\\":\\n      for (const block of event.content) {\\n        if (block.type === \\\"text\\\") {\\n          process.stdout.write(block.text);\\n        }\\n      }\\n      break;\\n    case \\\"agent.custom_tool_use\\\":\\n      // Custom tool invocation — session is now idle\\n      console.log(`\\\\nCustom tool call: ${event.name}`);\\n      console.log(`Input: ${JSON.stringify(event.input)}`);\\n      break;\\n    case \\\"session.status_idle\\\":\\n      console.log(\\\"\\\\n--- Agent idle ---\\\");\\n      break;\\n    case \\\"session.status_terminated\\\":\\n      console.log(\\\"\\\\n--- Session terminated ---\\\");\\n      break;\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Provide Custom Tool Result\\n\\n```typescript\\nawait client.beta.sessions.events.send(\\n  session.id,\\n  {\\n    events: [\\n      {\\n        type: \\\"user.custom_tool_result\\\",\\n        custom_tool_use_id: \\\"sevt_abc123\\\",\\n        content: [{ type: \\\"text\\\", text: \\\"All 42 tests passed.\\\" }],\\n      },\\n    ],\\n  },\\n);\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Poll Events\\n\\n```typescript\\nconst events = await client.beta.sessions.events.list(\\n  session.id,\\n);\\nfor (const event of events.data) {\\n  console.log(`${event.type}: ${event.id}`);\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Full Streaming Loop with Custom Tools\\n\\n```typescript\\nfunction runCustomTool(toolName: string, toolInput: unknown): string {\\n  if (toolName === \\\"run_tests\\\") {\\n    // Your tool implementation here\\n    return \\\"All tests passed.\\\";\\n  }\\n  return `Unknown tool: ${toolName}`;\\n}\\n\\nasync function runSession(client: Anthropic, sessionId: string) {\\n  while (true) {\\n    const stream = await client.beta.sessions.events.stream(\\n      sessionId,\\n    );\\n\\n    const toolCalls: Anthropic.Beta.Sessions.BetaManagedAgentsAgentCustomToolUseEvent[] = [];\\n\\n    for await (const event of stream) {\\n      if (event.type === \\\"agent.message\\\") {\\n        for (const block of event.content) {\\n          if (block.type === \\\"text\\\") {\\n            process.stdout.write(block.text);\\n          }\\n        }\\n      } else if (event.type === \\\"agent.custom_tool_use\\\") {\\n        toolCalls.push(event);\\n      } else if (event.type === \\\"session.status_idle\\\") {\\n        break;\\n      } else if (event.type === \\\"session.status_terminated\\\") {\\n        return;\\n      }\\n    }\\n\\n    if (toolCalls.length === 0) break;\\n\\n    // Process custom tool calls\\n    const results = toolCalls.map((call) => ({\\n      type: \\\"user.custom_tool_result\\\" as const,\\n      custom_tool_use_id: call.id,\\n      content: [{ type: \\\"text\\\" as const, text: runCustomTool(call.name, call.input) }],\\n    }));\\n\\n    await client.beta.sessions.events.send(\\n      sessionId,\\n      { events: results },\\n    );\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Upload a File\\n\\n```typescript\\nimport fs from \\\"fs\\\";\\n\\nconst file = await client.beta.files.upload({\\n  file: fs.createReadStream(\\\"data.csv\\\"),\\n  purpose: \\\"agent\\\",\\n});\\n\\n// Use in a session\\nconst session = await client.beta.sessions.create(\\n  {\\n    agent: { type: \\\"agent\\\", id: agent.id, version: agent.version },\\n    environment_id: environment.id,\\n    resources: [{ type: \\\"file\\\", file_id: file.id, mount_path: \\\"/workspace/data.csv\\\" }],\\n  },\\n);\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## List and Download Session Files\\n\\nList files the agent wrote to `/mnt/session/outputs/` during a session, then download them.\\n\\n```typescript\\nimport fs from \\\"fs\\\";\\n\\n// List files associated with a session\\nconst files = await client.beta.files.list({\\n  scope_id: session.id,\\n  betas: [\\\"managed-agents-2026-04-01\\\"],\\n});\\nfor (const f of files.data) {\\n  console.log(f.filename, f.size_bytes);\\n\\n  // Download and save to disk\\n  const resp = await client.beta.files.download(f.id);\\n  const buffer = Buffer.from(await resp.arrayBuffer());\\n  fs.writeFileSync(f.filename, buffer);\\n}\\n```\\n\\n> 💡 There's a brief indexing lag (~1–3s) between `session.status_idle` and output files appearing in `files.list`. Retry once or twice if the list is empty.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Session Management\\n\\n```typescript\\n// Get session details\\nconst session = await client.beta.sessions.retrieve(\\\"sesn_011CZxAbc123Def456\\\");\\nconsole.log(session.status, session.usage);\\n\\n// List sessions\\nconst sessions = await client.beta.sessions.list();\\n\\n// Delete a session\\nawait client.beta.sessions.delete(\\\"sesn_011CZxAbc123Def456\\\");\\n\\n// Archive a session\\nawait client.beta.sessions.archive(\\\"sesn_011CZxAbc123Def456\\\");\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## MCP Server Integration\\n\\n```typescript\\n// Agent declares MCP server (no auth here — auth goes in a vault)\\nconst agent = await client.beta.agents.create({\\n  name: \\\"MCP Agent\\\",\\n  model: \\\"claude-opus-4-7\\\",\\n  mcp_servers: [\\n    { type: \\\"url\\\", name: \\\"my-tools\\\", url: \\\"https://my-mcp-server.example.com/sse\\\" },\\n  ],\\n  tools: [\\n    { type: \\\"agent_toolset_20260401\\\", default_config: { enabled: true } },\\n    { type: \\\"mcp_toolset\\\", mcp_server_name: \\\"my-tools\\\" },\\n  ],\\n});\\n\\n// Session attaches vault(s) containing credentials for those MCP server URLs\\nconst session = await client.beta.sessions.create({\\n  agent: agent.id,\\n  environment_id: environment.id,\\n  vault_ids: [vault.id],\\n});\\n```\\n\\nSee `shared/managed-agents-tools.md` §Vaults for creating vaults and adding credentials.\\n</doc>\\n\\n## When to Use WebFetch\\n\\nUse WebFetch to get the latest documentation when:\\n\\n- User asks for \\\"latest\\\" or \\\"current\\\" information\\n- Cached data seems incorrect\\n- User asks about features not covered here\\n\\nLive documentation URLs are in `shared/live-sources.md`.\\n\\n## Common Pitfalls\\n\\n- Don't truncate inputs when passing files or content to the API. If the content is too long to fit in the context window, notify the user and discuss options (chunking, summarization, etc.) rather than silently truncating.\\n- **Opus 4.7 thinking:** Adaptive only. `thinking: {type: \\\"enabled\\\", budget_tokens: N}` returns 400 on Opus 4.7 — `budget_tokens` is fully removed there (along with `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`). Use `thinking: {type: \\\"adaptive\\\"}`.\\n- **Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 thinking:** Use `thinking: {type: \\\"adaptive\\\"}` — do NOT use `budget_tokens` for new 4.6 code (deprecated on both Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6; for gradual migration of existing code, see the transitional escape hatch in `shared/model-migration.md` — note this carve-out does not apply to Opus 4.7). For older models, `budget_tokens` must be less than `max_tokens` (minimum 1024). This will throw an error if you get it wrong.\\n- **4.6/4.7 family prefill removed:** Assistant message prefills (last-assistant-turn prefills) return a 400 error on Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, and Sonnet 4.6. Use structured outputs (`output_config.format`) or system prompt instructions to control response format instead.\\n- **Confirm migration scope before editing:** When a user asks to migrate code to a newer Claude model without naming a specific file, directory, or file list, **ask which scope to apply first** — the entire working directory, a specific subdirectory, or a specific set of files. Do not start editing until the user confirms. Imperative phrasings like \\\"migrate my codebase\\\", \\\"move my project to X\\\", \\\"upgrade to Sonnet 4.6\\\", or bare \\\"migrate to Opus 4.7\\\" are **still ambiguous** — they tell you what to do but not where, so ask. Proceed without asking only when the prompt names an exact file, a specific directory, or an explicit file list (\\\"migrate `app.py`\\\", \\\"migrate everything under `services/`\\\", \\\"update `a.py` and `b.py`\\\"). See `shared/model-migration.md` Step 0.\\n- **`max_tokens` defaults:** Don't lowball `max_tokens` — hitting the cap truncates output mid-thought and requires a retry. For non-streaming requests, default to `~16000` (keeps responses under SDK HTTP timeouts). For streaming requests, default to `~64000` (timeouts aren't a concern, so give the model room). Only go lower when you have a hard reason: classification (`~256`), cost caps, deliberately short outputs, or **`max_tokens: 0`** for cache pre-warming (see `shared/prompt-caching.md` → Pre-warming).\\n- **128K output tokens:** Opus 4.6 and Opus 4.7 support up to 128K `max_tokens`, but the SDKs require streaming for values that large to avoid HTTP timeouts. This is a general API change, not 4.6-specific.\\n- **Don't reimplement SDK functionality:** The SDK provides high-level helpers — use them instead of building from scratch. Use `Anthropic.MessageParam` for messages, `Anthropic.Tool` for tool definitions, `Anthropic.ToolUseBlock` / `Anthropic.ToolResultBlockParam` for tool results, `Anthropic.Message` for responses. Defining your own `interface ChatMessage { role: string; content: unknown }` duplicates what the SDK already provides and loses type safety.\\n- **Report and document output:** For tasks that produce reports, documents, or visualizations, the code execution sandbox has `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `matplotlib`, `pillow`, and `pypdf` pre-installed. It is fundamentally a **socket networking** architecture: services communicate via Unix domain sockets (gRPC over UDS) and the network fabric is built on **Open vSwitch (OVS) with OpenFlow routing**, managed inside **Incus containers**.\\n\\n**Why:** The system is designed around zero-copy shared memory (`/dev/shm` SchemaEngine), WireGuard identity, Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain), and a full compliance/accountability loop via gRPC metadata headers (`X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`, `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`).\\n\\n**Key crates and roles:**\\n- `op-grpc-bridge` — gRPC client/server, schema engine (over Unix sockets)\\n- `op-dbus-mirror` — D-Bus → OVSDB event mirroring, JSON-RPC interface\\n- `op-network` — OpenFlow controller, OVS/OVSDB integration, rtnetlink\\n- `op-xdp-ovs-incus` — XDP/eBPF + OVS + Incus container networking\\n- `op-cognitive-mcp` — AI/MCP layer, RAG pipeline, soul memory, Qdrant\\n- `op-assistant-grpc` — User-facing assistant overlay (newest layer)\\n- `op-identity` — WireGuard identity / A.N.N.A. Scribe / Snowball sessions\\n- `op-blockchain` — Btrfs vectorized footprint ledger\\n\\n**Incus containers in use:** `assistant`, `mail-3tched`, `wg-xray`\\n\\n**How to apply:** When debugging networking issues, always think in terms of Unix socket paths, OVS/OpenFlow rules, and Incus container networking — NOT traditional TCP/IP or systemd-networkd assumptions. gRPC is over UDS internally. The turn lifecycle lives in `chat_loop.rs` (`ForcedToolChatLoop`), system prompt assembly in `system_prompt.rs`, tool loading in `tool_loader.rs`. The memory infrastructure is already built but not wired into the stream:\\n- `CognitiveMemoryStore` — CozoDB-backed namespace key/value store (`op-cognitive-mcp/src/memory_store.rs`)\\n- `MemoryService` — gRPC CRUD over CognitiveMemoryStore (`op-assistant-grpc/src/memory.rs`)\\n- `SoulService` — per-container soul storage (`op-assistant-grpc/src/soul.rs`)\\n- `QdrantSemanticShuttle` — Qdrant + Voyage AI `voyage-4` 1024-dim embeddings (`op-cognitive-mcp/src/qdrant_shuttle.rs`, existing collection `ctl_plane_reasoning_episodes` is for accountability loop — do not use)\\n- UserDB has just been migrated to CozoDB — do not add any dependency on user records\\n\\n---\\n\\n**Identity and memory model:**\\n\\nThe chatbot is a user entity with a session. Every user has one container. The session carries `container_id` directly — this is the authority, no user record lookup needed.\\n\\nThree memory layers, injected at session start in this order:\\n\\n```\\n1. system identity     — chatbot's global persona (session-scoped)\\n2. soul                — loaded via session.container_id from SoulService\\n                         each container has its own individual soul (work/home/barmitzvah)\\n3. domain memory       — loaded via session.container_id from CognitiveMemoryStore\\n                         namespace: container:{container_id}\\n                         isolated per container — work never bleeds into home\\n```\\n\\nSystem prompt injection order:\\n`FIXED_BASE_PROMPT` (immutable, never modify) | system identity | soul block | domain memory block\\n\\n---\\n\\n**The memory loop owns both CozoDB and Qdrant for user memory. Nothing else touches these directly.**\\n\\n---\\n\\n**What needs to be built:**\\n\\n**1. Session start — inject all three layers**\\n\\nRead `container_id` from the session. Then:\\n- Load chatbot system-wide identity from session\\n- Load soul for `container_id` from `SoulService`\\n- Embed opening message via Voyage AI → semantic query Qdrant `user_memory` collection scoped to `container_id` → load matched entries in full from `CognitiveMemoryStore` (`container:{container_id}` namespace)\\n- Fall back to loading `MEMORY_INDEX` key from CozoDB if Qdrant is unavailable\\n\\n**2. Post-turn memory detection — non-blocking**\\n\\nAfter each turn completes in `chat_loop.rs`, spawn async task (must not stall the stream):\\n- Detect new memorable information in the completed turn\\n- Write to CognitiveMemoryStore (`container:{container_id}` namespace)\\n- Embed via Voyage AI → upsert vector to Qdrant `user_memory` collection with `container_id` as payload\\n- Update `MEMORY_INDEX` key in the namespace\\n\\nBoth writes in the same async task. Qdrant failure is non-fatal — log and continue, CozoDB is the durable record.\\n\\nMemory categories to detect:\\n- `user` — preferences, expertise, collaboration style\\n- `project` — decisions, goals, context not derivable from code\\n- `feedback` — corrections or confirmed approaches\\n- `reference` — external systems, resource locations\\n\\n**3. MEMORY_INDEX**\\n\\nOne key per namespace. Format: `slug — one-line description` per line. Updated on every write. Injected at session start for orientation before full entries load.\\n\\n**4. Qdrant `user_memory` collection**\\n\\nCreate separate from `ctl_plane_reasoning_episodes`. Payload per vector: entry key + `container_id`. Queries at session start scope to active `container_id`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n**Constraints:**\\n- `crates/op-chat/` is the implementation boundary — memory loop logic stays in this plugin\\n- `FIXED_BASE_PROMPT` in `system_prompt.rs` is immutable — memory block appends after it\\n- `container_id` comes from the session — no user record lookup (UserDB in migration)\\n- Soul memory and domain memory are both container-scoped\\n- No new CozoDB schemas — use existing `store_entry` / `retrieve_entry` / `query_entries`\\n- Qdrant `user_memory` collection is separate from the accountability loop collection\\n\\n**Ask factory to:**\\nAssess what is already partially wired, identify what can ship immediately vs. what has dependencies, and propose a sequenced implementation order. Flag any conflicts with the current UserDB migration state.\"}]\n674:[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Good timing then — ask factory for a status report first before handing it the full prompt, so you're not duplicating work or overwriting what's in progress.\\n\\nSomething like:\\n\\n---\\n\\n**Status check before continuing memory loop implementation:**\\n\\nWhat has been completed so far on the memory loop in `crates/op-chat/`? Specifically:\\n- Is `MEMORY_INDEX` implemented?\\n- Is Qdrant `user_memory` collection created and being written to?\\n- Is session start injection wired into `system_prompt.rs`?\\n- Is post-turn detection hooked into `chat_loop.rs`?\\n- Is soul loading from `SoulService` wired?\\n- Is `container_id` being read from the session?\\n\\nList what is done, what is partially done, and what is not started. Then continue from where work stopped.\\n\\n---\\n\\nThat way factory picks up its own thread rather than restarting cold.\"}]\n675:[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"That's a clean status report — hand it back with a go:\\n\\n---\\n\\n**Continue memory loop implementation. Wire `handle_chat` — read `container_id` from `RpcRequest::Chat`, call `MemoryLoop::inject_session_memory` before building messages, call `spawn_post_turn_memory_task` after `pipeline.process_message()` returns\\n3. Wire analytics route — add `/api/analytics/semantic-search` to router in `routes/mod.rs`\\n7. Verify — `cargo check --workspace`, rebuild UI, restart server\\n\\nDo not skip steps or reorder. match field_type {\n        FieldType::String => \"string\".to_string(),\n        FieldType::Integer => \"integer\".to_string(),\n        FieldType::Float => \"float\".to_string(),\n"}}

&str,\n        tool_calls: &[(String, Value)],\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        let ns = Self::namespace_for(container_id);\n        let mut new_memories: Vec<(String, MemoryCategory, Value)> = n.starts_with(\"ovs_\") || n.starts_with(\"s6_\") || n.starts_with(\"incus_\")\n        }) {\n            let key = format!(\"ref-{}-{}\", tool_name, Utc::now().timestamp());\n            new_memories.push((\n                key,\n                MemoryCategory::Reference,\n                json!({\"tool\": tool_name, \"args\": args}),\n            ));\n        }\n\n        // Write to CozoDB (durable)\n        for (key, cat, value) in &new_memories {\n            if let Err(e) = cozo\n                .store_entry(\n                    &ns,\n                    key,\n                    value.clone(),\n                    vec![cat.as_str().to_string()],\n                    None,\n                )\n                .await\n            {\n                warn!(\"Failed to store {\n        let lower = text.to_lowercase();\n        if lower.contains(\"project\") || lower.contains(\"goal\") || lower.contains(\"decided\") {\n            MemoryCategory::Project\n        } else if lower.contains(\"prefer\") || lower.contains(\"always\") || lower.contains(\"never\") {\n            MemoryCategory::User\n        } else if lower.contains(\"correct\") || lower.contains(\"wrong\") || lower.contains(\"should\") {\n            MemoryCategory::Feedback\n        } else {\n            MemoryCategory::Reference\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn memory_key(text: &str) -> String {\n        // Regex::new(r\"[^a-z0-9-]\")\n            .expect(\"hardcoded regex pattern is valid\")\n            .replace_all(&slug, \"\");\n        format!(\"{}-{}\", slug, Utc::now().timestamp())\n    }\n\n    async fn update_memory_index(\n        cozo: &Arc<CognitiveMemoryStore>,\n        namespace: &str,\n        new_entries: &[(String, MemoryCategory, Value)],\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        // Read existing index\n        let existing = cozo\n            .retrieve_entry(namespace, \"MEMORY_INDEX\")\n            .await\n            .unwrap_or_default();\n\n        let mut lines: Vec<String> = existing\n            .map(|e| e.value.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string()).unwrap_or_default())\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n            .lines()\n            .map(|s| s.to_string())\n            .collect();\n\n        // Append new entries as one-liner slugs\n        for (key, cat, value) in new_entries {\n            let preview = match value {\n                Value::String(s) => {\n                    let truncated = if s.len() > 60 {\n                        format!(\"{}...\", &s[..60])\n                    } else {\n                        s.clone()\n                    };\n                    truncated\n                }\n                other => other.to_string().chars().take(60).collect(),\n            };\n            lines.push(format!(\"{} — [{}] {}\", key, cat.as_str(), preview));\n        }\n\n        // Deduplicate and limit\n        lines.sort();\n        lines.dedup();\n        if lines.len() > 100 {\n            let skip = lines.len() - 100;\n            lines = lines.into_iter().skip(skip).collect();\n        }\n\n        let index_value = json!(lines.join(\"\\n\"));\n        cozo.store_entry(\n            namespace,\n            \"MEMORY_INDEX\",\n            index_value,\n            vec![\"index\".to_string()],\n            None,\n        )\n        .await\n        .context(\"update MEMORY_INDEX\")?;\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n"}}

Result<Qdrant> {\n    let url = std::env::var(\"COGNITIVE_MCP_QDRANT_URL\")\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"http://127.0.0.1:6334\".into());\n    Qdrant::from_url(&url)\n        .build()\n        .context(\"Failed to build Qdrant client\")\n}\n\n/// Load the Voyage API key from a secret file when env vars are unset.\n///\n/// Defaults to `~/.ssh/mongo-voyage`; override with the\n/// `COGNITIVE_MCP_VOYAGE_KEY_FILE` env var. The first non-empty line is used\n/// (so a key file with a trailing newline or comment lines works).\nfn voyage_key_from_file() -> Option<String> {\n    let path = std::env::var(\"COGNITIVE_MCP_VOYAGE_KEY_FILE\")\n        .ok()\n        .map(std::path::PathBuf::from)\n        .or_else(|| std::env::var_os(\"HOME\").map(|h| Path::new(&h).join(\".ssh/mongo-voyage\")))?;\n\n    let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).ok()?;\n    // The creds file may contain multiple credential types (Atlas service\n    // account ID/secret, plus a Voyage API key).  We must skip service\n    // account lines and pick the actual API key.\n    let key = contents\n        .lines()\n        .map(str::trim)\n        .find(|l| {\n            !l.is_empty()\n                && !l.starts_with('#')\n                // skip Atlas service-account tokens\n                && !l.starts_with(\"mdb_sa_id_\")\n                && !l.starts_with(\"mdb_sa_sk_\")\n                // line should look like a Voyage key (MongoDB-hosted or public)\n                && (l.starts_with(\"al-\") || l.starts_with(\"pa-\"))\n        })?\n        .to_string();\n\n    if key.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        info!(path = %path.display(), \"Loaded Voyage API key from file\");\n        Some(key)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Determine the correct Voyage endpoint for a given API key.\nfn voyage_url_for_key(key: &str) -> &'static str {\n    let trimmed = key.trim();\n    if trimmed.starts_with(\"al-\") {\n        VOYAGE_MONGODB_URL\n    } else {\n        VOYAGE_PUBLIC_URL\n    }\n}\n\n/// Map a scored Qdrant point + payload into a `RagResult`.\nfn point_to_result(pt: ScoredPoint) -> RagResult {\n    let p = serde_json::to_value(&pt.payload).unwrap_or_default();\n    RagResult {\n        score: pt.score,\n        repo: str_field(&p, \"repo\"),\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T22:24:37.205Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes: vectorization is the embedding step.\n\n**How It Works**\n1. **Vectorization / indexing**\n   Raw evidence is chunked, embedded by Voyage, then stored in Qdrant:\n   `text chunk -> Voyage embedding vector -> Qdrant point + payload`\n\n2. **Retrieval**\n   A user/chatbot query is embedded with the matching Voyage retrieval model, then Qdrant returns nearest vectors:\n   `query -> Voyage query vector -> Qdrant search -> evidence payloads`\n\n3. **Chatbot answer**\n   The chatbot does **not** reason from Qdrant vectors directly. It receives the retrieved evidence text/payloads in its prompt/context, then answers with citations/trace IDs.\n\n**Important Rule**\nFor one Qdrant collection, the document-vectorization model and query-retrieval model must be compatible. Usually that means the **same model** with different input types:\n\n- indexing: `input_type = \"document\"`\n- searching: `input_type = \"query\"`\n\nSo for the main semantic memory path:\n\n```text\ncollection: user_memory / ctl_plane_reasoning_episodes\ndocument model: voyage-4\nquery model: voyage-4\ndimension: 1024\n```\n\nNot `large`, agreed.\n\n**Model Layout**\nUse different models by **collection/domain**, not randomly inside one collection:\n\n```text\nOperational/accountability evidence\n  collection: ctl_plane_reasoning_episodes\n  model: voyage-4\n  purpose: A.N.N.A. Scribe trace search, chatbot confrontation\n\nUser/container memory\n  collection: user_memory\n  model: voyage-4\n  purpose: chatbot remembers user/project/session context\n\nCode/repo knowledge\n  collection: code_knowledge\n  model: voyage-code-3\n  purpose: source-code and infra retrieval\n\nLegal/compliance subscriber knowledge\n  collection: legal_compliance_evidence\n  model: legal/law-oriented Voyage model if MongoDB Voyage exposes one\n  purpose: OSCAL, GDPR, EU AI Act, contracts, subscriber counsel\n```\n\n**Where The Lawyer Model Goes**\nThe lawyer model should **not** replace the main model. It belongs in the compliance/legal evidence collection and in the Compliance Engine roles:\n\n- **Olivia Scal**: OSCAL/FedRAMP/control mappings\n- **E.U.gene Risk**: EU AI Act\n- **Penny Privacy**: GDPR/privacy\n- **Reggie O.P.A.**: policy/prosecution checks\n\nA subscriber with legal/compliance features gets an extra collection:\n\n```text\ntenant:<id>:legal_compliance_evidence\n```\n\nThe chatbot can retrieve from both:\n\n```text\nA.N.N.A. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n"}}

The subid taxonomy is the missing organizing layer for the Voyage/Qdrant plan.\n\nUse **Voyage 4 for now everywhere** because of the token economics. The separation should be by **subid + collection metadata**, not by different embedding models yet.\n\n**Pipeline With Subids**\nEvery vectorized thing gets both:\n\n```text\nuuid  = machine identity / stable point identity\nsubid = operational taxonomy / “what kind of thing is this?”\n```\n\nThen Qdrant payloads should carry:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"uuid\": \"...\",\n  \"subid\": \"obs.service.accountability.semantic-search@v1\",\n  \"trace_id\": \"...\",\n  \"session_id\": \"...\",\n  \"schema_name\": \"...\",\n  \"plugin_id\": \"...\",\n  \"source_subid\": \"...\",\n  \"control_refs\": [],\n  \"statement_refs\": [],\n  \"content\": \"...\"\n}\n```\n\n**How The Categories Fit**\n`src.*` is where evidence comes from:\n\n```text\nsrc.software.workspace.index@v1\nsrc.service.chat-transcript.capture@v1\nsrc.service.notebooklm.export@v1\nsrc.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1\n```\n\n`sch.*` is the schema/contract:\n\n```text\nsch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1\nsch.service.ctl-plane-chatbot.reasoning-episode@v1\nsch.service.oscal-subid-registry.contract@v1\n```\n\n`prj.*` is the D-Bus projection:\n\n```text\nprj.service.projected-object.publish@v1\nprj.service.plugin-projection.render@v1\n```\n\n`mut.*` is anything that changes state, and must include `actor_id` + `capability_id`:\n\n```text\nmut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1\nmut.service.chat-memory.store@v1\nmut.service.qdrant.upsert-vector@v1\n```\n\n`obs.*` is retrieval/search/read:\n\n```text\nobs.service.code-rag.search@v1\nobs.service.accountability.semantic-search@v1\nobs.service.user-memory.retrieve@v1\n```\n\n`evt.*` is the proof/audit event, must include `event_id` or `event_hash`:\n\n```text\nevt.service.snowball.append@v1\nevt.service.reasoning-episode.vectorized@v1\nevt.network.xray.identity-injected@v1\n```\n\n`exp.*` is what the user/tool sees:\n\n```text\nexp.service.accountability-page.render@v1\nexp.service.chatbot.answer@v1\nexp.service.cognitive-mcp.tool@v1\n```\n\n**Voyage 4 Role**\nFor now:\n\n```text\nmodel: voyage-4\ninput_type=document for vectorization\ninput_type=query for retrieval\ndimension: 1024\n```\n\nUse it for code too until the economics justify `voyage-code-3`.\n\nThe important part is that the **model name goes in payload/config**, while the **subid says what the vector means**. That lets you revectorize later without losing taxonomy:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"embedding_model\": \"voyage-4\",\n  \"embedding_input_type\": \"document\",\n  \"vector_version\": \"v1\",\n  \"subid\": \"src.software.workspace.index@v1\"\n}\n```\n\n**A.N.N.A. Scribe’s Place**\nA.N.N.A. Scribe is not the embedding model. It is the notary/arbitrator that binds:\n\n```text\nsession_id + trace_id + hashed footprint + subid + schema\n```\n\nSo the final demo chain is:\n\n```text\nPluginSchema exists\n→ artifact gets uuid + subid\n→ A.N.N.A. Scribe stamps trace/session proof\n→ Voyage 4 embeds the content\n→ Qdrant stores vector + subid payload\n→ chatbot retrieves via obs.* query\n→ Accountability Page renders exp.* evidence\n```\n\nThe practical implementation rule: every Qdrant upsert/search path should require a subid. If it cannot classify the vector as `src/sch/prj/mut/obs/evt/exp`, it should not enter the evidence store.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

a{color:var(--a2);text-decoration:none}\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n\n<!-- HERO -->\n<section style=\"border:none;padding-top:90px\">\n  <div class=\"wrap\">\n    <div class=\"eyebrow\">GhostBridge × Netmaker</div>\n    <h1>Netmaker isn't a dependency in this project.<br><span class=\"grad\">It's core code.</span></h1>\n    <p class=\"lead\">A zero-trust, compliance-grade AI control plane — built in Rust, running on a Netmaker mesh that we treat as the spine: the transport <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">and</b> the root of identity.</p>\n    <div class=\"chips\">\n      <span class=\"chip\">Rust · 31-crate workspace</span>\n      <span class=\"chip\">No-NIC hardened mesh</span>\n      <span class=\"chip\">OSCAL-gated</span>\n      <span class=\"chip\">Tamper-evident chain</span>\n      <span class=\"chip\">Confrontable AI</span>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"hero-sub\">Honest note: this is the first time anyone outside the project will have seen it. We booked the trial call because it was the door — but what we really want is for a sharp engineer on your side to look closely and tell us, straight, what you think.</p>\n    <div style=\"margin-top:20px\"><span class=\"pill\"><span class=\"live\"></span> cognitive-mcp verified live this session</span></div>\n  </div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- WHAT IT IS -->\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow\">The one paragraph</div>\n  <h2>A mesh you can <span class=\"grad\">trust</span>, not just connect</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">Traffic flows through a hardened pipeline — decoy ingress, identity sled, Xray header injection, a per-hop interceptor — where every request is classified, routed, gated against machine-readable policy (OSCAL), and recorded into a tamper-evident hash-linked chain. An AI layer reasons over that verified history but <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">cannot execute anything itself</b>. Same codebase ships as a <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">privacy</b> edition or a <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">compliance</b> edition — one config flag decides which world you're in.</p>\n</div></section>\n\n<!-- GOVERNANCE STACK -->\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow\">How it works</div>\n  <h2>One governance pattern, every layer</h2>\n  <p>Make the wrong thing impossible first; gate what's left; record everything. The same idea at three scales — <span class=\"kv\">Rust</span> says code can't be wrong, <span class=\"kv\">schema</span> says state can't be invalid, <span class=\"kv\">A.N.N.A.</span> says action can't be unauthorized — and the chain says it's all on the record.</p>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap\" style=\"margin-top:14px\">\n    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 900 470\" width=\"100%\" role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Governance stack\">\n      <defs>\n        <linearGradient id=\"g\" x1=\"0\" y1=\"0\" x2=\"1\" y2=\"0\"><stop offset=\"0\" stop-color=\"#7c5cff\"/><stop offset=\"1\" stop-color=\"#22d3ee\"/></linearGradient>\n        <marker id=\"ar\" markerWidth=\"9\" markerHeight=\"9\" refX=\"6\" refY=\"3\" orient=\"auto\"><path d=\"M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z\" fill=\"#5b6478\"/></marker>\n      </defs>\n      <!-- rows -->\n      <g font-size=\"13\" fill=\"#e8ebf2\">\n        <!-- helper repeated boxes -->\n        <g>\n          <rect x=\"40\" y=\"20\" width=\"820\" height=\"46\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/>\n          <rect x=\"40\" y=\"20\" width=\"6\" height=\"46\" rx=\"3\" fill=\"url(#g)\"/>\n          <text x=\"64\" y=\"40\" fill=\"#22d3ee\">RUST</text><text x=\"64\" y=\"57\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"11\">the compiler is the first enforcer — invalid code won't build</text>\n        </g>\n        <g>\n          <rect x=\"40\" y=\"80\" width=\"820\" height=\"46\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/>\n          <rect x=\"40\" y=\"80\" width=\"6\" height=\"46\" rx=\"3\" fill=\"url(#g)\"/>\n          <text x=\"64\" y=\"100\" fill=\"#22d3ee\">SCHEMA</text><text x=\"64\" y=\"117\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"11\">invalid STATE is unrepresentable — the silent gate, before any rule runs</text>\n        </g>\n        <g>\n          <rect x=\"40\" y=\"140\" width=\"820\" height=\"46\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/>\n          <rect x=\"40\" y=\"140\" width=\"6\" height=\"46\" rx=\"3\" fill=\"url(#g)\"/>\n          <text x=\"64\" y=\"160\" fill=\"#22d3ee\">TRAFFIC COP · Gemma + Xray</text><text x=\"64\" y=\"177\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"11\">Gemma classifies (what is this?) + Xray routes (where to?) — directs, never authorizes</text>\n        </g>\n        <g>\n          <rect x=\"40\" y=\"200\" width=\"820\" height=\"46\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/>\n fill=\"#22d3ee\">A.N.N.A.</text><text x=\"64\" y=\"297\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"11\">OSCAL-gated approval at EVERY hop (HMAC-stamped identity header) — the higher-up that says yes/no</text>\n action becomes a block</text>\n        </g>\n        <g>\n          <rect x=\"40\" y=\"380\" width=\"820\" height=\"46\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/>\n          <rect x=\"40\" y=\"380\" width=\"6\" height=\"46\" rx=\"3\" fill=\"url(#g)\"/>\n          <text x=\"64\" y=\"400\" fill=\"#22d3ee\">THE LOOP</text><text x=\"64\" y=\"417\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"11\">AI reassembles chain → Qdrant (semantic) + Cozo (realtime graph) → reasons → new blocks</text>\n        </g>\n      </g>\n      <!-- arrows down right side -->\n      <g stroke=\"#5b6478\" stroke-width=\"1.4\">\n        <line x1=\"878\" y1=\"66\" x2=\"878\" y2=\"80\" marker-end=\"url(#ar)\"/>\n        <line x1=\"878\" y1=\"126\" x2=\"878\" y2=\"140\" marker-end=\"url(#ar)\"/>\n        <line x1=\"878\" y1=\"186\" x2=\"878\" y2=\"200\" marker-end=\"url(#ar)\"/>\n        <line x1=\"878\" y1=\"246\" x2=\"878\" y2=\"260\" marker-end=\"url(#ar)\"/>\n        <line x1=\"878\" y1=\"306\" x2=\"878\" y2=\"320\" marker-end=\"url(#ar)\"/>\n        <line x1=\"878\" y1=\"366\" x2=\"878\" y2=\"380\" marker-end=\"url(#ar)\"/>\n      </g>\n    </svg>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<!-- IDENTITY & MUTATION VECTORS -->\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow\">What's on every block</div>\n  <h2>Identity vector × Mutation vector</h2>\n  <p>Two structured vectors ride every entry in the chain. Together they make <span class=\"kv mono\">\"who changed what, when, on whose authority\"</span> a provable query — and they're exactly what A.N.N.A. gates on.</p>\n  <div class=\"grid g2\" style=\"margin-top:14px\">\n    <div class=\"card\" style=\"border-color:#1f3a31\">\n      <h3><span class=\"dot\" style=\"background:var(--a3)\"></span>Identity vector — the WHO</h3>\n      <p><span class=\"mono kv\">session_id = Argon2(PSK, salt=WG_pubkey)</span><br><br>Derived from the Netmaker WireGuard key. Stable, deterministic, unforgeable. Privacy mode: the key alone (anonymous, consistent). Compliance mode: resolves to a verified user.</p>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"card\" style=\"border-color:#26384a\">\n      <h3><span class=\"dot\" style=\"background:var(--a2)\"></span>Mutation vector — the WHAT-CHANGED</h3>\n      <p>The <span class=\"mono kv\">mut</span> class of the subid taxonomy: <i>what kind</i> of change, <i>on what resource</i>, <i>under what OSCAL authority</i>. Reads (<span class=\"mono\">obs</span>) and changes (<span class=\"mono\">mut</span>) are distinct classes — so you can prove nothing was altered, not just that it was logged.</p>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap\" style=\"margin-top:16px\">\n    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 900 170\" width=\"100%\" role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Identity and mutation vectors combine into a block\">\n      <defs><marker id=\"ar4\" markerWidth=\"9\" markerHeight=\"9\" refX=\"6\" refY=\"3\" orient=\"auto\"><path d=\"M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z\" fill=\"#5b6478\"/></marker>\n        <linearGradient id=\"g4\" x1=\"0\" y1=\"0\" x2=\"1\" y2=\"0\"><stop offset=\"0\" stop-color=\"#7c5cff\"/><stop offset=\"1\" stop-color=\"#22d3ee\"/></linearGradient></defs>\n      <rect x=\"40\" y=\"40\" width=\"210\" height=\"40\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a5a4a\"/><text x=\"145\" y=\"65\" fill=\"#34d399\" font-size=\"12\" text-anchor=\"middle\" font-family=\"ui-monospace\">identity_vector (WHO)</text>\n      <rect x=\"40\" y=\"95\" width=\"210\" height=\"40\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#26384a\"/><text x=\"145\" y=\"120\" fill=\"#22d3ee\" font-size=\"12\" text-anchor=\"middle\" font-family=\"ui-monospace\">mutation_vector (WHAT)</text>\n      <rect x=\"380\" y=\"55\" width=\"170\" height=\"64\" rx=\"12\" fill=\"#11151f\" stroke=\"#3a3566\"/>\n      <text x=\"465\" y=\"82\" fill=\"#e8ebf2\" font-size=\"13\" text-anchor=\"middle\">A.N.N.A.</text>\n      <text x=\"465\" y=\"101\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"10.5\" text-anchor=\"middle\">role satisfies authority?</text>\n      <rect x=\"690\" y=\"48\" width=\"180\" height=\"78\" rx=\"12\" fill=\"#0c0e15\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/>\n      <text x=\"780\" y=\"72\" fill=\"#22d3ee\" font-size=\"12\" text-anchor=\"middle\" font-family=\"ui-monospace\">BLOCK</text>\n      <text x=\"780\" y=\"92\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"9.5\" text-anchor=\"middle\" font-family=\"ui-monospace\">id · mut · payload#</text>\n      <text x=\"780\" y=\"108\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"9.5\" text-anchor=\"middle\" font-family=\"ui-monospace\">timestamp · prev#</text>\n      <g stroke=\"#5b6478\" stroke-width=\"1.4\">\n        <line x1=\"250\" y1=\"60\" x2=\"378\" y2=\"78\" marker-end=\"url(#ar4)\"/>\n        <line x1=\"250\" y1=\"115\" x2=\"378\" y2=\"96\" marker-end=\"url(#ar4)\"/>\n        <line x1=\"550\" y1=\"87\" x2=\"688\" y2=\"87\" marker-end=\"url(#ar4)\"/>\n      </g>\n    </svg>\n  </div>\n  <p class=\"muted\" style=\"margin-top:12px\">Cross-examination becomes exact: <span class=\"mono\">identity #abc performed mut <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">config.write</b> on <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">netmaker.peer</b> at T, authorized by OSCAL <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">authorizing-official</b>.</span> That's the receipt.</p>\n</div></section>\n\n<!-- VOYAGE / SEMANTIC VECTORS -->\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow\">The semantic memory</div>\n  <h2>Voyage vectors → <span class=\"grad\">searchable meaning</span></h2>\n  <p>Identity & mutation vectors are <i>structured provenance</i>. <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">Voyage vectors are meaning.</b> Every block, document, and transcript is embedded by <span class=\"mono kv\">voyage-code-3</span> into <span class=\"mono kv\">Qdrant</span> — so the chain isn't just verifiable, it's <i>searchable by similarity</i>. This is the bottom pane when you cross-examine the agent, and the raw material the loop reasons over.</p>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:14px\">\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Embed</h3><p><span class=\"mono\">voyage-code-3</span> turns each chunk of the chain (actions, configs, docs, transcripts) into a high-dimensional vector. Code-aware, so it understands infra, not just prose.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Store &amp; search</h3><p>Vectors land in <span class=\"mono\">Qdrant</span>, keyed <span class=\"mono\">notebook:source:chunk</span>. Ask <i>\"show me peers like the one that misbehaved\"</i> — similarity, not keywords.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Rebuildable</h3><p>Qdrant is a <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">derived projection</b> of the chain. Lose it in a disk casualty → re-embed from the canonical blocks. Trust lives in the chain; retrieval lives here.</p></div>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap\" style=\"margin-top:16px\">\n    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 900 150\" width=\"100%\" role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Voyage embedding pipeline into Qdrant feeding the loop\">\n      <defs><marker id=\"ar5\" markerWidth=\"9\" markerHeight=\"9\" refX=\"6\" refY=\"3\" orient=\"auto\"><path d=\"M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z\" fill=\"#5b6478\"/></marker></defs>\n      <g font-size=\"12\" text-anchor=\"middle\">\n        <rect x=\"30\" y=\"52\" width=\"150\" height=\"46\" rx=\"10\" fill=\"#0c0e15\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/><text x=\"105\" y=\"73\" fill=\"#e8ebf2\">chain blocks</text><text x=\"105\" y=\"89\" fill=\"#6b7385\" font-size=\"10\">+ docs · transcripts</text>\n        <rect x=\"270\" y=\"52\" width=\"160\" height=\"46\" rx=\"10\" fill=\"#11151f\" stroke=\"#3a3566\"/><text x=\"350\" y=\"73\" fill=\"#22d3ee\">voyage-code-3</text><text x=\"350\" y=\"89\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"10\">embed</text>\n        <rect x=\"520\" y=\"52\" width=\"150\" height=\"46\" rx=\"10\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a5a4a\"/><text x=\"595\" y=\"73\" fill=\"#34d399\">Qdrant</text><text x=\"595\" y=\"89\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"10\">semantic vectors</text>\n        <rect x=\"760\" y=\"52\" width=\"120\" height=\"46\" rx=\"10\" fill=\"#0c0e15\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/><text x=\"820\" y=\"73\" fill=\"#e8ebf2\">the loop</text><text x=\"820\" y=\"89\" fill=\"#6b7385\" font-size=\"10\">+ cross-exam</text>\n      </g>\n      <g stroke=\"#5b6478\" stroke-width=\"1.4\">\n        <line x1=\"180\" y1=\"75\" x2=\"268\" y2=\"75\" marker-end=\"url(#ar5)\"/>\n        <line x1=\"430\" y1=\"75\" x2=\"518\" y2=\"75\" marker-end=\"url(#ar5)\"/>\n        <line x1=\"670\" y1=\"75\" x2=\"758\" y2=\"75\" marker-end=\"url(#ar5)\"/>\n      </g>\n    </svg>\n  </div>\n  <p class=\"muted\" style=\"margin-top:12px\">Two vector families, two jobs: <b style=\"color:var(--a2)\">Voyage</b> = \"find things <i>like</i> this\" (semantic). <b style=\"color:var(--a3)\">Identity / mutation</b> = \"who did <i>exactly</i> this, and was it allowed\" (provenance). The AI uses both — meaning to reason, provenance to prove.</p>\n</div></section>\n\n<!-- FOUR DIFFERENTIATORS -->\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow\">Why it's different</div>\n  <h2>Four things nobody else can credibly claim</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g2\" style=\"margin-top:14px\">\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>A brain with no hands</h3><p>The AI is a <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">delegator, recommender, fixer</b> — and that's the ceiling. <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">No internet, no execution rights, no execution control.</b> It proposes into a schema-shaped mold; a separate, OSCAL-gated, chained layer disposes. A compromised model can't do damage — worst case is a rejected suggestion.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>You can cross-examine it</h3><p>Every action is a chained, searchable block. Confront the agent in real time — <span class=\"mono kv\">\"why did you do this?\"</span> — and it answers with cryptographic receipts pulled live by semantic search. If the model confabulates, the evidence pane contradicts it. <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">An AI you can put on the stand.</b></p></div>\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>The chain is the truth</h3><p>The hash-linked chain is canonical and tamper-evident. Qdrant + Cozo are <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">AI-rebuilt projections</b> of it — lose them, re-derive them. It's a blockchain <i>by structure</i>, kept honest by <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">anchoring</b>, not consensus — the right call for a single-operator compliance ledger.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Schema-native, all the way down</h3><p>Components were <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">chosen because they're schema-based from the ground up</b> (e.g. zeroclaw), and the code is safe by construction (Rust — memory-safe, race-free, single static binaries). Governance holds at every layer because nothing was bolted on.</p></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<!-- THE DIAL -->\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow\">One dial</div>\n  <h2>As <span style=\"color:var(--a3)\">Snowden</span> as you want — or as <span style=\"color:var(--warn)\">Big&nbsp;Brother</span> as you want</h2>\n  <p>Same mesh, same chain, same confrontable AI. <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">Only the identity-linkage layer changes</b>, and it's a deploy-time config — not a rewrite, not a hidden switch.</p>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap\" style=\"margin-top:14px\">\n    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 900 210\" width=\"100%\" role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Privacy to compliance dial\">\n      <defs><linearGradient id=\"dial\" x1=\"0\" y1=\"0\" x2=\"1\" y2=\"0\"><stop offset=\"0\" stop-color=\"#34d399\"/><stop offset=\"1\" stop-color=\"#f59e0b\"/></linearGradient></defs>\n      <rect x=\"60\" y=\"92\" width=\"780\" height=\"12\" rx=\"6\" fill=\"url(#dial)\"/>\n      <circle cx=\"60\" cy=\"98\" r=\"11\" fill=\"#0a0b10\" stroke=\"#34d399\" stroke-width=\"3\"/>\n      <circle cx=\"840\" cy=\"98\" r=\"11\" fill=\"#0a0b10\" stroke=\"#f59e0b\" stroke-width=\"3\"/>\n      <text x=\"60\" y=\"60\" fill=\"#34d399\" font-size=\"15\" text-anchor=\"start\">PRIVACY EDITION</text>\n      <text x=\"60\" y=\"140\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"11.5\">key IS identity</text>\n      <text x=\"60\" y=\"158\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"11.5\">no PII · no email</text>\n      <text x=\"60\" y=\"176\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"11.5\">de-anon cryptographically impossible</text>\n      <text x=\"840\" y=\"60\" fill=\"#f59e0b\" font-size=\"15\" text-anchor=\"end\">COMPLIANCE EDITION</text>\n      <text x=\"840\" y=\"140\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"11.5\" text-anchor=\"end\">identity ↔ verified user</text>\n      <text x=\"840\" y=\"158\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"11.5\" text-anchor=\"end\">vault escrow + user graph</text>\n      <text x=\"840\" y=\"176\" fill=\"#8b93a7\" font-size=\"11.5\" text-anchor=\"end\">de-anon only on signed OSCAL authority</text>\n    </svg>\n  </div>\n  <p class=\"muted\" style=\"margin-top:14px\">Even in full-oversight mode, de-anonymization isn't a backdoor — it requires a signed OSCAL <span class=\"mono\">authorizing-official</span> action that <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">itself becomes a chained, confrontable block.</b> You can cross-examine the watchers.</p>\n</div></section>\n\n<!-- NO-NIC HARDENING -->\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow\">For Netmaker specifically</div>\n  <h2>A control server with <span class=\"grad\">no network interface</span></h2>\n  <p>The <span class=\"mono\">netmaker</span>, <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-mq</span> (Mosquitto) and <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-ui</span> containers run loopback-only. {"timestamp":"2026-06-14T22:38:04.578Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-14</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T22:38:14.348Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_yJcgJFb2xo7MC69IgbAX9hiQ","output":"Chunk ID: ec61b4\nWall time: 0.0001 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 5762\nOutput:\ntotal 444K\n-rw-r--r-- 1 jeremy jeremy 8.1K Jun 13 14:34 GhostBridge-Netmaker-pitch.md\n-rw-r--r-- 1 jeremy jeremy  32K Jun 13 14:32 GhostBridge-Netmaker.html\n-rw-r--r-- 1 jeremy jeremy 356K Jun 13 14:33 GhostBridge-Netmaker.pdf\n-rw-r--r-- 1 jeremy jeremy  390 Jun 13 13:54 cover-note.txt\n-rw-r--r-- 1 jeremy jeremy  27K Jun 13 14:32 index.html\n-rw-r--r-- 1 jeremy jeremy 9.1K Jun 13 13:04 system-overview-netmaker-spin.md\n# GhostBridge × Netmaker\n### Netmaker isn't a dependency in this project — it's core code.\n\n*A short read before we meet. Honestly: this is the first time anyone outside the\nproject will have seen it. We booked the trial/sales call because it was the door —\nbut what we actually want is for a sharp engineer on your side to look closely and\ntell us what you really think.*\n\n---\n\n## TL;DR (for the busy reader)\n\n- We've built a **zero-trust, compliance-grade AI control plane** — in Rust — that runs **on a Netmaker mesh** and treats it as the spine: the transport **and** the root of identity.\n- We deploy your control server in a pattern most of your customers don't: **no network interface at all** — loopback + unix sockets, fronted by Xray. A port scan returns nothing.\n- We already run Netmaker in production. We're not here for a standard enterprise eval — we're here because **you're already load-bearing in something we think is genuinely novel**, and you should see it.\n- **Why we're sending this:** not an ask. We already run this in production on what's available today — we just figured the people who built the layer it all stands on should be the first to see what got built on top of it.\n\n---\n\n## What GhostBridge is, in one paragraph\n\nGhostBridge turns a Netmaker mesh into a **trusted** backbone. Traffic flows through a hardened pipeline — decoy ingress, identity sled, Xray header injection, a per-hop interceptor — where every request is classified, routed, gated against machine-readable policy (OSCAL), and recorded into a **tamper-evident hash-linked chain**. An AI layer reasons over that verified history but **cannot execute anything itself**. Same codebase ships as a **privacy** edition or a **compliance** edition — one config flag decides which world you're in.\n\n---\n\n## How it works — one governance pattern, every layer\n\nThe whole system runs on a single discipline: **make the wrong thing impossible first; gate what's left; record everything.** Here it is top to bottom.\n\n```\n  RUST          the compiler is the first enforcer — invalid code won't build\n    ▼\n  SCHEMA        invalid STATE is unrepresentable — the silent gate, before any rule runs\n    ▼\n  TRAFFIC COP   Gemma classifies (what is this?) + Xray routes (where does it go?)\n  (Gemma+Xray)  — directs traffic, reports every decision up. Directs, never authorizes.\n    ▼\n  ZEROCLAW      routes to the right MODEL by cost / reasoning / specialty —\n                schema-native from the ground up, so it can't route off-policy\n    ▼\n  A.N.N.A.      OSCAL-gated approval at EVERY hop (HMAC-stamped identity header)\n                — the higher-up that actually says yes/no\n    ▼\n  CHAIN         hash-linked, tamper-evident evidence. Every action becomes a block.\n    ▼\n  THE LOOP      AI reassembles the chain into a semantic DB (Qdrant) + realtime graph\n                (Cozo), reasons over it, recommends/acts-by-delegation → new blocks\n```\n\n**The same idea at three scales:** Rust says *code can't be wrong*, schema says *state can't be invalid*, A.N.N.A. says *action can't be unauthorized* — and the chain says *and it's all on the record.*\n\n---\n\n## Four things that make this different\n\n**1. The AI is a brain with no hands.**\nThe chatbot is a **delegator, recommender, and fixer** — and that's the ceiling. **No internet access, no execution rights, no execution control.** It proposes into a schema-shaped mold; a separate, OSCAL-gated, chained layer disposes. A confabulating or compromised model can't do damage — the worst case is a rejected recommendation. Autonomous *reasoning* without autonomous *risk*.\n\n**2. You can cross-examine it.**\nBecause every action is a chained, content-addressed, searchable block, you can confront the agent in real time — *\"why did you do this?\"* — and it answers with **cryptographic receipts** pulled live by semantic search (chatbot on top, evidence on the bottom). If the model confabulates, the evidence pane contradicts it. **An AI you can put on the stand.**\n\n**3. The chain is the truth; the DB and graph are rebuilt views.**\nThe hash-linked chain is canonical and tamper-evident. Qdrant (semantic) and Cozo (realtime graph) are **AI-reassembled projections** of it — if they're lost or corrupted, you re-derive them from the chain. Trust lives in the chain; queryability lives in the projections. (It's a blockchain *by structure* — hashed, chained blocks — kept honest by **anchoring**, not consensus, which is the right call for a single-operator compliance system.)\n\n**4. One dial: Snowden ↔ Big Brother.**\nSame mesh, same chain, same confrontable AI — **only the identity-linkage layer changes**, at deploy time:\n- **Privacy edition (Snowden):** key *is* identity, no PII, de-anonymization **cryptographically impossible**.\n- **Compliance edition (Big Brother):** every actor attributable, de-anon **only on a signed OSCAL authority — which is itself a chained, confrontable block.** You can cross-examine the watchers.\n\n---\n\n## The Netmaker hardening pattern (the part we want to show you)\n\nYour control server runs with **no NIC**:\n- `netmaker`, `netmaker-mq` (Mosquitto), `netmaker-ui` → loopback only.\n- Exposed to the host as **unix sockets** (`/run/netmaker/api.sock`, `mq.sock`, `mqtts.sock`, `ui.sock`) via Incus proxy devices.\n- `wg-xray` + Xray terminate TLS and route by SNI to those sockets.\n\n**There is no open port on the Netmaker server.** The attack surface is a socket file behind the WireGuard + identity gate. We'd love to publish this jointly as a reference architecture for your security-conscious users.\n\n---\n\n## Why Netmaker is core, not a dependency\n\n- It's a **first-class state plugin** — managed by the same engine that runs the whole platform.\n- Its peers **are the identity model**: `session_id = Argon2(PSK, salt = WG_pubkey)`, rooted in the WireGuard pre-shared key you already manage. Remove Netmaker and the identity layer has no root. It is **link #0 of the evidence chain.**\n- **Every GhostBridge deployment is a hardened Netmaker deployment**, sold into regulated rooms Netmaker alone doesn't reach yet.
