Core Architectural Rules (The \\\"Reality\\\")\\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\\n\\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\\n\\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\\n\\n#### 5. It is fundamentally a **socket networking** architecture: services communicate via Unix domain sockets (gRPC over UDS) and the network fabric is built on **Open vSwitch (OVS) with OpenFlow routing**, managed inside **Incus containers**.\\n\\n**Why:** The system is designed around zero-copy shared memory (`/dev/shm` SchemaEngine), WireGuard identity, Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain), and a full compliance/accountability loop via gRPC metadata headers (`X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`, `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`).\\n\\n**Key crates and roles:**\\n- `op-grpc-bridge` — gRPC client/server, schema engine (over Unix sockets)\\n- `op-dbus-mirror` — D-Bus → OVSDB event mirroring, JSON-RPC interface\\n- `op-network` — OpenFlow controller, OVS/OVSDB integration, rtnetlink\\n- `op-xdp-ovs-incus` — XDP/eBPF + OVS + Incus container networking\\n- `op-cognitive-mcp` — AI/MCP layer, RAG pipeline, soul memory, Qdrant\\n- `op-assistant-grpc` — User-facing assistant overlay (newest layer)\\n- `op-identity` — WireGuard identity / A.N.N.A. Scribe / Snowball sessions\\n- `op-blockchain` — Btrfs vectorized footprint ledger\\n\\n**Incus containers in use:** `assistant`, `mail-3tched`, `wg-xray`\\n\\n**How to apply:** When debugging networking issues, always think in terms of Unix socket paths, OVS/OpenFlow rules, and Incus container networking — NOT traditional TCP/IP or systemd-networkd assumptions. gRPC is over UDS internally. {"timestamp":"2026-06-14T22:39:55.095Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"I read the Netmaker Claude context, especially [netmaker.handoff](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/netmaker.handoff) from the exported session `3840b230-12e4-4f60-9e0c-56e670d22fd9`, plus the pitch at [GhostBridge-Netmaker-pitch.md](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/GhostBridge-Netmaker-pitch.md).\n\nThe meeting is about showing Netmaker as core infrastructure, not a normal dependency: Netmaker provides the WireGuard identity spine, GhostBridge wraps it with schema/D-Bus authority, Xray identity routing, A.N.N.A. Scribe/Snowball accountability, and a “chatbot on top, semantic evidence on bottom” confrontable AI demo.\n\nCurrent truth check:\n\n- Real: there is a live D-Bus plugin object for Netmaker at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/netmaker`.\n- Real: `netmaker-ui` and `netmaker-mq` are running with loopback-only networking. Inside both containers I saw only `lo`, no NIC.\n- Real: host sockets exist at `/run/netmaker/{api.sock,mq.sock,mqtts.sock,ui.sock}`.\n- Real: `wg-xray` has routing config for `api.ghostbridge.tech`, `broker.ghostbridge.tech`, and `dashboard.ghostbridge.tech`.\n- Real: the UI path works through the TCP proxy: `127.0.0.1:28082` returns `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.\n\nGaps that matter before you say “this is fully operational”:\n\n- Main `netmaker` API container is currently `STOPPED`.\n- `/run/netmaker/api.sock` is not listening because the API container is stopped.\n- `wg-xray` does not currently show `/run/netmaker` mounted inside the container, despite the device config saying it should be mounted.\n- Xray currently routes Netmaker through loopback TCP redirects like `127.0.0.1:18081`, not directly to Unix sockets.\n- `netmaker-ui` listens on `0.0.0.0:80` inside the container, but because it has no NIC that is effectively loopback-contained. Acceptable, but phrase it carefully.\n- The pitch’s “we already run Netmaker in production” is too strong unless you mean the mesh/client side, because the Netmaker control API is stopped right now.\n\nBest framing for the meeting:\n\n“This is a working prototype/reference architecture with real D-Bus plugin projection, loopback-only Netmaker sidecars, Xray routing, and live GhostBridge accountability infrastructure. The hardened Netmaker control-plane pattern exists and is partially live, but the main Netmaker API service and final socket-to-Xray path still need tightening before I’d call it production-complete.”\n\nI would not send the deck unchanged as a strict factual claim. It is directionally real and interesting, but a few lines should be softened from “we already run this in production” to “we have this deployed as a prototype/hardened pattern and want engineering feedback.”","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T22:42:32.583Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_25mwiTOSfSbEnNd37w4nueI5","output":"Chunk ID: fbe3e9\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 2053\nOutput:\n# GhostBridge × Netmaker\n### Netmaker isn't a dependency in this project — it's core code.\n\n*A short read before we meet. Honestly: this is the first time anyone outside the\nproject will have seen it. We booked the trial/sales call because it was the door —\nbut what we actually want is for a sharp engineer on your side to look closely and\ntell us what you really think.*\n\n---\n\n## TL;DR (for the busy reader)\n\n- We've built a **zero-trust, compliance-grade AI control plane** — in Rust — that runs **on a Netmaker mesh** and treats it as the spine: the transport **and** the root of identity.\n- We deploy your control server in a pattern most of your customers don't: **no network interface at all** — loopback + unix sockets, fronted by Xray. A port scan returns nothing.\n- We already run Netmaker in production. We're not here for a standard enterprise eval — we're here because **you're already load-bearing in something we think is genuinely novel**, and you should see it.\n- **Why we're sending this:** not an ask. We already run this in production on what's available today — we just figured the people who built the layer it all stands on should be the first to see what got built on top of it.\n\n---\n\n## What GhostBridge is, in one paragraph\n\nGhostBridge turns a Netmaker mesh into a **trusted** backbone. Traffic flows through a hardened pipeline — decoy ingress, identity sled, Xray header injection, a per-hop interceptor — where every request is classified, routed, gated against machine-readable policy (OSCAL), and recorded into a **tamper-evident hash-linked chain**. An AI layer reasons over that verified history but **cannot execute anything itself**. Same codebase ships as a **privacy** edition or a **compliance** edition — one config flag decides which world you're in.\n\n---\n\n## How it works — one governance pattern, every layer\n\nThe whole system runs on a single discipline: **make the wrong thing impossible first; gate what's left; record everything.** Here it is top to bottom.\n\n```\n  RUST          the compiler is the first enforcer — invalid code won't build\n    ▼\n  SCHEMA        invalid STATE is unrepresentable — the silent gate, before any rule runs\n    ▼\n  TRAFFIC COP   Gemma classifies (what is this?) + Xray routes (where does it go?)\n  (Gemma+Xray)  — directs traffic, reports every decision up. Directs, never authorizes.\n    ▼\n  ZEROCLAW      routes to the right MODEL by cost / reasoning / specialty —\n                schema-native from the ground up, so it can't route off-policy\n    ▼\n  A.N.N.A.      OSCAL-gated approval at EVERY hop (HMAC-stamped identity header)\n                — the higher-up that actually says yes/no\n    ▼\n  CHAIN         hash-linked, tamper-evident evidence. Every action becomes a block.\n    ▼\n  THE LOOP      AI reassembles the chain into a semantic DB (Qdrant) + realtime graph\n                (Cozo), reasons over it, recommends/acts-by-delegation → new blocks\n```\n\n**The same idea at three scales:** Rust says *code can't be wrong*, schema says *state can't be invalid*, A.N.N.A. says *action can't be unauthorized* — and the chain says *and it's all on the record.*\n\n---\n\n## Four things that make this different\n\n**1. The AI is a brain with no hands.**\nThe chatbot is a **delegator, recommender, and fixer** — and that's the ceiling. **No internet access, no execution rights, no execution control.** It proposes into a schema-shaped mold; a separate, OSCAL-gated, chained layer disposes. A confabulating or compromised model can't do damage — the worst case is a rejected recommendation. Autonomous *reasoning* without autonomous *risk*.\n\n**2. You can cross-examine it.**\nBecause every action is a chained, content-addressed, searchable block, you can confront the agent in real time — *\"why did you do this?\"* — and it answers with **cryptographic receipts** pulled live by semantic search (chatbot on top, evidence on the bottom). If the model confabulates, the evidence pane contradicts it. **An AI you can put on the stand.**\n\n**3. The chain is the truth; the DB and graph are rebuilt views.**\nThe hash-linked chain is canonical and tamper-evident. Qdrant (semantic) and Cozo (realtime graph) are **AI-reassembled projections** of it — if they're lost or corrupted, you re-derive them from the chain. Trust lives in the chain; queryability lives in the projections. (It's a blockchain *by structure* — hashed, chained blocks — kept honest by **anchoring**, not consensus, which is the right call for a single-operator compliance system.)\n\n**4. One dial: Snowden ↔ Big Brother.**\nSame mesh, same chain, same confrontable AI — **only the identity-linkage layer changes**, at deploy time:\n- **Privacy edition (Snowden):** key *is* identity, no PII, de-anonymization **cryptographically impossible**.\n- **Compliance edition (Big Brother):** every actor attributable, de-anon **only on a signed OSCAL authority — which is itself a chained, confrontable block.** You can cross-examine the watchers.\n\n---\n\n## The Netmaker hardening pattern (the part we want to show you)\n\nYour control server runs with **no NIC**:\n- `netmaker`, `netmaker-mq` (Mosquitto), `netmaker-ui` → loopback only.\n- Exposed to the host as **unix sockets** (`/run/netmaker/api.sock`, `mq.sock`, `mqtts.sock`, `ui.sock`) via Incus proxy devices.\n- `wg-xray` + Xray terminate TLS and route by SNI to those sockets.\n\n**There is no open port on the Netmaker server.** The attack surface is a socket file behind the WireGuard + identity gate. We'd love to publish this jointly as a reference architecture for your security-conscious users.\n\n---\n\n## Why Netmaker is core, not a dependency\n\n- It's a **first-class state plugin** — managed by the same engine that runs the whole platform.\n- Its peers **are the identity model**: `session_id = Argon2(PSK, salt = WG_pubkey)`, rooted in the WireGuard pre-shared key you already manage. Remove Netmaker and the identity layer has no root. It is **link #0 of the evidence chain.**\n- **Every GhostBridge deployment is a hardened Netmaker deployment**, sold into regulated rooms Netmaker alone doesn't reach yet. We expand your surface; you anchor our spine.\n\n---\n\n## What we're actually after\n\nPlainly: **we want a knowledgeable human to look closely and react.** This is the first outside set of eyes on the project, and your team is the right first audience — because you built the layer it all stands on.\n\nWe're not asking for anything. We already run this in production on what's available today. We just figured the people who built the layer it all stands on should be the first to see what got built on top of it.\n\nSo in the meeting: if any of it is interesting, we'll happily go deeper. If not — no harm, no homework. Be the first humans to see this, and tell us if it's as interesting as we think it is.\n\n---\n\n## Close\n\n> Netmaker connects the machines.\n> GhostBridge proves *who* they are and *that policy was enforced* — every hop, auditor-grade, in an AI loop you can cross-examine.\n>\n> You're already in the core of what we built. We'd just like you to be the first to *see* it — and tell us, straight, what you think.\n\n---\n\n### Appendix — quick FAQ\n\n- **\"Is it really a blockchain if it's not distributed?\"** It's a blockchain *by structure* (hashed, chained blocks). Distribution buys trustless multi-party consensus; we don't need that — we get operator-tamper-resistance by **anchoring** the chain head externally. Correct tool for a single-operator compliance ledger.\n- **\"What stops the AI going rogue?\"** It has no hands — no internet, no execution rights. It recommends; the governed layer executes. Hallucination has no reach.\n- **\"Why Rust / why these components?\"** Selection principle: **schema-native from the ground up** (e.g. zeroclaw) and **safe by construction** (Rust — memory-safe, race-free, single static binaries). The governance holds at every layer because nothing was bolted on.\n- **\"What do you actually want from us?\"** Nothing, really — this is a heads-up, not a request. We already run it on what's available. We just wanted the people who built the layer it stands on to be the first to see it.\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T22:44:13.115Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_x1eUZnlmsISqkqNcCrJaKUeQ","output":"Chunk ID: 0a496d\nWall time: 0.0002 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 2098\nOutput:\n# GhostBridge × Netmaker\n### Netmaker isn't a dependency in this project — it's core code.\n\n*A short read before we meet. Honestly: this is the first time anyone outside the\nproject will have seen it. We booked the trial/sales call because it was the door —\nbut what we actually want is for a sharp engineer on your side to look closely and\ntell us what you really think.*\n\n---\n\n## TL;DR (for the busy reader)\n\n- We've built a **zero-trust, compliance-grade AI control plane** — in Rust — that runs **on a Netmaker mesh** and treats it as the spine: the transport **and** the root of identity.\n- We deploy your control server in a pattern most of your customers don't: **no network interface at all** — loopback + unix sockets, fronted by Xray. A port scan returns nothing.\n- We already use Netmaker as load-bearing design infrastructure. We're not here for a standard enterprise eval — we're here because **you're at the root of something we think is genuinely novel**, and you should see it early.\n- **Why we're sending this:** not an ask. This is an implemented, technically grounded reference architecture built around what exists today — we figured the people who built the layer it all stands on should be the first to see what got built on top of it.\n\n---\n\n## What GhostBridge is, in one paragraph\n\nGhostBridge turns a Netmaker mesh into a **trusted** backbone. Traffic flows through a hardened pipeline — decoy ingress, identity sled, Xray header injection, a per-hop interceptor — where every request is classified, routed, gated against machine-readable policy (OSCAL), and recorded into a **tamper-evident hash-linked chain**. An AI layer reasons over that verified history but **cannot execute anything itself**. Same codebase ships as a **privacy** edition or a **compliance** edition — one config flag decides which world you're in.\n\n---\n\n## How it works — one governance pattern, every layer\n\nThe whole system runs on a single discipline: **make the wrong thing impossible first; gate what's left; record everything.** Here it is top to bottom.\n\n```\n  RUST          the compiler is the first enforcer — invalid code won't build\n    ▼\n  SCHEMA        invalid STATE is unrepresentable — the silent gate, before any rule runs\n    ▼\n  TRAFFIC COP   Gemma classifies (what is this?) + Xray routes (where does it go?)\n  (Gemma+Xray)  — directs traffic, reports every decision up. Directs, never authorizes.\n    ▼\n  ZEROCLAW      routes to the right MODEL by cost / reasoning / specialty —\n                schema-native from the ground up, so it can't route off-policy\n    ▼\n  A.N.N.A.      OSCAL-gated approval at EVERY hop (HMAC-stamped identity header)\n                — the higher-up that actually says yes/no\n    ▼\n  CHAIN         hash-linked, tamper-evident evidence. Every action becomes a block.\n    ▼\n  THE LOOP      AI reassembles the chain into a semantic DB (Qdrant) + realtime graph\n                (Cozo), reasons over it, recommends/acts-by-delegation → new blocks\n```\n\n**The same idea at three scales:** Rust says *code can't be wrong*, schema says *state can't be invalid*, A.N.N.A. says *action can't be unauthorized* — and the chain says *and it's all on the record.*\n\n---\n\n## Four things that make this different\n\n**1. The AI is a brain with no hands.**\nThe chatbot is a **delegator, recommender, and fixer** — and that's the ceiling. **No internet access, no execution rights, no execution control.** It proposes into a schema-shaped mold; a separate, OSCAL-gated, chained layer disposes. A confabulating or compromised model can't do damage — the worst case is a rejected recommendation. Autonomous *reasoning* without autonomous *risk*.\n\n**2. You can cross-examine it.**\nBecause every action is a chained, content-addressed, searchable block, you can confront the agent in real time — *\"why did you do this?\"* — and it answers with **cryptographic receipts** pulled live by semantic search (chatbot on top, evidence on the bottom). If the model confabulates, the evidence pane contradicts it. **An AI you can put on the stand.**\n\n**3. The chain is the truth; the DB and graph are rebuilt views.**\nThe hash-linked chain is canonical and tamper-evident. Qdrant (semantic) and Cozo (realtime graph) are **AI-reassembled projections** of it — if they're lost or corrupted, you re-derive them from the chain. Trust lives in the chain; queryability lives in the projections. (It's a blockchain *by structure* — hashed, chained blocks — kept honest by **anchoring**, not consensus, which is the right call for a single-operator compliance system.)\n\n**4. One dial: Snowden ↔ Big Brother.**\nSame mesh, same chain, same confrontable AI — **only the identity-linkage layer changes**, at deploy time:\n- **Privacy edition (Snowden):** key *is* identity, no PII, de-anonymization **cryptographically impossible**.\n- **Compliance edition (Big Brother):** every actor attributable, de-anon **only on a signed OSCAL authority — which is itself a chained, confrontable block.** You can cross-examine the watchers.\n\n---\n\n## The Netmaker hardening pattern (the part we want to show you)\n\nThe hardening pattern is: run the control server with **no NIC**:\n- `netmaker`, `netmaker-mq` (Mosquitto), `netmaker-ui` → loopback only.\n- Exposed to the host as **unix sockets** (`/run/netmaker/api.sock`, `mq.sock`, `mqtts.sock`, `ui.sock`) via Incus proxy devices.\n- `wg-xray` + Xray terminate TLS and route by SNI to those sockets.\n\nThe target posture is **no open port on the Netmaker server**: the attack surface becomes a socket file behind the WireGuard + identity gate. We'd love to publish this jointly as a reference architecture for your security-conscious users.\n\n---\n\n## Why Netmaker is core, not a dependency\n\n- It's a **first-class state plugin** — managed by the same engine that runs the whole platform.\n- Its peers **are the identity model**: `session_id = Argon2(PSK, salt = WG_pubkey)`, rooted in the WireGuard pre-shared key you already manage. Remove Netmaker and the identity layer has no root. It is **link #0 of the evidence chain.**\n- **Every GhostBridge deployment wants to be a hardened Netmaker deployment**, sold into regulated rooms Netmaker alone doesn't reach yet. We expand your surface; you anchor our spine.\n\n---\n\n## What we're actually after\n\nPlainly: **we want a knowledgeable human to look closely and react.** This is the first outside set of eyes on the project, and your team is the right first audience — because you built the layer it all stands on.\n\nWe're not asking for anything. The architecture is implemented far enough to be worth a serious engineering reaction, and it is built on what's available today. We just figured the people who built the layer it all stands on should be the first to see what got built on top of it.\n\nSo in the meeting: if any of it is interesting, we'll happily go deeper. If not — no harm, no homework. Be the first humans to see this, and tell us if it's as interesting as we think it is.\n\n---\n\n## Close\n\n> Netmaker connects the machines.\n> GhostBridge proves *who* they are and *that policy was enforced* — every hop, auditor-grade, in an AI loop you can cross-examine.\n>\n> You're already in the core of what we built. We'd just like you to be the first to *see* it — and tell us, straight, what you think.\n\n---\n\n### Appendix — quick FAQ\n\n- **\"Is it really a blockchain if it's not distributed?\"** It's a blockchain *by structure* (hashed, chained blocks). Distribution buys trustless multi-party consensus; we don't need that — we get operator-tamper-resistance by **anchoring** the chain head externally. Correct tool for a single-operator compliance ledger.\n- **\"What stops the AI going rogue?\"** It has no hands — no internet, no execution rights. It recommends; the governed layer executes. Hallucination has no reach.\n- **\"Why Rust / why these components?\"** Selection principle: **schema-native from the ground up** (e.g. zeroclaw) and **safe by construction** (Rust — memory-safe, race-free, single static binaries). The governance holds at every layer because nothing was bolted on.\n- **\"What do you actually want from us?\"** Nothing, really — this is a heads-up, not a request. We built the pattern around what's available today and want the people who built the layer it stands on to be the first to see it.\n"}}

Traffic moves through decoy ingress, identity sled, Xray header injection, a per-hop interceptor, schema validation, OSCAL policy gates, and a tamper-evident Snowball ledger.</p>\n+        <p>An AI layer reasons over verified history, but <strong>it has no hands</strong>: no execution rights, no direct control, and no ability to bypass the governed layer. Scribe and the Compliance Engine decide what is allowed to become real state.</p>\n+      </section>\n+\n+      <section class=\"section\">\n+        <p class=\"eyebrow\">Why This Is Different</p>\n+        <div class=\"grid g2\">\n+          <div class=\"card\">\n+            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> AI you can cross-examine</h3>\n+            <p>Chatbot on top, Qdrant evidence on the bottom. }\n    .g2, .g3 { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }\n    .row { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 5px; }\n  }\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n  <main class=\"page\">\n    <article class=\"shell\">\n      <header class=\"hero\">\n        <p class=\"eyebrow\">GhostBridge x Netmaker</p>\n        <h1>Netmaker is not a dependency.<br><span class=\"gradient\">It is core code.</span></h1>\n        <p class=\"lead\">We built a zero-trust, compliance-grade AI control plane in Rust, and Netmaker is the spine: transport, identity root, and link zero of the evidence chain.</p>\n        <p class=\"note\">This is the first time anyone outside the project will have seen it. The meeting started as a trial/sales call, but the real point is simpler: we want a sharp Netmaker engineer to look closely and tell us what you think.</p>\n        <div class=\"chips\">\n          <span class=\"chip\">Rust control plane</span>\n          <span class=\"chip\">Netmaker identity spine</span>\n          <span class=\"chip\">No-NIC hardening pattern</span>\n          <span class=\"chip\">OSCAL-gated actions</span>\n          <span class=\"chip\">Confrontable AI</span>\n        </div>\n        <div class=\"subject\">\n          Suggested subject line: <code>First human eyes: GhostBridge built on Netmaker</code>\n        </div>\n      </header>\n\n      <section class=\"section\">\n        <p class=\"eyebrow\">The One Paragraph</p>\n        <h2>A mesh you can trust, not just connect</h2>\n        <p>GhostBridge turns a Netmaker mesh into a trusted backbone. Traffic moves through decoy ingress, identity sled, Xray header injection, a per-hop interceptor, schema validation, OSCAL policy gates, and a tamper-evident Snowball ledger.</p>\n        <p>An AI layer reasons over verified history, but <strong>it has no hands</strong>: no execution rights, no direct control, and no ability to bypass the governed layer. It recommends into schema. A.N.N.A. Scribe and the Compliance Engine decide what is allowed to become real state.</p>\n      </section>\n\n      <section class=\"section\">\n        <p class=\"eyebrow\">Why This Is Different</p>\n        <div class=\"grid g2\">\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> AI you can cross-examine</h3>\n            <p>Chatbot on top, Qdrant evidence on the bottom. Ask why something happened and the system answers with semantic receipts from the chain.</p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> Chain is truth</h3>\n            <p>Qdrant and Cozo are rebuildable projections. The canonical record is the hash-linked Snowball ledger, not the search database.</p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> Model has no hands</h3>\n            <p>The AI can reason, delegate, and recommend. It cannot directly execute. Hallucination becomes a rejected recommendation, not an incident.</p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> One privacy dial</h3>\n            <p>Same mesh and chain can run privacy-first or compliance-first. The identity-linkage layer changes, not the whole architecture.</p>\n          </div>\n        </div>\n      </section>\n\n      <section class=\"section\">\n        <p class=\"eyebrow\">Governance Stack</p>\n        <h2>Make the wrong thing impossible first</h2>\n        <div class=\"stack\">\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">Rust</span><span>The compiler is the first enforcer: invalid code should not build.</span></div>\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">Schema</span><span>Invalid state is unrepresentable. In this system, plugin is schema; without validated schema, the object does not exist.</span></div>\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">Gemma + Xray</span><span>Classify and route traffic. They direct; they do not authorize.</span></div>\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">ZeroClaw</span><span>Route to the right model by cost, reasoning depth, specialty, and policy.</span></div>\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">A.N.N.A.</span><span>A.N.N.A. Scribe notarizes identity and Snowball session state. The Law Firm gates policy.</span></div>\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">Chain</span><span>Every accepted action becomes a hash-linked, tamper-evident block.</span></div>\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">The Loop</span><span>AI rebuilds semantic and graph projections from the chain, reasons over them, and produces the next governed recommendation.</span></div>\n        </div>\n      </section>\n\n      <section class=\"section\">\n        <p class=\"eyebrow\">Netmaker Hardening Pattern</p>\n        <h2>The part we want Netmaker to see</h2>\n        <div class=\"callout\">\n          <p>The reference pattern is a Netmaker control plane with no exposed service port: loopback-only services, Incus proxy devices, Unix sockets under <strong>/run/netmaker</strong>, and Xray routing by SNI behind WireGuard identity.</p>\n        </div>\n        <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:16px\">\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> No NIC posture</h3>\n            <p><strong>netmaker</strong>, <strong>netmaker-mq</strong>, and <strong>netmaker-ui</strong> are treated as loopback/socket services, not public daemons.</p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> Sockets not ports</h3>\n            <p>The attack surface moves to socket files such as <strong>/run/netmaker/api.sock</strong> and <strong>ui.sock</strong>, behind the identity gate.</p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> Xray routing</h3>\n            <p><strong>wg-xray</strong> terminates and routes traffic by domain to the correct internal socket-backed service.</p>\n          </div>\n        </div>\n      </section>\n\n      <section class=\"section\">\n        <p class=\"eyebrow\">Why Netmaker Is Core</p>\n        <h2>You are at the root of the identity story</h2>\n        <ul>\n          <li>Netmaker is represented as a first-class state plugin, not a bolt-on integration.</li>\n          <li>WireGuard peers are the identity root: <strong>session_id = Argon2(PSK, salt = WG_pubkey)</strong>.</li>\n          <li>Remove Netmaker and the identity layer loses link zero of the evidence chain.</li>\n          <li>GhostBridge turns hardened Netmaker deployments into a regulated-room story: privacy, compliance, accountability, and AI evidence.</li>\n        </ul>\n      </section>\n\n      <section class=\"section\">\n        <p class=\"eyebrow\">What We Want</p>\n        <h2>Not a pitch. A first look.</h2>\n        <p>We are not asking for a purchase decision, a partnership commitment, or homework. We want a knowledgeable human at Netmaker to see what has been built on top of your layer and react like an engineer.</p>\n        <p>The architecture is implemented far enough to deserve that reaction. Some edges are still being hardened, but the core idea is real and implementable with what exists today.</p>\n      </section>\n\n      <section class=\"section\">\n        <p class=\"quote\">Netmaker connects the machines. GhostBridge proves who they are and that policy was enforced, every hop, auditor-grade, in an AI loop you can cross-examine.</p>\n        <p class=\"small\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">Confidential pre-meeting brief. }\n    .g2, .g3 { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }\n    .row { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 5px; }\n  }\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n  <main class=\"page\">\n    <article class=\"shell\">\n      <header class=\"hero\">\n        <p class=\"eyebrow\">GhostBridge x Netmaker</p>\n        <h1>Netmaker is not a dependency.<br><span class=\"gradient\">It is core code.</span></h1>\n        <p class=\"lead\">We built a zero-trust, compliance-grade AI control plane in Rust, and Netmaker is the spine: transport, identity root, and link zero of the evidence chain.</p>\n        <p class=\"note\">This is the first time anyone outside the project will have seen it. The meeting started as a trial/sales call, but the real point is simpler: we want a sharp Netmaker engineer to look closely and tell us what you think.</p>\n        <div class=\"chips\">\n          <span class=\"chip\">Rust control plane</span>\n          <span class=\"chip\">Netmaker identity spine</span>\n          <span class=\"chip\">No-NIC hardening pattern</span>\n          <span class=\"chip\">OSCAL-gated actions</span>\n          <span class=\"chip\">Confrontable AI</span>\n        </div>\n        <div class=\"subject\">\n          Suggested subject line: <code>First human eyes: GhostBridge built on Netmaker</code>\n        </div>\n      </header>\n\n      <section class=\"section\">\n        <p class=\"eyebrow\">The One Paragraph</p>\n        <h2>A mesh you can trust, not just connect</h2>\n        <p>GhostBridge turns a Netmaker mesh into a trusted backbone. Traffic moves through decoy ingress, identity sled, Xray header injection, a per-hop interceptor, schema validation, OSCAL policy gates, and a tamper-evident Snowball ledger.</p>\n        <p>An AI layer reasons over verified history, but <strong>it has no hands</strong>: no execution rights, no direct control, and no ability to bypass the governed layer. It recommends into schema. A.N.N.A. Scribe and the Compliance Engine decide what is allowed to become real state.</p>\n      </section>\n\n      <section class=\"section\">\n        <p class=\"eyebrow\">Why This Is Different</p>\n        <div class=\"grid g2\">\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> AI you can cross-examine</h3>\n            <p>Chatbot on top, Qdrant evidence on the bottom. Ask why something happened and the system answers with semantic receipts from the chain.</p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> Chain is truth</h3>\n            <p>Qdrant and Cozo are rebuildable projections. The canonical record is the hash-linked Snowball ledger, not the search database.</p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> Model has no hands</h3>\n            <p>The AI can reason, delegate, and recommend. It cannot directly execute. Hallucination becomes a rejected recommendation, not an incident.</p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> One privacy dial</h3>\n            <p>Same mesh and chain can run privacy-first or compliance-first. The identity-linkage layer changes, not the whole architecture.</p>\n          </div>\n        </div>\n      </section>\n\n      <section class=\"section\">\n        <p class=\"eyebrow\">Governance Stack</p>\n        <h2>Make the wrong thing impossible first</h2>\n        <div class=\"stack\">\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">Rust</span><span>The compiler is the first enforcer: invalid code should not build.</span></div>\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">Schema</span><span>Invalid state is unrepresentable. In this system, plugin is schema; without validated schema, the object does not exist.</span></div>\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">Gemma + Xray</span><span>Classify and route traffic. They direct; they do not authorize.</span></div>\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">ZeroClaw</span><span>Route to the right model by cost, reasoning depth, specialty, and policy.</span></div>\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">A.N.N.A.</span><span>A.N.N.A. Scribe notarizes identity and Snowball session state. The Law Firm gates policy.</span></div>\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">Chain</span><span>Every accepted action becomes a hash-linked, tamper-evident block.</span></div>\n          <div class=\"row\"><span class=\"label\">The Loop</span><span>AI rebuilds semantic and graph projections from the chain, reasons over them, and produces the next governed recommendation.</span></div>\n        </div>\n      </section>\n\n      <section class=\"section\">\n        <p class=\"eyebrow\">Netmaker Hardening Pattern</p>\n        <h2>The part we want Netmaker to see</h2>\n        <div class=\"callout\">\n          <p>The reference pattern is a Netmaker control plane with no exposed service port: loopback-only services, Incus proxy devices, Unix sockets under <strong>/run/netmaker</strong>, and Xray routing by SNI behind WireGuard identity.</p>\n        </div>\n        <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:16px\">\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> No NIC posture</h3>\n            <p><strong>netmaker</strong>, <strong>netmaker-mq</strong>, and <strong>netmaker-ui</strong> are treated as loopback/socket services, not public daemons.</p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> Sockets not ports</h3>\n            <p>The attack surface moves to socket files such as <strong>/run/netmaker/api.sock</strong> and <strong>ui.sock</strong>, behind the identity gate.</p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"card\">\n            <h3><span class=\"mark\"></span> Xray routing</h3>\n            <p><strong>wg-xray</strong> terminates and routes traffic by domain to the correct internal socket-backed service.</p>\n          </div>\n        </div>\n"}}

This is the bottom pane when you cross-examine the agent, and the raw material the loop reasons over.</p>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:14px\">\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Embed</h3><p><span class=\"mono\">voyage-code-3</span> turns each chunk of the chain (actions, configs, docs, transcripts) into a high-dimensional vector. Code-aware, so it understands infra, not just prose.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Store &amp; search</h3><p>Vectors land in <span class=\"mono\">Qdrant</span>, keyed <span class=\"mono\">notebook:source:chunk</span>. The AI uses both — meaning to reason, provenance to prove.</p>\n</div></section>\n\n<!-- FOUR DIFFERENTIATORS -->\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow\">Why it's different</div>\n  <h2>Four things nobody else can credibly claim</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g2\" style=\"margin-top:14px\">\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>A brain with no hands</h3><p>The AI is a <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">delegator, recommender, fixer</b> — and that's the ceiling. <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">No internet, no execution rights, no execution control.</b> It proposes into a schema-shaped mold; a separate, OSCAL-gated, chained layer disposes. A compromised model can't do damage — worst case is a rejected suggestion.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>You can cross-examine it</h3><p>Every action is a chained, searchable block. Confront the agent in real time — <span class=\"mono kv\">\"why did you do this?\"</span> — and it answers with cryptographic receipts pulled live by semantic search. If the model confabulates, the evidence pane contradicts it. <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">An AI you can put on the stand.</b></p></div>\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>The chain is the truth</h3><p>The hash-linked chain is canonical and tamper-evident. Qdrant + Cozo are <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">AI-rebuilt projections</b> of it — lose them, re-derive them. It's a blockchain <i>by structure</i>, kept honest by <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">anchoring</b>, not consensus — the right call for a single-operator compliance ledger.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Schema-native, all the way down</h3><p>Components were <b style=\"color:var(--ink)\">chosen because they're schema-based from the ground up</b> (e.g. zeroclaw), and the code is safe by construction (Rust — memory-safe, race-free, single static binaries). Governance holds at every layer because nothing was bolted on.</p></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<!-- THE DIAL -->\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow\">One dial</div>\n Sending the full system context now; I will answer questions in the meeting tomorrow.</p>\n+  </div>\n+</section>\n+\n+<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n+  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">System thesis</div>\n+  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">A mesh is more than transport when it becomes the root of evidence.</h2>\n+  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">GhostBridge treats Netmaker/WireGuard identity as link zero. Every governed action carries identity, mutation, schema, policy authority, trace, footprint, and semantic meaning. AI can reason over the evidence, but only the governed layer can mutate state.</p>\n+  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:20px\">\n+    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Transport</h3><p>Netmaker mesh carries the trusted path. Xray routes by SNI and injects identity/accountability headers.</p></div>\n+    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Identity</h3><p>WireGuard peer material anchors <span class=\"mono kv\">session_id = Argon2(PSK, salt = WG_pubkey)</span>.</p></div>\n+    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Evidence</h3><p>The Snowball ledger records accepted actions as hash-linked blocks with semantic projections.</p></div>\n+  </div>\n+</div></section>\n+\n+<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n+  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Core runtime architecture</div>\n+  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">One control plane. One schema truth. Multiple transport surfaces.</h2>\n+  <div class=\"table reveal d2\">\n+    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">D-Bus projection</div><div class=\"td\">Live authority is <span class=\"mono kv\">org.opdbus.projection</span>; plugin objects publish under <span class=\"mono kv\">/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/&lt;name&gt;</span>.</div></div>\n+    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">PluginSchema</div><div class=\"td\">Plugin is schema. If a validated schema/object is missing, the thing does not exist in the system.</div></div>\n+    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Sled</div><div class=\"td\">1:1 shared-memory layout for identity/state projection; schema-guided direct read/write semantics.</div></div>\n+    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Shuttle</div><div class=\"td\">Rust bridge/courier between D-Bus, gRPC, vector search, state projection, and UI surfaces.</div></div>\n+    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Snowball</div><div class=\"td\">Append-only session ledger. Each accepted action extends evidence rather than overwriting history.</div></div>\n+    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Strike / Etch</div><div class=\"td\">Hash generation and footprint binding for blocks, traces, and payloads.</div></div>\n+    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC / UDS</div><div class=\"td\">Internal service RPC over Unix sockets or controlled bridge paths; D-Bus remains authority, gRPC is transport.</div></div>\n+  </div>\n+</div></section>\n+\n+<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n+  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Technology stack map</div>\n+  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">What is in the stack</h2>\n+  <div class=\"grid g4\" style=\"margin-top:20px\">\n+    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Mesh</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>Netmaker</li><li>WireGuard</li><li>PSK identity root</li><li>peer/session binding</li></ul></div>\n+    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Network</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>Xray</li><li>SNI routing</li><li>Open vSwitch</li><li>OpenFlow</li><li>Incus proxy sockets</li></ul></div>\n+    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Control</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>D-Bus projection</li><li>PluginSchema</li><li>SchemaEngine</li><li>/dev/shm Sled</li><li>Rust crates</li></ul></div>\n+    <div class=\"card reveal d3\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>AI evidence</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>cognitive-mcp</li><li>ZeroClaw</li><li>Gemma routing</li><li>Voyage vectors</li><li>Qdrant</li><li>Cozo</li></ul></div>\n+  </div>\n+</div></section>\n+\n+<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n+  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Netmaker hardening pattern</div>\n+  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Control services become socket-backed, identity-gated surfaces.</h2>\n+  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">The pattern treats <span class=\"mono\">netmaker</span>, <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-mq</span>, and <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-ui</span> as loopback/socket services. Incus exposes Unix sockets under <span class=\"mono kv\">/run/netmaker</span>. Xray terminates and routes by SNI behind WireGuard identity. The intended public posture is no direct Netmaker service port.</p>\n+  <div class=\"svgwrap reveal d2\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n+    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 980 260\" width=\"100%\" aria-label=\"No Every governed action carries identity, mutation, schema, policy authority, trace, footprint, and semantic meaning. AI can reason over the evidence, but only the governed layer can mutate state.</p>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:20px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Transport</h3><p>Netmaker mesh carries the trusted path. One schema truth. {"timestamp":"2026-06-14T23:29:42.024Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"`UDS` means **Unix Domain Socket**.\n\nIt is a socket file on the same machine, used for local inter-process communication instead of TCP/IP networking.\n\nExample:\n\n```text\n/run/netmaker/api.sock\n/run/op-dbus/session-bus.sock\n/var/lib/ovs/db.sock\n```\n\nWhy it matters here:\n\n- No open network port is required.\n- Access can be controlled with filesystem permissions.\n- Services can talk locally without exposing TCP.\n- It fits the no-NIC / loopback-only hardening story.\n\nSo when I say `gRPC/UDS`, I mean **gRPC running over Unix socket files instead of a network port**.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-14T23:29:42.028Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"`UDS` means **Unix Domain Socket**.\n\nIt is a socket file on the same machine, used for local inter-process communication instead of TCP/IP networking.\n\nExample:\n\n```text\n/run/netmaker/api.sock\n/run/op-dbus/session-bus.sock\n/var/lib/ovs/db.sock\n```\n\nWhy it matters here:\n\n- No open network port is required.\n- Access can be controlled with filesystem permissions.\n- Services can talk locally without exposing TCP.\n- It fits the no-NIC / loopback-only hardening story.\n\nSo when I say `gRPC/UDS`, I mean **gRPC running over Unix socket files instead of a network port**."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

class=\"scan\"></div>\n\n<section>\n  <div class=\"wrap\">\n    <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">GhostBridge x Netmaker</div>\n    <h1 class=\"reveal d1\">Full technical use case deck.</h1>\n    <p class=\"lead reveal d2\">Netmaker is the mesh and identity backbone of GhostBridge: a Rust platform-as-a-service control plane for governed AI, schema-authored state, no-NIC service hardening, semantic evidence, and tamper-evident accountability.</p>\n    <div class=\"chips reveal d3\">\n      <span class=\"chip\">Netmaker</span><span class=\"chip\">WireGuard</span><span class=\"chip\">D-Bus</span><span class=\"chip\">PluginSchema</span><span class=\"chip\">Xray</span><span class=\"chip\">Incus</span><span class=\"chip\">Open vSwitch</span><span class=\"chip\">gRPC/UDS</span><span class=\"chip\">Qdrant</span><span class=\"chip\">Cozo</span><span class=\"chip\">Voyage</span><span class=\"chip\">OSCAL</span>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"muted reveal d3\" style=\"max-width:850px\">First human eyes outside the project. Sending the full system context now; I will answer questions in the meeting tomorrow.</p>\n  </div>\n</section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">System thesis</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">A mesh is more than transport when it becomes the root of evidence.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">GhostBridge treats Netmaker/WireGuard identity as link zero. Every governed action carries identity, mutation, schema, policy authority, trace, footprint, and semantic meaning. AI can reason over the evidence, but only the governed layer can mutate state.</p>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:20px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Transport</h3><p>Netmaker mesh carries the trusted path. Xray routes by SNI and injects identity/accountability headers.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Identity</h3><p>WireGuard peer material anchors <span class=\"mono kv\">session_id = Argon2(PSK, salt = WG_pubkey)</span>.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Evidence</h3><p>The Snowball ledger records accepted actions as hash-linked blocks with semantic projections.</p></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Core runtime architecture</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">One control plane. One schema truth. Multiple transport surfaces.</h2>\n  <div class=\"table reveal d2\">\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">D-Bus projection</div><div class=\"td\">Live authority is <span class=\"mono kv\">org.opdbus.projection</span>; plugin objects publish under <span class=\"mono kv\">/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/&lt;name&gt;</span>.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">PluginSchema</div><div class=\"td\">Plugin is schema. If a validated schema/object is missing, the thing does not exist in the system.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Sled</div><div class=\"td\">1:1 shared-memory layout for identity/state projection; schema-guided direct read/write semantics.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Shuttle</div><div class=\"td\">Rust bridge/courier between D-Bus, gRPC, vector search, state projection, and UI surfaces.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Snowball</div><div class=\"td\">Append-only session ledger. Each accepted action extends evidence rather than overwriting history.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Strike / Etch</div><div class=\"td\">Hash generation and footprint binding for blocks, traces, and payloads.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC / UDS</div><div class=\"td\">Internal service RPC over Unix sockets or controlled bridge paths; D-Bus remains authority, gRPC is transport.</div></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Technology stack map</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">What is in the stack</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g4\" style=\"margin-top:20px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Mesh</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>Netmaker</li><li>WireGuard</li><li>PSK identity root</li><li>peer/session binding</li></ul></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Network</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>Xray</li><li>SNI routing</li><li>Open vSwitch</li><li>OpenFlow</li><li>Incus proxy sockets</li></ul></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Control</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>D-Bus projection</li><li>PluginSchema</li><li>SchemaEngine</li><li>/dev/shm Sled</li><li>Rust crates</li></ul></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d3\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>AI evidence</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>cognitive-mcp</li><li>ZeroClaw</li><li>Gemma routing</li><li>Voyage vectors</li><li>Qdrant</li><li>Cozo</li></ul></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Netmaker hardening pattern</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Control services become socket-backed, identity-gated surfaces.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">The pattern treats <span class=\"mono\">netmaker</span>, <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-mq</span>, and <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-ui</span> as loopback/socket services. Incus exposes Unix sockets under <span class=\"mono kv\">/run/netmaker</span>. Xray terminates and routes by SNI behind WireGuard identity. The intended public posture is no direct Netmaker service port.</p>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap reveal d2\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 980 260\" width=\"100%\" aria-label=\"No NIC socket-backed Netmaker pattern\">\n      <rect x=\"35\" y=\"54\" width=\"190\" height=\"148\" rx=\"16\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/>\n      <text x=\"130\" y=\"44\" fill=\"#a8b5cc\" font-size=\"12\" text-anchor=\"middle\">wg-xray · TLS/SNI</text>\n      <text x=\"130\" y=\"132\" fill=\"#21d4fd\" font-size=\"15\" text-anchor=\"middle\">Xray</text>\n      <g font-size=\"11\" fill=\"#a8b5cc\">mq.sock · mqtts.sock</text>\n        <rect x=\"330\" y=\"158\" width=\"210\" height=\"42\" rx=\"10\" fill=\"#0c0e15\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/><text x=\"435\" y=\"184\" stroke-width=\"1.7\" fill=\"none\" opacity=\".9\">\n        <line class=\"flow\" x1=\"225\" y1=\"128\" x2=\"328\" y2=\"63\"/><line class=\"flow\" x1=\"225\" y1=\"128\" x2=\"328\" y2=\"121\"/><line posture · Unix sockets · Incus proxy devices · Xray routing · WireGuard identity</text>\n    </svg>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Accountability loop</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Chatbot on top. Semantic evidence underneath.</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g2\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Header provenance</h3><p>Xray/OpenClaw metadata carries <span class=\"mono kv\">X-Ghostbridge-Footprint</span>, <span class=\"mono kv\">X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID</span>, or WireGuard pubkey identity.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Snowball block</h3><p>Accepted action becomes a hash-linked block with previous hash, event hash, trace id, footprint, subid, actor, and capability.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Semantic projection</h3><p>Voyage embeds blocks, docs, transcripts, and chat turns. Qdrant makes meaning searchable. Cozo tracks graph/realtime relationships.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Cross-examination</h3><p>The model explains. The evidence pane verifies. If the explanation drifts, semantic receipts contradict it.</p></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">AI and MCP surfaces</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">External clients enter through cognitive-mcp.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">cognitive-mcp is the universal external gateway for NotebookLM, Droid/factory.ai, Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI, and related clients. compact-mcp remains loopback/chatbot only. The gateway exposes memory, gRPC service, auth, tool surfaces, and context retrieval.</p>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>cognitive-mcp</h3><p>Universal MCP gateway, memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and protocol surface.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>ZeroClaw</h3><p>Routes to the right model/provider by cost, reasoning depth, policy, specialty, and structured output needs.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>NotebookLM path</h3><p>Notebook/imported context becomes source material for vectorization and semantic evidence, not an authority bypass.</p></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Schema and subid</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Every artifact has machine identity and human taxonomy.</h2>\n  <div class=\"table reveal d2\">\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">uuid</div><div class=\"td\">Machine identity. Exact, stable, never replaced by a subid.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">subid</div><div class=\"td\"><span class=\"mono kv\">&lt;category&gt;.&lt;component-type&gt;.&lt;subject&gt;.&lt;verb&gt;[.&lt;facet&gt;][@vN]</span></div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">categories</div><div class=\"td\"><span class=\"mono\">src · prj · sch · mut · obs · evt · exp</span></div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">mut.*</div><div class=\"td\">Write path records require actor_id and capability_id.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">evt.*</div><div class=\"td\">Event records require event_id or event_hash.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">OSCAL props</div><div class=\"td\">subid is stored as a prop value. Control refs and statement refs remain metadata arrays.</div></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">A.N.N.A. and the Law Firm</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Human roles as enforcement components.</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>A.N.N.A. Scribe</h3><p>Axon Network Notary Arbitrator. Notarizes WireGuard identity, session state, Snowball trace, footprint, and trace id.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Olivia Scal</h3><p>Managing Partner / OSCAL. Owns control mapping, profiles, and authority structure.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>E.U.gene Risk</h3><p>EU AI Act counsel. Maps model behavior, risk posture, and evidence requirements.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Penny Privacy</h3><p>GDPR/privacy counsel. Data minimization, identity linkage mode, privacy posture, and lawful basis.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Reggie O.P.A.</h3><p>Cloud prosecutor. OPA/policy enforcement and contradiction checks.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>semantic_vectors</h3><p>Separate plugin for Voyage/Qdrant config, vector schema, endpoint metadata, and revectorization policy.</p></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Vectorization</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Meaning is a projection, not the source of truth.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">The chain is canonical. Qdrant and Cozo are rebuildable projections. Voyage embeddings make evidence searchable by meaning; identity and mutation vectors prove exact provenance.</p>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Voyage</h3><p>Initial vector model target: <span class=\"mono kv\">voyage-4</span>, routed through MongoDB AI/Voyage when using <span class=\"mono\">al-*</span> keys.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Qdrant</h3><p>Semantic vector store for evidence search, trace lookup, transcript search, and chatbot confrontation.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Cozo</h3><p>Graph/realtime projection for relationships among sessions, traces, controls, actors, capabilities, and artifacts.</p></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Product surfaces</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">One engine, multiple editions.</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\" style=\"background:var(--green)\"></span>Privacy edition</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>key is identity</li><li>no PII linkage</li><li>journalist/source networks</li><li>at-risk community meshes</li><li>confidential rooms</li></ul></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\" style=\"background:var(--violet)\"></span>Compliance edition</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>attributable actors</li><li>signed authority</li><li>GDPR</li><li>NIS2</li><li>DORA</li><li>EU AI Act</li></ul></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\" style=\"background:var(--cyan)\"></span>Enterprise drop-in</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>Active Directory</li><li>databases</li><li>Slack</li><li>CMS</li><li>schema-backed deployment</li><li>governed mesh</li></ul></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">What Netmaker anchors</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Netmaker is load-bearing in the PaaS architecture.</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Mesh spine</h3><p>Private, governed connectivity across the platform and customer deployments.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Identity root</h3><p>WireGuard peer material binds sessions, traces, and actor/accountability records.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Hardening story</h3><p>No-NIC/socket-backed Netmaker control plane as a reference pattern for security-sensitive customers.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Regulated rooms</h3><p>GhostBridge packages Netmaker into privacy/compliance environments with evidence and policy.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>AI accountability</h3><p>The mesh identity becomes the anchor for confrontable AI evidence.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Future surface</h3><p>Every GhostBridge deployment wants to be a hardened Netmaker deployment.</p></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Tomorrow</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">No pre-work. Bring engineering questions.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">This deck is the full technical context for the meeting. I am not asking Netmaker to decide anything from the email. I am showing the use case, the platform architecture, and where Netmaker sits in the backbone. I will answer questions live tomorrow.</p>\n  <p class=\"quote reveal d3\" style=\"margin-top:28px\">Netmaker connects the machines. AI can reason over the evidence, but only the governed layer can mutate state. gRPC is the service plane that moves these contracts between Rust components over Unix sockets and controlled bridge paths.</p>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:20px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Transport</h3><p>Netmaker mesh carries the trusted path. If a validated schema/object is missing, the thing does not exist in the system.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Sled</div><div class=\"td\">1:1 shared-memory layout for identity/state projection; schema-guided direct read/write semantics.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Shuttle</div><div class=\"td\">Rust bridge/courier between D-Bus, gRPC, vector search, state projection, and UI surfaces.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Snowball</div><div class=\"td\">Append-only session ledger. Each accepted action extends evidence rather than overwriting history.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Strike / Etch</div><div class=\"td\">Hash generation and footprint binding for blocks, traces, and payloads.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC / UDS</div><div class=\"td\">Internal service RPC over Unix sockets or controlled bridge paths; Sending the full system context now; I will answer questions in the meeting tomorrow.</p>\n  </div>\n</section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">System thesis</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">A mesh is more than transport when it becomes the root of evidence.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">GhostBridge treats Netmaker/WireGuard identity as link zero. Multiple transport surfaces.</h2>\n  <div class=\"table reveal d2\">\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">D-Bus projection</div><div class=\"td\">Live authority is <span class=\"mono kv\">org.opdbus.projection</span>; plugin objects publish under <span class=\"mono kv\">/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/&lt;name&gt;</span>.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">PluginSchema</div><div class=\"td\">Plugin is schema. If a validated schema/object is missing, the thing does not exist in the system.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Sled</div><div class=\"td\">1:1 shared-memory layout for identity/state projection; schema-guided direct read/write semantics.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Shuttle</div><div class=\"td\">Rust bridge/courier between D-Bus, gRPC, vector search, state projection, and UI surfaces.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Snowball</div><div class=\"td\">Append-only session ledger. Each accepted action extends evidence rather than overwriting history.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Strike / Etch</div><div class=\"td\">Hash generation and footprint binding for blocks, traces, and payloads.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC / UDS</div><div class=\"td\">Internal service RPC over Unix sockets or controlled bridge paths; D-Bus remains authority, gRPC is transport.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC bridge</div><div class=\"td\">Service-to-service APIs, event-chain search, assistant surfaces, and internal contracts flow over gRPC when they are not directly D-Bus-bound.</div></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Technology stack map</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">What is in the stack</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g4\" style=\"margin-top:20px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Mesh</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>Netmaker</li><li>WireGuard</li><li>PSK identity root</li><li>peer/session binding</li></ul></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Network</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>Xray</li><li>SNI routing</li><li>Open vSwitch</li><li>OpenFlow</li><li>Incus proxy sockets</li><li>gRPC bridge</li></ul></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Control</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>D-Bus projection</li><li>PluginSchema</li><li>SchemaEngine</li><li>/dev/shm Sled</li><li>Rust crates</li></ul></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d3\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>AI evidence</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>cognitive-mcp</li><li>ZeroClaw</li><li>Gemma routing</li><li>Voyage vectors</li><li>Qdrant</li><li>Cozo</li></ul></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Netmaker hardening pattern</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Control services become socket-backed, identity-gated surfaces.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">The pattern treats <span class=\"mono\">netmaker</span>, <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-mq</span>, and <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-ui</span> as loopback/socket services. Every governed action carries identity, mutation, schema, policy authority, trace, footprint, and semantic meaning. AI can reason over the evidence, but only the governed layer can mutate state. gRPC is the service plane that moves these contracts between Rust components over Unix sockets and controlled bridge paths.</p>\n90:    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Transport</h3><p>Netmaker mesh carries the trusted path. One schema truth. Multiple transport surfaces.</h2>\n126:    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">PluginSchema</div><div class=\"td\">Plugin is schema. If a validated schema/object is missing, the thing does not exist in the system.</div></div>\n127:    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Sled</div><div class=\"td\">1:1 shared-memory layout for identity/state projection; schema-guided direct read/write semantics.</div></div>\n128:    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Shuttle</div><div class=\"td\">Rust bridge/courier between D-Bus, gRPC, vector search, state projection, and UI surfaces.</div></div>\n131:    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC / UDS</div><div class=\"td\">Internal service RPC over Unix sockets or controlled bridge paths; D-Bus remains authority, gRPC is transport.</div></div>\n132:    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC bridge</div><div class=\"td\">Service-to-service APIs, event-chain search, assistant surfaces, and internal contracts flow over gRPC when they are not directly D-Bus-bound.</div></div>\n138:  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Plugin is schema. A.N.N.A. notarizes the state.</h2>\n162:        <text x=\"209\" y=\"176\" fill=\"#21d4fd\" font-size=\"12\">schema is contract</text>\n163:        <text x=\"209\" y=\"193\" fill=\"#68758d\" font-size=\"10.5\">if it has no validated schema, it does not exist</text>\n172:        <text x=\"965\" y=\"193\" fill=\"#68758d\" font-size=\"10.5\">UI, MCP, gRPC, and operator tooling all derive from schema</text>\n174:      <text x=\"580\" y=\"232\" fill=\"#68758d\" font-size=\"11\" text-anchor=\"middle\">authority starts with the D-Bus object and the schema that defines it; everything else is a projection or transport</text>\n184:    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Network</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>Xray</li><li>SNI routing</li><li>Open vSwitch</li><li>OpenFlow</li><li>Incus proxy sockets</li><li>gRPC bridge</li></ul></div>\n186:    <div class=\"card reveal d3\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>AI evidence</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>cognitive-mcp</li><li>ZeroClaw</li><li>Gemma routing</li><li>Voyage vectors</li><li>Qdrant</li><li>Cozo</li></ul></div>\n193:  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">The pattern treats <span class=\"mono\">netmaker</span>, <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-mq</span>, and <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-ui</span> as loopback/socket services. Incus exposes Unix sockets under <span class=\"mono kv\">/run/netmaker</span>. Xray terminates and routes by SNI behind WireGuard identity. The intended public posture is no direct Netmaker service port.</p>\n198:      <text x=\"130\" y=\"132\" fill=\"#21d4fd\" font-size=\"15\" text-anchor=\"middle\">Xray</text>\n211:      <text x=\"490\" y=\"238\" fill=\"#68758d\" font-size=\"11\" text-anchor=\"middle\">loopback service posture · Unix sockets · Incus proxy devices · Xray routing · WireGuard identity</text>\n220:    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Header provenance</h3><p>Xray/OpenClaw metadata carries <span class=\"mono kv\">X-Ghostbridge-Footprint</span>, <span class=\"mono kv\">X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID</span>, or WireGuard pubkey identity.</p></div>\n230:  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">cognitive-mcp is the universal external gateway for NotebookLM, Droid/factory.ai, Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI, and related clients. compact-mcp remains loopback/chatbot only. The gateway exposes memory, gRPC service, auth, tool surfaces, and context retrieval.</p>\n232:    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>cognitive-mcp</h3><p>Universal MCP gateway, memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and protocol surface.</p></div>\n233:    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>ZeroClaw</h3><p>Routes to the right model/provider by cost, reasoning depth, policy, specialty, and structured output needs.</p></div>\n239:  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">gRPC plane</div>\n240:  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">gRPC is the high-throughput service plane between the governed components.</h2>\n242:    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Transport</h3><p>gRPC runs over Unix domain sockets or controlled local bridge paths when the service should stay inside the host boundary.</p></div>\n244:    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Search/API</h3><p>Semantic search, chat tools, and assistant integration use gRPC surfaces where D-Bus itself is not the best transport.</p></div>\n247:    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 1160 220\" width=\"100%\" aria-label=\"gRPC service plane\">\n254:        <rect x=\"422\" y=\"60\" width=\"160\" height=\"54\" rx=\"12\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/><text x=\"502\" y=\"81\" fill=\"#edf4ff\">gRPC</text><text x=\"502\" y=\"99\" fill=\"#68758d\">UDS transport</text>\n266:      <text x=\"580\" y=\"176\" fill=\"#68758d\" font-size=\"11\" text-anchor=\"middle\">same system, two planes: HTTP/UI for presentation; gRPC for governed service-to-service transport; D-Bus remains authority</text>\n293:    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>semantic_vectors</h3><p>Separate plugin for Voyage/Qdrant config, vector schema, endpoint metadata, and revectorization policy.</p></div>\n326:      <text x=\"580\" y=\"176\" fill=\"#68758d\" font-size=\"11\" text-anchor=\"middle\">semantic projection is derived from evidence; it is not the authority. the authority is the chain + schema + D-Bus control plane.</text>\n337:    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\" style=\"background:var(--cyan)\"></span>Enterprise drop-in</h3><ul class=\"clean\"><li>Active Directory</li><li>databases</li><li>Slack</li><li>CMS</li><li>schema-backed deployment</li><li>governed mesh</li></ul></div>\n361:<div class=\"footer\">GhostBridge · Operation D-Bus · Netmaker technical use case deck · self-contained HTML · confidential pre-meeting context</div>\n"}}

class=\"scan\"></div>\n\n<section>\n  <div class=\"wrap\">\n    <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">GhostBridge x Netmaker</div>\n    <h1 class=\"reveal d1\">Full technical use case deck.</h1>\n    <p class=\"lead reveal d2\">Netmaker is the mesh and identity backbone of GhostBridge: a Rust platform-as-a-service control plane for governed AI, schema-authored state, no-NIC service hardening, gRPC-over-UDS service transport, semantic evidence, and tamper-evident accountability.</p>\n    <div class=\"chips reveal d3\">\n      <span class=\"chip\">Netmaker</span><span class=\"chip\">WireGuard</span><span class=\"chip\">D-Bus</span><span class=\"chip\">PluginSchema</span><span class=\"chip\">Xray</span><span class=\"chip\">Incus</span><span class=\"chip\">Open vSwitch</span><span class=\"chip\">gRPC</span><span class=\"chip\">Unix sockets</span><span class=\"chip\">Qdrant</span><span class=\"chip\">Cozo</span><span class=\"chip\">Voyage</span><span class=\"chip\">OSCAL</span>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"muted reveal d3\" style=\"max-width:850px\">First human eyes outside the project. Sending the full system context now; I will answer questions in the meeting tomorrow.</p>\n  </div>\n</section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">System thesis</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">A mesh is more than transport when it becomes the root of evidence.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">GhostBridge treats Netmaker/WireGuard identity as link zero. Every governed action carries identity, mutation, schema, policy authority, trace, footprint, and semantic meaning. AI can reason over the evidence, but only the governed layer can mutate state. gRPC is the service plane that moves these contracts between Rust components over Unix sockets and controlled bridge paths.</p>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:20px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Transport</h3><p>Netmaker mesh carries the trusted path. Xray routes by SNI and injects identity/accountability headers.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Identity</h3><p>WireGuard peer material anchors <span class=\"mono kv\">session_id = Argon2(PSK, salt = WG_pubkey)</span>.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Evidence</h3><p>The Snowball ledger records accepted actions as hash-linked blocks with semantic projections.</p></div>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap reveal d3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 1160 260\" width=\"100%\"
