contracts move in gRPC, and evidence is searchable in Qdrant</text>\n    </svg>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Core runtime architecture</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">One control plane. One schema truth. Multiple transport surfaces.</h2>\n  <div class=\"table reveal d2\">\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">D-Bus projection</div><div class=\"td\">Live authority is <span class=\"mono kv\">org.opdbus.projection</span>; plugin objects publish under <span class=\"mono kv\">/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/&lt;name&gt;</span>.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">PluginSchema</div><div class=\"td\">Plugin is schema. If a validated schema/object is missing, the thing does not exist in the system.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Sled</div><div class=\"td\">1:1 shared-memory layout for identity/state projection; schema-guided direct read/write semantics.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Shuttle</div><div class=\"td\">Rust bridge/courier between D-Bus, gRPC, vector search, state projection, and UI surfaces.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Snowball</div><div class=\"td\">Append-only session ledger. Each accepted action extends evidence rather than overwriting history.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Strike / Etch</div><div class=\"td\">Hash generation and footprint binding for blocks, traces, and payloads.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC / UDS</div><div class=\"td\">Internal service RPC over Unix sockets or controlled bridge paths; D-Bus remains authority, gRPC is transport.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC bridge</div><div class=\"td\">Service-to-service APIs, event-chain search, assistant surfaces, and internal contracts flow over gRPC when they are not directly D-Bus-bound.</div></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Authority plane</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Plugin is schema. D-Bus is authority. A.N.N.A. notarizes the state.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">This is the control contract that keeps the rest of the platform honest: D-Bus publishes the object, PluginSchema defines the shape, A.N.N.A. Scribe notarizes identity and trace, and the Law Firm enforces policy references on top.</p>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap reveal d3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 1160 250\" width=\"100%\" aria-label=\"Authority plane\">\n      <defs>\n        <marker id=\"arrowA\" markerWidth=\"10\" markerHeight=\"10\" refX=\"7\" refY=\"3\" orient=\"auto\"><path d=\"M0,0 L7,3 L0,6 Z\" fill=\"#68758d\"/></marker>\n      </defs>\n      <g font-size=\"12\" text-anchor=\"middle\">\n        <rect x=\"24\" y=\"66\" width=\"150\" height=\"52\" rx=\"12\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/><text x=\"99\" y=\"88\" fill=\"#edf4ff\">D-Bus</text><text x=\"99\" y=\"106\" fill=\"#68758d\">org.opdbus.projection</text>\n        <rect x=\"204\" y=\"66\" width=\"180\" height=\"52\" rx=\"12\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/><text x=\"294\" y=\"88\" fill=\"#edf4ff\">PluginSchema</text><text x=\"294\" y=\"106\" fill=\"#68758d\">shape + validation</text>\n        <rect x=\"414\" y=\"66\" width=\"170\" height=\"52\" rx=\"12\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/><text x=\"499\" y=\"88\" fill=\"#edf4ff\">Plugin Objects</text><text x=\"499\" y=\"106\" fill=\"#68758d\">/org/opdbus/v1/plugins</text>\n        <rect x=\"614\" y=\"66\" width=\"170\" height=\"52\" rx=\"12\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/><text x=\"699\" y=\"88\" fill=\"#edf4ff\">A.N.N.A. class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Netmaker hardening pattern</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Control services become socket-backed, identity-gated surfaces.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">The pattern treats <span class=\"mono\">netmaker</span>, <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-mq</span>, and <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-ui</span> as loopback/socket services. Incus exposes Unix sockets under <span class=\"mono kv\">/run/netmaker</span>. Xray terminates and routes by SNI behind WireGuard identity. The intended public posture is no direct Netmaker service port.</p>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap reveal d2\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 980 260\" width=\"100%\" aria-label=\"No NIC socket-backed Netmaker pattern\">\n      <rect x=\"35\" y=\"54\" width=\"190\" height=\"148\" rx=\"16\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/>\n      <text x=\"130\" y=\"44\" fill=\"#a8b5cc\" reveal\">Accountability loop</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Chatbot on top. Semantic evidence underneath.</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g2\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Header provenance</h3><p>Xray/OpenClaw metadata carries <span class=\"mono kv\">X-Ghostbridge-Footprint</span>, <span class=\"mono kv\">X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID</span>, or WireGuard pubkey identity.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Snowball block</h3><p>Accepted action becomes a hash-linked block with previous hash, event hash, trace id, footprint, subid, actor, and capability.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Semantic projection</h3><p>Voyage embeds blocks, docs, transcripts, and chat turns. Qdrant makes meaning searchable. Cozo tracks graph/realtime relationships.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Cross-examination</h3><p>The model explains. The evidence pane verifies. If the explanation drifts, semantic receipts contradict it.</p></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">AI and MCP surfaces</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">External clients enter through cognitive-mcp.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">cognitive-mcp is the universal external gateway for NotebookLM, Droid/factory.ai, Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI, and related clients. compact-mcp remains loopback/chatbot only. The gateway exposes memory, gRPC service, auth, tool surfaces, and context retrieval.</p>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>cognitive-mcp</h3><p>Universal MCP gateway, memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and protocol surface.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>ZeroClaw</h3><p>Routes to the right model/provider by cost, reasoning depth, policy, specialty, and structured output needs.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>NotebookLM path</h3><p>Notebook/imported context becomes source material for vectorization and semantic evidence, not an authority bypass.</p></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section class=\"short\"><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">gRPC plane</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">gRPC is the high-throughput service plane between the governed components.</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Transport</h3><p>gRPC runs over Unix domain sockets or controlled local bridge paths when the service should stay inside the host boundary.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Bridge</h3><p>The Shuttle and bridge services move requests between D-Bus authority, memory/state, and higher-level assistants without inventing a second control plane.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Search/API</h3><p>Semantic search, chat tools, and assistant integration use gRPC surfaces where D-Bus itself is not the best transport.</p></div>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap reveal d3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 1160 220\" width=\"100%\" aria-label=\"gRPC service plane\">\n      <defs>\n        <marker id=\"arrow2\" AI can reason over the evidence, but only the governed layer can mutate state. gRPC is the service plane that moves these contracts between Rust components over Unix sockets and controlled bridge paths, and Tonic is the Rust implementation of that gRPC transport.</p>\n   <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:20px\">\n@@ -124,2 +124,3 @@\n   <div class=\"table reveal d2\">\n+    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Rust control plane</div><div class=\"td\">The whole system is a Rust control plane first: state, validation, bridges, and projections live in compiled Rust crates rather than ad hoc scripts.</div></div>\n     <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">D-Bus projection</div><div class=\"td\">Live authority is <span class=\"mono kv\">org.opdbus.projection</span>; plugin objects publish under <span class=\"mono kv\">/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/&lt;name&gt;</span>.</div></div>\n@@ -136,2 +137,33 @@\n <section><div class=\"wrap\">\n+  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Why these choices</div>\n+  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Tonic, Gemma, and ZeroClaw each fill a specific role.</h2>\n+  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n+    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Tonic</h3><p>The gRPC implementation in Rust. It fits the control plane because it keeps service transport type-safe, schema-driven, and local-socket friendly.</p></div>\n+    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Gemma</h3><p>The traffic classifier/router for the front of the pipeline. Gemma decides what a request is before Xray/OpenFlow decide where it should go.</p></div>\n+    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>ZeroClaw</h3><p>Policy-aware model dispatch. It is not a generic wrapper; it centralizes model routing by cost, reasoning depth, provider, structure, and policy so the rest of the stack stays schema-native.</p></div>\n+  </div>\n+  <div {"timestamp":"2026-06-15T05:28:33.449Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_lrunC2KwGAJ8f32fNz2l3ELG","output":"Chunk ID: 22b6da\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1942\nOutput:\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Core runtime architecture</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">One control plane. One schema truth. Multiple transport surfaces.</h2>\n  <div class=\"table reveal d2\">\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Rust control plane</div><div class=\"td\">The whole system is a Rust control plane first: state, validation, bridges, and projections live in compiled Rust crates rather than ad hoc scripts.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">D-Bus projection</div><div class=\"td\">Live authority is <span class=\"mono kv\">org.opdbus.projection</span>; plugin objects publish under <span class=\"mono kv\">/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/&lt;name&gt;</span>.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">PluginSchema</div><div class=\"td\">Plugin is schema. If a validated schema/object is missing, the thing does not exist in the system.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Sled</div><div class=\"td\">1:1 shared-memory layout for identity/state projection; schema-guided direct read/write semantics.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Shuttle</div><div class=\"td\">Rust bridge/courier between D-Bus, gRPC, vector search, state projection, and UI surfaces.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Snowball</div><div class=\"td\">Append-only session ledger. Each accepted action extends evidence rather than overwriting history.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Strike / Etch</div><div class=\"td\">Hash generation and footprint binding for blocks, traces, and payloads.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC / UDS</div><div class=\"td\">Internal service RPC over Unix sockets or controlled bridge paths; D-Bus remains authority, gRPC is transport.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC bridge</div><div class=\"td\">Service-to-service APIs, event-chain search, assistant surfaces, and internal contracts flow over gRPC when they are not directly D-Bus-bound.</div></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Why these choices</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Tonic, Gemma, and ZeroClaw each fill a specific role.</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Tonic</h3><p>The gRPC implementation in Rust. It fits the control plane because it keeps service transport type-safe, schema-driven, and local-socket friendly.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Gemma</h3><p>The traffic classifier/router for the front of the pipeline. Gemma decides what a request is before Xray/OpenFlow decide where it should go.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>ZeroClaw</h3><p>Policy-aware model dispatch. Multiple transport surfaces.</h2>\n  <div class=\"table reveal d2\">\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Rust control plane</div><div class=\"td\">The whole system is a Rust control plane first: state, validation, bridges, and projections live in compiled Rust crates rather than ad hoc scripts.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">D-Bus projection</div><div class=\"td\">Live authority is <span class=\"mono kv\">org.opdbus.projection</span>; plugin objects publish under <span class=\"mono kv\">/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/&lt;name&gt;</span>.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">PluginSchema</div><div class=\"td\">Plugin is schema. If a validated schema/object is missing, the thing does not exist in the system.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Sled</div><div class=\"td\">1:1 shared-memory layout for identity/state projection; schema-guided direct read/write semantics.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Shuttle</div><div class=\"td\">Rust bridge/courier between D-Bus, gRPC, vector search, state projection, and UI surfaces.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Snowball</div><div class=\"td\">Append-only session ledger and memory-loop substrate. Chat turns, tool actions, and approvals are appended here, then replayed into semantic search and UI evidence.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Strike / Etch</div><div class=\"td\">Hash generation and footprint binding for blocks, traces, and payloads.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC / UDS</div><div class=\"td\">Internal service RPC over Unix sockets or controlled bridge paths; D-Bus remains authority, gRPC is transport.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC bridge</div><div class=\"td\">Service-to-service APIs, event-chain search, assistant surfaces, and internal contracts flow over gRPC when they are not directly D-Bus-bound.</div></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Why these choices</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Tonic, Gemma, and ZeroClaw each fill a specific role.</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Tonic</h3><p>The gRPC implementation in Rust. It fits the control plane because it keeps service transport type-safe, schema-driven, and local-socket friendly.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Gemma</h3><p>The traffic classifier/router for the front of the pipeline. AI can reason over the evidence, but only the governed layer can mutate state. gRPC is the service plane that moves these contracts between Rust components over Unix sockets and controlled bridge paths, and Tonic is the Rust implementation of that gRPC transport.</p>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:20px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Transport</h3><p>Netmaker mesh carries the trusted path. Xray routes by SNI and injects identity/accountability headers.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Identity</h3><p>WireGuard peer material anchors <span class=\"mono kv\">session_id = Argon2(PSK, salt = WG_pubkey)</span>.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Evidence</h3><p>The Snowball ledger is the memory-loop target: accepted actions are appended as hash-linked blocks, then replayed into semantic projections for retrieval and confrontation.</p></div>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap reveal d3\" class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>No verified schema, no existence</h3><p>If a thing has no validated schema, it is not a real object in this system. That is the primary attack boundary and the primary source of truth.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Single source of truth</h3><p>Schema-backed D-Bus projection is authoritative. UI, gRPC, MCP, search, and evidence are projections or transports, not alternate realities.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Use live resources</h3><p>Build from working realtime resources that already exist. Let current evidence shape the future state instead of searching for hypothetical resources to invent later.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Reality first</h3><p>Prefer observed state, live traces, and actual object graphs over claims, intentions, or clean-room abstractions.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Future from present</h3><p>The future is shaped by what is already running, measurable, and schema-valid today. That is how the platform stays grounded.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>No speculative resources</h3><p>We do not “find resources to use in the future.” We use current realtime resources to build the next state from the current one.</p></div>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap reveal d3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 1160 220\" width=\"100%\" aria-label=\"Core philosophies\">\n      <defs><marker id=\"arrowP\" markerWidth=\"10\" markerHeight=\"10\" refX=\"7\" refY=\"3\" orient=\"auto\"><path d=\"M0,0 L7,3 L0,6 Z\" fill=\"#68758d\"/></marker></defs>\n      <g font-size=\"12\" text-anchor=\"middle\">\n        <rect x=\"30\" y=\"54\" width=\"180\" height=\"54\" rx=\"12\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/><text font-size=\"11\" text-anchor=\"middle\">live resources are validated into schema; schema becomes truth; memory loop appends/replays; the future is built from the present state, not imagined inventory</text>\n    </svg>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Core runtime architecture</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">One control plane. One schema truth. Multiple transport surfaces.</h2>\n  <div class=\"table reveal d2\">\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Rust control plane</div><div class=\"td\">The whole system is a Rust control plane first: state, validation, bridges, and projections live in compiled Rust crates rather than ad hoc scripts.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">D-Bus projection</div><div class=\"td\">Live authority is <span class=\"mono kv\">org.opdbus.projection</span>; plugin objects publish under <span class=\"mono kv\">/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/&lt;name&gt;</span>.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">PluginSchema</div><div class=\"td\">Plugin is schema. If a validated schema/object is missing, the thing does not exist in the system.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Sled</div><div class=\"td\">1:1 shared-memory layout for identity/state projection; schema-guided direct read/write semantics.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Shuttle</div><div class=\"td\">Rust bridge/courier between D-Bus, gRPC, vector search, state projection, and UI surfaces.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Snowball</div><div class=\"td\">Append-only session ledger and memory-loop substrate. Chat turns, tool actions, and approvals are appended here, then replayed into semantic search and UI evidence.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Strike / Etch</div><div class=\"td\">Hash generation and footprint binding for blocks, traces, and payloads.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC / UDS</div><div class=\"td\">Internal service RPC over Unix sockets or controlled bridge paths; D-Bus remains authority, gRPC is transport.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC bridge</div><div class=\"td\">Service-to-service APIs, event-chain search, assistant surfaces, and internal contracts flow over gRPC when they are not directly D-Bus-bound.</div></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Why these choices</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Tonic, Gemma, and ZeroClaw each fill a specific role.</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Tonic</h3><p>The gRPC implementation in Rust. It fits the control plane because it keeps service transport type-safe, schema-driven, and local-socket friendly.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Gemma</h3><p>The traffic classifier/router for the front of the pipeline. Gemma decides what a request is before Xray/OpenFlow decide where it should go.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>ZeroClaw</h3><p>Policy-aware model dispatch. It is not a generic wrapper; it centralizes model routing by cost, reasoning depth, provider, structure, and policy so the rest of the stack stays schema-native.</p></div>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Netmaker hardening pattern</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Control services become socket-backed, identity-gated surfaces.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">The pattern treats <span class=\"mono\">netmaker</span>, <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-mq</span>, and <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-ui</span> as loopback/socket services. Incus exposes Unix sockets under <span class=\"mono kv\">/run/netmaker</span>. Xray terminates and routes by SNI behind WireGuard identity. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. class=\"scan\"></div>\n\n<section>\n  <div class=\"wrap\">\n    <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">GhostBridge x Netmaker</div>\n    <h1 class=\"reveal d1\">Full technical use case deck.</h1>\n    <p class=\"lead reveal d2\">Netmaker is the mesh and identity backbone of GhostBridge: a Rust control plane platform-as-a-service for governed AI, schema-authored state, no-NIC service hardening, gRPC-over-UDS service transport, semantic evidence, and tamper-evident accountability.</p>\n    <div class=\"chips reveal d3\">\n      <span class=\"chip\">Netmaker</span><span class=\"chip\">WireGuard</span><span class=\"chip\">D-Bus</span><span class=\"chip\">PluginSchema</span><span class=\"chip\">Xray</span><span class=\"chip\">Incus</span><span class=\"chip\">Open vSwitch</span><span class=\"chip\">OpenFlow</span><span class=\"chip\">gRPC</span><span class=\"chip\">Tonic</span><span class=\"chip\">Gemma</span><span class=\"chip\">Unix sockets</span><span class=\"chip\">Qdrant</span><span class=\"chip\">Cozo</span><span class=\"chip\">Voyage</span><span class=\"chip\">OSCAL</span>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"muted reveal d3\" style=\"max-width:850px\">First human eyes outside the project. Sending the full system context now; I will answer questions in the meeting tomorrow.</p>\n  </div>\n</section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">System thesis</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">A mesh is more than transport when it becomes the root of evidence.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">GhostBridge treats Netmaker/WireGuard identity as link zero. Every governed action carries identity, mutation, schema, policy authority, trace, footprint, and semantic meaning. AI can reason over the evidence, but only the governed layer can mutate state. gRPC is the service plane that moves these contracts between Rust components over Unix sockets and controlled bridge paths, and Tonic is the Rust implementation of that gRPC transport.</p>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:20px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Transport</h3><p>Netmaker mesh carries the trusted path. Xray routes by SNI and injects identity/accountability headers.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Identity</h3><p>WireGuard peer material anchors <span class=\"mono kv\">session_id = Argon2(PSK, salt = WG_pubkey)</span>.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Evidence</h3><p>The Snowball ledger is the memory-loop target: accepted actions are appended as hash-linked blocks, then replayed into semantic projections for retrieval and confrontation.</p></div>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap reveal d3\" </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Core philosophies</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">What cannot be verified does not exist.</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>No verified schema, no existence</h3><p>If a thing has no validated schema, it is not a real object in this system. That is the primary attack boundary and the primary source of truth.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Single source of truth</h3><p>Schema-backed D-Bus projection is authoritative. UI, gRPC, MCP, search, and evidence are projections or transports, not alternate realities.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Use live resources</h3><p>Build from working realtime resources that already exist. Let current evidence shape the future state instead of searching for hypothetical resources to invent later.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Reality first</h3><p>Prefer observed state, live traces, and actual object graphs over claims, intentions, or clean-room abstractions.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Future from present</h3><p>The future is shaped by what is already running, measurable, and schema-valid today. That is how the platform stays grounded.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>No speculative resources</h3><p>We do not “find resources to use in the future.” We use current realtime resources to build the next state from the current one.</p></div>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"svgwrap reveal d3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <svg viewBox=\"0 0 1160 220\" width=\"100%\" aria-label=\"Core philosophies\">\n      <defs><marker id=\"arrowP\" markerWidth=\"10\" markerHeight=\"10\" refX=\"7\" refY=\"3\" orient=\"auto\"><path d=\"M0,0 L7,3 L0,6 Z\" fill=\"#68758d\"/></marker></defs>\n      <g font-size=\"12\" text-anchor=\"middle\">\n        <rect x=\"30\" y=\"54\" width=\"180\" height=\"54\" rx=\"12\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/><text x=\"120\" y=\"76\" fill=\"#edf4ff\">Realtime resources</text><text x=\"120\" y=\"94\" fill=\"#68758d\">live objects, traces, state</text>\n        <rect x=\"250\" y=\"54\" width=\"180\" height=\"54\" y=\"54\" width=\"180\" height=\"54\" rx=\"12\" fill=\"#0f1320\" stroke=\"#2a3550\"/><text x=\"560\" y=\"76\" fill=\"#edf4ff\">Single truth</text><text x=\"560\" y=\"94\" fill=\"#68758d\">D-Bus y2=\"81\" marker-end=\"url(#arrowP)\"/>\n        <line x1=\"874\" y1=\"81\" x2=\"906\" y2=\"81\" marker-end=\"url(#arrowP)\"/>\n      </g>\n      <text x=\"580\" y=\"176\" fill=\"#68758d\" font-size=\"11\" text-anchor=\"middle\">live resources are validated into schema; schema becomes truth; memory loop appends/replays; the future is built from the present state, not imagined inventory</text>\n    </svg>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Core runtime architecture</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">One control plane. One schema truth. Multiple transport surfaces.</h2>\n  <div class=\"table reveal d2\">\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Rust control plane</div><div class=\"td\">The whole system is a Rust control plane first: state, validation, bridges, and projections live in compiled Rust crates rather than ad hoc scripts.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">D-Bus projection</div><div class=\"td\">Live authority is <span class=\"mono kv\">org.opdbus.projection</span>; plugin objects publish under <span class=\"mono kv\">/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/&lt;name&gt;</span>.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">PluginSchema</div><div class=\"td\">Plugin is schema. If a validated schema/object is missing, the thing does not exist in the system.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Sled</div><div class=\"td\">1:1 shared-memory layout for identity/state projection; schema-guided direct read/write semantics.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Shuttle</div><div class=\"td\">Rust bridge/courier between D-Bus, gRPC, vector search, state projection, and UI surfaces.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">The Snowball</div><div class=\"td\">Append-only session ledger and memory-loop substrate. Chat turns, tool actions, and approvals are appended here, then replayed into semantic search and UI evidence.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">Strike / Etch</div><div class=\"td\">Hash generation and footprint binding for blocks, traces, and payloads.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC / UDS</div><div class=\"td\">Internal service RPC over Unix sockets or controlled bridge paths; D-Bus remains authority, gRPC is transport.</div></div>\n    <div class=\"tr\"><div class=\"td\">gRPC bridge</div><div class=\"td\">Service-to-service APIs, event-chain search, assistant surfaces, and internal contracts flow over gRPC when they are not directly D-Bus-bound.</div></div>\n  </div>\n</div></section>\n\n<section><div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Why these choices</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Tonic, Gemma, and ZeroClaw each fill a specific role.</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid g3\" style=\"margin-top:18px\">\n    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Tonic</h3><p>The gRPC implementation in Rust. It fits the control plane because it keeps service transport type-safe, schema-driven, and local-socket friendly.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d1\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Gemma</h3><p>The traffic classifier/router for the front of the pipeline. Gemma decides what a request is before Xray/OpenFlow decide where it should go.</p></div>\n    <div class=\"card reveal d2\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>ZeroClaw</h3><p>Policy-aware model dispatch. It is not a generic wrapper; it centralizes model routing by cost, reasoning depth, provider, structure, and policy so the rest of the stack stays schema-native.</p></div>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">Netmaker hardening pattern</div>\n  <h2 class=\"reveal d1\">Control services become socket-backed, identity-gated surfaces.</h2>\n  <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">The pattern treats <span class=\"mono\">netmaker</span>, <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-mq</span>, and <span class=\"mono\">netmaker-ui</span> as loopback/socket services. {"timestamp":"2026-06-15T05:47:08.223Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_Dz49CZlTkG6d5dAAmqMkCsd4","output":"Chunk ID: b34e50\nWall time: 0.0001 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 4189\nOutput:\n6:<title>GhostBridge x Netmaker - Technical Platform Deck</title>\n16:  font:16px/1.62 -apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,\"Segoe UI\",Inter,Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif}\n75:    <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">GhostBridge x Netmaker</div>\n77:    <p class=\"lead reveal d2\">Netmaker is the mesh and identity backbone of GhostBridge: a Rust control plane platform-as-a-service for governed AI, schema-authored state, no-NIC service hardening, gRPC over Unix domain sockets (UDS), semantic evidence, and tamper-evident accountability.</p>\n79:      <span class=\"chip\">Netmaker</span><span class=\"chip\">WireGuard</span><span class=\"chip\">D-Bus</span><span class=\"chip\">PluginSchema</span><span class=\"chip\">Xray</span><span class=\"chip\">Incus</span><span class=\"chip\">Open vSwitch</span><span class=\"chip\">OpenFlow</span><span class=\"chip\">gRPC</span><span class=\"chip\">Tonic</span><span class=\"chip\">Gemma</span><span class=\"chip\">Unix domain sockets</span><span class=\"chip\">Qdrant</span><span class=\"chip\">Cozo</span><span class=\"chip\">Voyage</span><span class=\"chip\">OSCAL</span>\n88:    <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">GhostBridge treats Netmaker/WireGuard identity as link zero. {"timestamp":"2026-06-15T06:44:27.538Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"`Tonic reflection` usually means **gRPC server reflection** in the Rust `tonic` ecosystem.\n\nIn practice, it lets a running gRPC server answer questions like:\n\n- what services are available\n- what methods they expose\n- what request/response types they use\n- what protobuf descriptors define them\n\nWhy it matters:\n\n- tools like `grpcurl` can inspect the service without a local `.proto` file\n- developers can debug and explore the API at runtime\n- it makes the service more self-describing\n\nIn `tonic`, reflection is typically an **optional server feature**, not the core RPC mechanism. The core RPC still comes from your normal protobuf-generated service definitions. Reflection just exposes metadata about them.\n\nSo if you want deck wording, the clean version is:\n\n- `Tonic` = Rust gRPC implementation\n- `Tonic reflection` = runtime API discovery for gRPC clients and debugging tools\n\nIf you want, I can also give you the exact sentence to drop into the deck so it reads naturally for a sales/engineer audience.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

The core RPC still comes from your normal protobuf-generated service definitions. LLM API routes for provider and model management\n\nuse axum::{\n    extract::{Extension, Query},\n    http::StatusCode,\n    response::IntoResponse,\n    Json,\n};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::{error, info};\n\nuse crate::state::AppState;\nuse op_llm::ProviderType;\n\n/// LLM status response\n#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]\npub struct LlmStatusResponse {\n    pub provider: String,\n    pub model: String,\n    pub model_non_sandboxed: bool,\n    pub available_providers: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n/// Model list response\n#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]\npub struct ModelsResponse {\n    pub provider: String,\n    pub models: Vec<ModelInfo>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]\npub struct ModelInfo {\n    pub id: String,\n    pub name: String,\n    pub description: Option<String>,\n    pub available: bool,\n    pub provider: Option<String>,\n    pub upstream_provider: Option<String>,\n    pub transport: Option<String>,\n    pub status: Option<String>,\n    pub route_hint: Option<String>,\n    pub route_kind: Option<String>,\n    pub status_reason: Option<String>,\n    pub source: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Provider switch request\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\npub struct SwitchProviderRequest {\n    pub provider: String,\n}\n\n/// Model switch request\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\npub struct SwitchModelRequest {\n    pub model: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub non_sandboxed: bool,\n}\n\n/// Query params for models endpoint\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\npub struct ModelsQuery {\n    pub provider: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// GET /api/llm/status - Get current LLM status\npub async fn get_llm_status(Extension(state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>) -> impl IntoResponse {\n    let status = state.chat_manager.get_status().await;\n\n    Json(LlmStatusResponse {\n        provider: status[\"provider\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string(),\n        model: status[\"model\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string(),\n        model_non_sandboxed: state.chat_manager.current_model_non_sandboxed().await,\n        available_providers: status[\"available_providers\"]\n            .as_array()\n            .map(|arr| {\n                arr.iter()\n                    .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(String::from))\n                    .collect()\n            })\n            .unwrap_or_default(),\n    })\n}\n\n/// Build the model list from the zeroclaw plugin projection (`model_routes`).\n///\n/// The zeroclaw plugin is the single source of truth: its `query_current_state`\n/// is projected verbatim at `/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw`. We read it from\n/// the projection cache and surface each route as a selectable model.\nasync fn models_from_zeroclaw(state: &AppState) -> Option<Vec<ModelInfo>> {\n    let routes = crate::zeroclaw_routes::routes(&state.projection_cache).await?;\n\n    let models: Vec<ModelInfo> = routes\n        .iter()\n        .map(|route| {\n            let description = match route.hint.as_deref() {\n                Some(h) => format!(\"{} · {} · {}\", route.provider, h, route.status),\n                None => format!(\"{} · {}\", route.provider, route.status),\n            };\n            let name = match route.hint.as_deref() {\n                Some(h) => format!(\"{} ({})\", route.model, h),\n                None => route.model.clone(),\n            };\n            ModelInfo {\n                id: route.model.clone(),\n                name,\n                description: Some(description),\n                available: route.available,\n                provider: Some(route.upstream_provider.clone()),\n                upstream_provider: Some(route.upstream_provider.clone()),\n                transport: route.transport.clone(),\n                status: Some(route.status.clone()),\n                route_hint: route.hint.clone(),\n                route_kind: route.kind.clone(),\n                status_reason: route.status_reason.clone(),\n                source: route.source.clone(),\n            }\n        })\n        .collect();\n\n    if models.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(models)\n    }\n}\n\n/// GET /api/llm/models - Get models for current or specified provider\npub async fn get_models(\n    Extension(state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Query(query): Query<ModelsQuery>,\n) -> impl IntoResponse {\n    let Some(ref provider_str) = query.provider else {\n        // The zeroclaw plugin projection is the default source of truth for the combined model list.\n        if let Some(models) = models_from_zeroclaw(&state).await {\n            return Json(ModelsResponse {\n                provider: \"zeroclaw\".to_string(),\n                models,\n            })\n            .into_response();\n        }\n\n        return (\n            StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,\n            Json(simd_json::json!({\n                \"error\": \"Zeroclaw model route projection is unavailable\",\n                \"provider\": \"zeroclaw\",\n                \"models\": []\n            })),\n        )\n            .into_response();\n    };\n\n    if provider_str == \"zeroclaw\" {\n        if let Some(models) = models_from_zeroclaw(&state).await {\n            return Json(ModelsResponse {\n                provider: \"zeroclaw\".to_string(),\n                models,\n            })\n            .into_response();\n        }\n    }\n\n    let provider_type = match provider_str.parse::<ProviderType>() {\n        Ok(pt) => pt,\n        Err(_) => {\n            return (\n                StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,\n                Json(simd_json::json!({ \"error\": format!(\"Unknown provider: {}\", provider_str) })),\n            )\n                .into_response();\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Check if provider is available\n    if !state.chat_manager.has_provider(&provider_type) {\n        return (\n            StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,\n            Json(simd_json::json!({\n                \"error\": format!(\"Provider {} not available. Check API key.\", provider_type),\n                \"provider\": provider_type.to_string(),\n                \"models\": []\n            })),\n        )\n            .into_response();\n    }\n\n    match state\n        .chat_manager\n        .list_models_for_provider(&provider_type)\n        .await\n    {\n        Ok(models) => {\n            let model_infos: Vec<ModelInfo> = models\n                .into_iter()\n                .map(|m| ModelInfo {\n                    id: m.id,\n                    name: m.name,\n                    description: m.description,\n                    available: m.available,\n                    provider: Some(provider_type.to_string()),\n                    upstream_provider: Some(provider_type.to_string()),\n                    transport: None,\n                    status: Some(\n                        if m.available {\n                            \"available\"\n                        } else {\n                            \"unavailable\"\n                        }\n                        .to_string(),\n                    ),\n                    route_hint: None,\n                    route_kind: None,\n                    status_reason: None,\n                    source: None,\n                })\n                .collect();\n"}}

Gemma — the subid → tag → OpenFlow + xray routing brain.\n//!\n//! Reads the canonical subid registry from `/etc/ghostbridge/subid-registry.json`\n//! and writes two tmpfs artifacts:\n//!   - `/dev/shm/xray-routes.json`    — routes for the op-identity-shuttle\n//!   - `/dev/shm/openflow-routes.json` — rules for the OpenFlow controller\n//!\n//! Per AGENTS.md §4: D-Bus is the control plane; Gemma is a host service that\n//! produces structured state, not a CLI bypass. It never shells out to network\n//! tools. OpenFlow rules may be applied via D-Bus by a separate controller.\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse tracing::info;\n\nconst SUBID_REGISTRY: &str = \"/etc/ghostbridge/subid-registry.json\";\nconst XRAY_ROUTES: &str = \"/dev/shm/xray-routes.json\";\nconst OPENFLOW_ROUTES: &str = \"/dev/shm/openflow-routes.json\";\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct SubidRegistry {\n    version: u32,\n    entries: Vec<RegistryEntry>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct RegistryEntry {\n    uuid: String,\n    subid: String,\n    #[serde(rename = \"category\")]\n    category: String,\n    #[serde(rename = \"component_type\")]\n    component_type: String,\n    subject: String,\n    verb: String,\n    version: u8,\n    tags: Vec<String>,\n    subdomains: Vec<String>,\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    gemma: Option<GemmaConfig>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct GemmaConfig {\n    backend: BackendSpec,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]\n#[serde(tag = \"type\")]\nenum BackendSpec {\n    #[serde(rename = \"ingress\")]\n    Ingress,\n    #[serde(rename = \"tcp\")]\n    Tcp { host: String, port: u16 },\n    #[serde(rename = \"grpc\")]\n    Grpc {\n        host: String,\n        port: u16,\n        #[serde(rename = \"service_name\")]\n        service_name: String,\n    },\n    #[serde(rename = \"unix\")]\n    Unix { path: String },\n    #[serde(rename = \"dns\")]\n    Dns { host: String, port: u16 },\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\nstruct XrayRoutingMap {\n    version: u32,\n    xray_routes: Vec<XrayRoute>,\n    openflow_rules: Vec<OpenFlowRule>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\nstruct XrayRoute {\n    tag: String,\n    subdomains: Vec<String>,\n    backend: BackendSpec,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\nstruct OpenFlowRule {\n    priority: u16,\n    #[serde(rename = \"match_fields\")]\n    match_fields: HashMap<String, String>,\n    actions: Vec<String>,\n    description: Option<String>,\n}\n\nfn main() -> Result<()> {\n    tracing_subscriber::fmt()\n        .with_env_filter(tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::from_default_env())\n        .init();\n\n    info!(\"Gemma routing brain starting\");\n\n    let registry = load_registry()?;\n    let routes = derive_routes(&registry);\n\n    write_json(XRAY_ROUTES, &routes)?;\n    write_json(OPENFLOW_ROUTES, &routes)?;\n\n    info!(\n        xray_routes = routes.xray_routes.len(),\n        openflow_rules = routes.openflow_rules.len(),\n        \"Gemma wrote routing artifacts\"\n    );\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn load_registry() -> Result<SubidRegistry> {\n    let raw = fs::read_to_string(SUBID_REGISTRY)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read subid registry: {SUBID_REGISTRY}\"))?;\n    let parsed: SubidRegistry =\n        serde_json::from_str(&raw).with_context(|| \"failed to parse subid registry as JSON\")?;\n    Ok(parsed)\n}\n\nfn derive_routes(registry: &SubidRegistry) -> XrayRoutingMap {\n    let mut xray_routes = Vec::new();\n    let mut openflow_rules = default_privacy_chain();\n\n    for entry in &registry.entries {\n        let Some(gemma) = &entry.gemma else { continue };\n        let tag = entry\n            .tags\n            .first()\n            .cloned()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| entry.subject.clone());\n\n        let route = XrayRoute {\n            tag: tag.clone(),\n            subdomains: entry.subdomains.clone(),\n            backend: gemma.backend.clone(),\n        };\n        xray_routes.push(route);\n\n        if let Some(rule) = backend_to_openflow_rule(&tag, &gemma.backend) {\n            openflow_rules.push(rule);\n        }\n    }\n\n    XrayRoutingMap {\n        version: 1,\n        xray_routes,\n        openflow_rules,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Default privacy chain flows for the GhostBridge OVS bridge.\n/// These match the conventions in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/privacy_router.rs`.\nfn default_privacy_chain() -> Vec<OpenFlowRule> {\n    vec![\n        OpenFlowRule {\n            priority: 100,\n            match_fields: HashMap::from([(\"in_port\".to_string(), \"gbr_wg\".to_string())]),\n            actions: vec![\"output:gbr_warp\".to_string()],\n            description: Some(\"gbr_wg -> gbr_warp\".to_string()),\n        },\n        OpenFlowRule {\n            priority: 100,\n            match_fields: HashMap::from([(\"in_port\".to_string(), \"gbr_warp\".to_string())]),\n            actions: vec![\"output:gbr_xray\".to_string()],\n            description: Some(\"gbr_warp -> gbr_xray\".to_string()),\n        },\n        OpenFlowRule {\n            priority: 100,\n            match_fields: HashMap::from([(\"in_port\".to_string(), \"gbr_xray\".to_string())]),\n            actions: vec![\"output:gbr_warp\".to_string()],\n            description: Some(\"gbr_xray -> gbr_warp\".to_string()),\n        },\n        OpenFlowRule {\n            priority: 200,\n            match_fields: HashMap::from([(\"dl_type\".to_string(), \"0x0806\".to_string())]),\n            actions: vec![\"arp_responder\".to_string()],\n            description: Some(\"ARP Responder for privacy network\".to_string()),\n        },\n    ]\n}\n\n/// Translate a Gemma backend into an OpenFlow rule for the bridge.\n/// Only TCP/GRPC backends produce IP/Port matchable rules here; Unix sockets\n/// are terminated by xray's freedom/ds transport so no bridge match is needed.\nfn backend_to_openflow_rule(tag: &str, backend: &BackendSpec) -> Option<OpenFlowRule> {\n    let (host, port) = match backend {\n        BackendSpec::Tcp { host, port } => (host.clone(), *port),\n        BackendSpec::Grpc { host, port, .. } => (host.clone(), *port),\n        BackendSpec::Ingress | BackendSpec::Unix { .. } | BackendSpec::Dns { .. } => return None,\n    };\n\n    let mut match_fields = HashMap::new();\n    match_fields.insert(\"dl_type\".to_string(), \"0x0800\".to_string());\n    match_fields.insert(\"nw_proto\".to_string(), \"6\".to_string()); // TCP\n    match_fields.insert(\"nw_dst\".to_string(), host.clone());\n    match_fields.insert(\"tp_dst\".to_string(), port.to_string());\n\n    Some(OpenFlowRule {\n        priority: 150,\n        match_fields,\n        actions: vec![\"output:ovsbr0-mgmt\".to_string()],\n        description: Some(format!(\"Gemma: {tag} -> host backend {host}:{port}\")),\n    })\n}\n\nfn write_json<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P, value: &XrayRoutingMap) -> Result<()> {\n    let tmp = format!(\"{}.tmp\", path.as_ref().display());\n    let mut f =\n        fs::File::create(&tmp).with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create tmp file: {tmp}\"))?;\n    let json =\n        serde_json::to_string_pretty(value).with_context(|| \"failed to serialize routing map\")?;\n    f.write_all(json.as_bytes())\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write tmp file: {tmp}\"))?;\n    f.sync_data()\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to sync tmp file: {tmp}\"))?;\n    fs::rename(&tmp, path.as_ref())\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to rename {tmp} to {}\", path.as_ref().display()))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-17T10:27:15.850Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. Cloudflare’s current official flow is:\n\n1. Add `ghostbridge.tech` to Cloudflare first and switch its nameservers to Cloudflare.\n2. Disable DNSSEC at the current registrar before the nameserver change if DS records are present.\n3. Wait for the zone to become `Active` in Cloudflare. Cloudflare will not let you enter the auth code until then.\n4. Start the registrar transfer in Cloudflare and enter the authorization code.\n5. Approve the confirmation email from the losing registrar if they send one.\n6. Wait for the transfer to finish.\n\nImportant current constraints from Cloudflare:\n- The domain must be on Cloudflare full setup to use Cloudflare Registrar.\n- A recent registrant contact change can trigger a 60-day transfer lock.\n- If the domain was recently renewed after expiry, Cloudflare says to wait at least 45 days after the original expiration date before transferring if you want the extra year preserved.\n\nOfficial sources:\n- [Transfer your domain to Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/registrar/get-started/transfer-domain-to-cloudflare/)\n- [Add a domain to Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/manage-domains/add-site/)\n- [Cloudflare Registrar FAQ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/registrar/faq/)\n\nI can walk you through the exact order for `ghostbridge.tech` next:\n1. Check whether it is already active in Cloudflare.\n2. Check whether DNSSEC is still enabled at the current registrar.\n3. Then start the transfer step.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-15</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

`requirements.md`, `design.md`, and `tasks.md` files in `.kiro/specs/`:\\n\\n1.  **`op-gateway`**: Secure entry point with WireGuard auth and MCP routing.\\n2.  **`op-mcp`**: Unified MCP server with multiple transports (Stdio, HTTP, WebSocket, gRPC).\\n3.  **`op-dbus-model`**: Persistent data layer for plugin metadata and D-Bus schemas.\\n4.  **`op-introspection`**: Automated D-Bus discovery, XML **`op-api`**: High-performance REST interface (axum).\\n8.  **`op-worker`**: Background job execution and lifecycle management.\\n9.  **`op-cli`**: Hierarchical command-line interface (clap).\\n10. sessions are DashMap-backed in-memory\\n- Update replacement table: op-identity uses DashMap sessions, not\\n  a SQLite backend (op-services SQLite for service defs is accurate)\",\"messageHeadline\":\"fix: remove two fabricated state-store claims\",\"oid\":\"adac93cc1cd38d72f3ce4322b326f69c3bcd5f18\"},{\"authoredDate\":\"2026-05-30T16:27:34Z\",\"authors\":[{\"email\":\"noreply@anthropic.com\",\"id\":\"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3\",\"login\":\"claude\",\"name\":\"Claude\"}],\"committedDate\":\"2026-05-30T16:27:34Z\",\"messageBody\":\"op-blockchain::BlockEvent hashes only its own content (no prev_hash).\\nThe actual hash-linked chain — event_hash = H(prev_hash || payload),\\ntamper-proof by construction — is op-state-store::ChainEvent.\\n\\nUpdate Chronicle section to document both components accurately:\\n- op-blockchain: append-only BTRFS event log, per-event SHA256\\n- op-state-store::ChainEvent: prev_hash linked compliance chain\\n\\nPropagate correction through marketing angles, use-case scenarios,\\nfeature table, and LLM prompting notes.\",\"messageHeadline\":\"fix: correct Chronicle hash-chain attribution to op-state-store\",\"oid\":\"f27c71c2e73570038c9ccade0dd4beb46d1860ff\"},{\"authoredDate\":\"2026-05-30T16:36:46Z\",\"authors\":[{\"email\":\"noreply@anthropic.com\",\"id\":\"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3\",\"login\":\"claude\",\"name\":\"Claude\"}],\"committedDate\":\"2026-05-30T16:36:46Z\",\"messageBody\":\"- op-network: narrow \\\"No daemon\\\" to \\\"No NetworkManager daemon\\\" — the\\n  OVS/OVSDB path requires openvswitch-switch to be running\\n- Web dashboard routes: remove BTRFS, Data Stores, and Embedding from\\n  the route list; they are not registered in App.tsx (routes end at\\n  /accountability + catch-all); correct count from 30+ to 20+\",\"messageHeadline\":\"fix: two more accuracy corrections in product baseline\",\"oid\":\"7b0220407a4639a907b57358d9d07e524d9aba55\"},{\"authoredDate\":\"2026-05-30T16:44:16Z\",\"authors\":[{\"email\":\"noreply@anthropic.com\",\"id\":\"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3\",\"login\":\"claude\",\"name\":\"Claude\"}],\"committedDate\":\"2026-05-30T16:44:16Z\",\"messageBody\":\"Chronicle replication is implemented as BTRFS snapshot streaming\\n(btrfs send | ssh ... btrfs receive) in op-blockchain/src/blockchain.rs.\\nThe gRPC EventChainService streams events to local subscribers — it is\\nnot a cross-node chain replication service. Narrow the brand voice note\\nto reflect the actual implemented path; mark gRPC as event subscription.\",\"messageHeadline\":\"fix: correct Chronicle distribution transport claim\",\"oid\":\"643301f0917b6590e31f6191081336418a4faf89\"},{\"authoredDate\":\"2026-05-30T16:54:16Z\",\"authors\":[{\"email\":\"noreply@anthropic.com\",\"id\":\"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3\",\"login\":\"claude\",\"name\":\"Claude\"}],\"committedDate\":\"2026-05-30T16:54:16Z\",\"messageBody\":\"The ai-review job was a stub that passed unconditionally after the\\noriginal actionname/ai-review-action@v1 reference was removed.
