Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-16</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

**Description**: The codebase frequently uses `unwrap_or_else(|_| \"{}\".to_string())` or `unwrap_or_default()` when converting agent profiles, task results, and cognitive memories to or from JSON strings. If JSON serialization or parsing fails due to corrupted structure or invalid data types, the error is quietly ignored, returning an empty JSON object or empty defaults, which hides system failures from the supervisor.\n./md-xml/audits.md:4429:  The codebase defines an extensive `SandboxExecutor` in `src/security/sandbox.rs` designed to enforce timeouts, CPU limits, memory limits, and command whitelists. However, **none of the standard language or analysis agents** (such as `GolangProAgent`, `PythonProAgent`, or `RustProAgent`) actually use it. Instead, they all spawn raw processes with the full privileges of the supervisor via:\n./md-xml/audits.md:16425:Several critical internal operations ignore errors without logging or notifying supervisors, violating basic service reliability standards:\n./md-xml/audits.md:16848:   * **Suggestion**: Implement a robust supervisor pattern or health-check monitor to automatically restart the child subprocess inside `ExternalMcpClient`.\n./md-xml/audits.md:16849:   * **Rationale**: The NotebookLM sidecar is spawned as an external node process over stdio (`notebooklm.rs:125`). If this sidecar process unexpectedly dies, exits, or hangs, the parent MCP server continues running in a degraded state without any automated mechanism to respawn or supervise the child.\n./md-xml/audits.md:21113:    The binary parses the environment variable `DINIT_DBUS_READY_FD` to signal daemon readiness back to the supervisor:\n./md-xml/audits.md:22114:*   **Remediation**: Implement structured concurrency by storing these `JoinHandle`s inside the `DbusMirror` struct, monitoring them for exits using `tokio::select!`, or utilizing a supervisor task that restarts failed worker threads.\n./md-xml/audits.md:22208:*   **Remediation**: Check the parsed file descriptor against standard descriptors and verify that the file descriptor is a valid, writable pipe or socket owned by the service supervisor before taking ownership of it. Do not allow raw environment variable overrides without descriptor validation.\n./md-xml/audits.md:22312:  Restrict file descriptor inheritance and validate that the parsed file descriptor is valid, is not a standard stream, and matches expected inherited file descriptors from the parent supervisor.\n./md-xml/audits.md:25184:* **Impact:** Stale or corrupt documents in the SQLite catalog are silently ignored during list operations, which can lead to incomplete runtime state representation without alerting control systems or supervisors via structured logging.\n./md-xml/audits.md:25643:* **Detail**: When listing documents, if a database row contains corrupted or drifted JSON structures, the error is written directly to standard error (`eprintln!`) and the entry is silently skipped. In production control planes, skipping registry entries silently can lead to inconsistent state where registered plugins fail to project without raising proper alerts to supervisory systems. Errors of this nature should be surfaced through structured error propagation or formal logging facades.\n./md-xml/audits.md:38156:  While `tokio::process::Command` does not invoke an intermediate shell (protecting against raw shell-metacharacter execution), it passes the variable `name` directly to the `dinitctl` binary. If `name` begins with a hyphen (e.g., `--help`, `--version`, or target switches specific to dinit), it can cause unexpected command flags to execute, altering binary behavior, logging, or crashing the init supervisor helper.\n./md-xml/audits.md:39773:    *   **Remediation:** Keep track of the `JoinHandle`s and use a task selector or coordinator (such as `tokio::select!` or a supervisor task) to ensure that if any critical listener exits, the parent process is notified or restarts appropriately.\n./md-xml/audits.md:45306:These representations lack any centralized, language-agnostic schema definition. Any modification to these structs will silently alter API boundaries without versioning validations or cross-crd coordination.\n./md-xml/audits.md:61307:Furthermore, if background workers start processes without structured supervision, child processes may become orphaned (zombies), leading to resource leaks on the host control plane.\n./md-xml/audits.md:61311:2. Ensure that any spawned child process is tied to an asynchronous supervisor that terminates the child process when the `McpClient` drop guard is triggered.\n./md-xml/audits.md:67854:        let _ = Command::new(\"s6-svc\").args([\"-d\", svc]).status();\n./md-xml/audits.md:68030:     This value is passed directly to `s6-svc` and `s6-svstat` without validation:\n./md-xml/audits.md:68032:     let _ = Command::new(\"s6-svc\").args([\"-d\", svc]).status();\n./md-xml/audits.md:68034:   * **Risk**: Allows local configuration manipulation of s6 process manager arguments.\n./md-xml/audits.md:68581:*   **`/run/service/ovs-vswitchd`** (`crates/op-network/src/bin/op-ovsbr0-setup.rs:50`): Target s6 control service location.\n./md-xml/audits.md:69206:*   **`stop_vswitchd` / `start_vswitchd`** (`crates/op-network/src/bin/op-ovsbr0-setup.rs:101-140` and `line 161`): Spawns `s6-svc` and `s6-svstat` using service name identifiers derived directly from environment variables.\n./md-xml/audits.md:69298:### HIGH: Privilege Escalation and Service Tampering via Environment-Controlled s6 Service Path\n./md-xml/audits.md:69310:This unvalidated value is then used in administrative child process calls to `s6-svc` and `s6-svstat` under an elevated security context:\n./md-xml/audits.md:69313:let _ = Command::new(\"s6-svc\").args([\"-d\", svc]).status();\n./md-xml/audits.md:69315:let _ = Command::new(\"s6-svc\").args([\"-t\", svc]).status();\n./md-xml/audits.md:69317:let out = Command::new(\"s6-svstat\").arg(svc).output();\n./md-xml/audits.md:69319:let _ = Command::new(\"s6-svc\").args([\"-u\", svc]).status();\n./md-xml/audits.md:69322:An attacker capable of setting environment variables can alter `VSWITCHD_SVC` to reference other critical system services managed by `s6`. When the `op-ovsbr0-setup` tool is executed, it will stop or start arbitrary services, causing system instability or tearing down security defenses.\n./md-xml/audits.md:76583:### LOW: Silent and Unsupervised Fallback to Non-isolated Process Manager\n./md-xml/audits.md:76585:* **Impact**: Bypassed Security & Supervision Policies\n./md-xml/audits.md:76956:  Store the handle and use `tokio::select!` or a supervisor task to exit or restart the daemon if either the gRPC or D-Bus tasks fail.\n./md-xml/audits.md:78199:2. **Suggestion**: Implement a Process Supervision/Monitoring Loop | **Rationale**: The `ProcessManager` spawns processes using `tokio::process::Command` but has no supervision routine to detect when a spawned child unexpectedly dies. This results in the internal state remaining `ManagerState::Running` while the actual process is dead (zombie state). A dedicated tokio supervision task or a signal-handling loop should actively manage and transition service status to `Failed` upon unexpected exit. | **Example**: `crates/op-services/src/manager/process.rs:13`\n./md-xml/audits.md:78418:| **Medium** | **Unhandled Critical Subsystem Failures (Silent Denial of Service)** | `crates/op-services/src/bin/op-services.rs:31`<br>`crates/op-services/src/grpc/server.rs:201` | Replace blind `tokio::spawn` tasks with a robust supervisor pattern. Use coordination primitives like `tokio::select!` or `tokio::try_join!` in the daemon root thread to guarantee that if either the D-Bus or gRPC server loops crash, the entire daemon tears down cleanly, allowing systemd/dinit to trigger a restart. |\n./md-xml/audits.md:78519:    \"recommendation\": \"Replace blind `tokio::spawn` tasks with a robust supervisor pattern. Use coordination primitives like `tokio::select!` or `tokio::try_join!` in the daemon root thread to guarantee that if either the D-Bus or gRPC server loops crash, the entire daemon tears down cleanly, allowing systemd/dinit to trigger a restart.\"\n./md-xml/audits.md:83697:* **Impact**: If the local JSON-RPC server restarts, experiences temporary network pressure, or the system transiently fails to spawn `sh` during a systemd reload, the synchronization loop will immediately return an error and exit permanently. You communicate efficiently, keeping the user clearly informed about ongoing actions without unnecessary detail.\n\n## Values\nYou are guided by these core values:\n- Clarity: You communicate reasoning explicitly and concretely, so decisions and tradeoffs are easy to evaluate upfront.\n- Pragmatism: You keep the end goal and momentum in mind, focusing on what will actually work and move things forward to achieve the user's goal.\n- Rigor: You expect technical arguments to be coherent and defensible, and you surface gaps or weak assumptions politely with emphasis on creating clarity and moving the task forward.\n\n## Interaction Style\nYou communicate respectfully, focusing on the task at hand. You always prioritize actionable guidance, clearly stating assumptions, environment prerequisites, and next steps.\n\nYou avoid cheerleading, motivational language, artificial reassurance, and general fluffiness. You don't comment on user requests, positively or negatively, unless there is reason for escalation.\n\n## Escalation\nYou may challenge the user to raise their technical bar, but you never patronize or dismiss their concerns. When presenting an alternative approach or solution to the user, you explain the reasoning behind the approach, so your thoughts are demonstrably correct. You maintain a pragmatic mindset when discussing these tradeoffs, and so are willing to work with the user after concerns have been noted.\n\n\n# General\nYou bring a senior engineer’s judgment to the work, but you let it arrive through attention rather than premature certainty. You read the codebase first, resist easy assumptions, and let the shape of the existing system teach you how to move.\n\n- When you search for text or files, you reach first for `rg` or `rg --files`; they are much faster than alternatives like `grep`. If `rg` is unavailable, you use the next best tool without fuss.\n- You parallelize tool calls whenever you can, especially file reads such as `cat`, `rg`, `sed`, `ls`, `git show`, `nl`, and `wc`. You use `multi_tool_use.parallel` for that parallelism, and only that. Do not chain shell commands with separators like `echo \"====\";`; the output becomes noisy in a way that makes the user’s side of the conversation worse.\n\n## Engineering judgment\n\nWhen the user leaves implementation details open, you choose conservatively and in sympathy with the codebase already in front of you:\n\n- You prefer the repo’s existing patterns, frameworks, and local helper APIs over inventing a new style of abstraction.\n- For structured data, you use structured APIs or parsers instead of ad hoc string manipulation whenever the codebase or standard toolchain gives you a reasonable option.\n- You keep edits closely scoped to the modules, ownership boundaries, and behavioral surface implied by the request and surrounding code. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-16</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-16T18:43:28.508Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_Moo9PsR02aF3YzcOCQDoujaR","output":"Chunk ID: 52f432\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 809\nOutput:\n# Subid Taxonomy — GhostBridge Operational Routing\n\nThis document is the authoritative subid taxonomy for the GhostBridge host\nconsolidation. It is derived from `oscal-subids-report.md` and is used by the\nGemma routing brain to map subids → tags → OpenFlow flow rules + xray routing\nrules.\n\n## Dual-identifier model\n\n- `uuid` is the immutable machine identity (OSCAL-style).\n- `subid` is the stable human-readable operational taxonomy key.\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs`, `statement_refs`, `control_source`) live in\n  metadata arrays, never inside the `subid` string.\n\n## Canonical subid pattern\n\n```\n<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]\n```\n\n- `category` — one of `src`, `prj`, `sch`, `mut`, `obs`, `evt`, `exp`.\n- `component-type` — OSCAL vocabulary: `service`, `software`, `network`, etc.\n- `subject` — lowercase hyphenated noun (e.g. `xray`, `cognitive-mcp`).\n- `verb` — lowercase hyphenated action (e.g. `serve`, `route`, `monitor`).\n- `facet` — optional qualifier for routing variants.\n- `@vN` — optional version, default `@v1`.\n\n## Routing tags\n\nA routing tag is a short stable label used by both OpenFlow and xray. Each tag\nis declared in the subid registry and maps to one or more subids.\n\nTags used by the host consolidation:\n\n| tag | purpose | primary subid |\n|---|---|---|\n| `xray-tls` | xray TLS ingress on 443 | `src.network.xray-serve@v1` |\n| `xray-reality` | xray REALITY ingress on 8443 | `src.network.xray-serve@v1` |\n| `grpc-bridge` | zeroclaw gateway on 127.0.0.1:18789 | `exp.service.zeroclaw-serve@v1` |\n| `cognitive-mcp` | cognitive MCP on 127.0.0.1:3003 | `exp.service.cognitive-mcp-serve@v1` |\n| `qdrant` | qdrant vector store | `src.service.qdrant-serve@v1` |\n| `netmaker-api` | Netmaker REST API | `src.service.netmaker-api-serve@v1` |\n| `netmaker-mq` | Netmaker message broker | `src.service.netmaker-mq-serve@v1` |\n| `netmaker-ui` | Netmaker dashboard | `exp.service.netmaker-ui-serve@v1` |\n| `nextdns` | local NextDNS resolver | `src.service.nextdns-serve@v1` |\n\n## Subid → tag → xray rule\n\nGemma reads each subid, extracts its tag, and emits an xray routing entry:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"tag\": \"qdrant\",\n  \"subdomains\": [\"qdrant.ghostbridge.tech\"],\n  \"outbound\": \"to-qdrant\"\n}\n```\n\nThe shuttle merges these entries into `routing.rules` before the catch-all rule.\n\n## Subid → tag → OpenFlow rule\n\nGemma also emits OpenFlow rules for the `ovsbr0` privacy bridge. The rules are\npassed to the OpenFlow controller as structured match/action pairs. The exact\nmatch syntax follows the controller's existing privacy-flow convention.\n\nExample:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"tag\": \"netmaker-api\",\n  \"match_fields\": { \"dl_type\": \"0x0800\", \"nw_proto\": \"6\", \"tp_dst\": \"28081\" },\n  \"actions\": [\"output:netmaker-api\"],\n  \"priority\": 100\n}\n```\n\n## Registry location\n\nThe canonical subid registry is `/etc/ghostbridge/subid-registry.json`.\nGemma watches this file (or receives it via D-Bus /dev/shm) and regenerates\nrouting artifacts on change.\n\n## Rules\n\n- `subid` is immutable per subject; material changes require a new `@vN`.\n- `mut.*` records must carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`.\n- `evt.*` records must carry `event_id` or `event_hash`.\n- All records must carry a paired `uuid`.\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-19T09:37:56.163Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-19</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-19T09:38:03.330Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call_output","call_id":"call_ovz80pGsi9KUVt8jV7aNwxxM","output":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.4 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"input_text","text":"---\nname: bash-linux\ndescription: \"Bash/Linux terminal patterns. Critical commands, piping, error handling, scripting. Use when working on macOS or Linux systems.\"\nrisk: unknown\nsource: community\ndate_added: \"2026-02-27\"\n---\n\n# Bash Linux Patterns\n\n> Essential patterns for Bash on Linux/macOS.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Operator Syntax\n\n### Chaining Commands\n\n| Operator | Meaning | Example |\n|----------|---------|---------|\n| `;` | Run sequentially | `cmd1; cmd2` |\n| `&&` | Run if previous succeeded | `npm install && npm run dev` |\n| `\\|\\|` | Run if previous failed | `npm test \\|\\| echo \"Tests failed\"` |\n| `\\|` | Pipe output | `ls \\| grep \".js\"` |\n\n---\n\n## 2. File Operations\n\n### Essential Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n|------|---------|\n| List all | `ls -la` |\n| Find files | `find . -name \"*.js\" -type f` |\n| File content | `cat file.txt` |\n| First N lines | `head -n 20 file.txt` |\n| Last N lines | `tail -n 20 file.txt` |\n| Follow log | `tail -f log.txt` |\n| Search in files | `grep -r \"pattern\" --include=\"*.js\"` |\n| File size | `du -sh *` |\n| Disk usage | `df -h` |\n\n---\n\n## 3. Process Management\n\n| Task | Command |\n|------|---------|\n| List processes | `ps aux` |\n| Find by name | `ps aux \\| grep node` |\n| Kill by PID | `kill -9 <PID>` |\n| Find port user | `lsof -i :3000` |\n| Kill port | `kill -9 $(lsof -t -i :3000)` |\n| Background | `npm run dev &` |\n| Jobs | `jobs -l` |\n| Bring to front | `fg %1` |\n\n---\n\n## 4. Text Processing\n\n### Core Tools\n\n| Tool | Purpose | Example |\n|------|---------|---------|\n| `grep` | Search | `grep -rn \"TODO\" src/` |\n| `sed` | Replace | `sed -i 's/old/new/g' file.txt` |\n| `awk` | Extract columns | `awk '{print $1}' file.txt` |\n| `cut` | Cut fields | `cut -d',' -f1 data.csv` |\n| `sort` | Sort lines | `sort -u file.txt` |\n| `uniq` | Unique lines | `sort file.txt \\| uniq -c` |\n| `wc` | Count | `wc -l file.txt` |\n\n---\n\n## 5. Environment Variables\n\n| Task | Command |\n|------|---------|\n| View all | `env` or `printenv` |\n| View one | `echo $PATH` |\n| Set temporary | `export VAR=\"value\"` |\n| Set in script | `VAR=\"value\" command` |\n| Add to PATH | `export PATH=\"$PATH:/new/path\"` |\n\n---\n\n## 6. Network\n\n| Task | Command |\n|------|---------|\n| Download | `curl -O https://example.com/file` |\n| API request | `curl -X GET https://api.example.com` |\n| POST JSON | `curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"key\":\"value\"}' URL` |\n| Check port | `nc -zv localhost 3000` |\n| Network info | `ifconfig` or `ip addr` |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Script Template\n\n```bash\n#!/bin/bash\nset -euo pipefail  # Exit on error, undefined var, pipe fail\n\n# Colors (optional)\nRED='\\033[0;31m'\nGREEN='\\033[0;32m'\nNC='\\033[0m'\n\n# Script directory\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\n\n# Functions\nlog_info() { echo -e \"${GREEN}[INFO]${NC} $1\"; }\nlog_error() { echo -e \"${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1\" >&2; }\n\n# Main\nmain() {\n    log_info \"Starting...\"\n    # Your logic here\n    log_info \"Done!\"\n}\n\nmain \"$@\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 8. Common Patterns\n\n### Check if command exists\n\n```bash\nif command -v node &> /dev/null; then\n    echo \"Node is installed\"\nfi\n```\n\n### Default variable value\n\n```bash\nNAME=${1:-\"default_value\"}\n```\n\n### Read file line by line\n\n```bash\nwhile IFS= read -r line; do\n    echo \"$line\"\ndone < file.txt\n```\n\n### Loop over files\n\n```bash\nfor file in *.js; do\n    echo \"Processing $file\"\ndone\n```\n\n---\n\n## 9. Differences from PowerShell\n\n| Task | PowerShell | Bash |\n|------|------------|------|\n| List files | `Get-ChildItem` | `ls -la` |\n| Find files | `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` | `find . -type f` |\n| Environment | `$env:VAR` | `$VAR` |\n| String concat | `\"$a$b\"` | `\"$a$b\"` (same) |\n| Null check | `if ($x)` | `if [ -n \"$x\" ]` |\n| Pipeline | Object-based | Text-based |\n\n---\n\n## 10. Error Handling\n\n### Set options\n\n```bash\nset -e          # Exit on error\nset -u          # Exit on undefined variable\nset -o pipefail # Exit on pipe failure\nset -x          # Debug: print commands\n```\n\n### Trap for cleanup\n\n```bash\ncleanup() {\n    echo \"Cleaning up...\"\n    rm -f /tmp/tempfile\n}\ntrap cleanup EXIT\n```\n\n---\n\n> **Remember:** Bash is text-based. Use `&&` for success chains, `set -e` for safety, and quote your variables!\n\n## When to Use\nThis skill is applicable to execute the workflow or actions described in the overview.\n\n## Limitations\n- Use this skill only when the task clearly matches the scope described above.\n- Do not treat the output as a substitute for environment-specific validation, testing, or expert review.\n- Stop and ask for clarification if required inputs, permissions, safety boundaries, or success criteria are missing.\n# Testing Conventions\n\n## File Organization\n- Test files live next to source: `Component.tsx` → `Component.test.tsx`.\n- Integration tests go in `__tests__/integration/` or `crates/tests/`.\n- Rust workspace unit/integration tests must adhere to behavior-focused naming: `should_handle_<scenario>`.\n\n## Test Structure\n- Use descriptive test names: \"should [action] when [condition]\".\n- One assertion per test when possible.\n- Use `beforeEach` for common setup, not `beforeAll`.\n\n## Mocking\n- Mock at the boundary (API calls, not internal functions).\n- Reset mocks in `afterEach`.\n# TypeScript Conventions\n\n## General\n- Use `interface` for object types, `type` for unions/intersections.\n- Avoid `any` - use `unknown` with type guards instead.\n- Export types alongside their implementations.\n\n## React Components\n- Use functional components with TypeScript FC type.\n- Props interfaces should be named `{ComponentName}Props`.\n- Use `React.ReactNode` for children, not `React.ReactChild`.\n\n## Imports\n- Group imports: React, external libs, internal modules, types.\n- Use absolute imports from `@/` prefix.\n- Avoid barrel files (index.ts re-exports) for performance.\n"}]}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-19T09:39:19.840Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"### s6 boot failure diagnosis\n\n**Root cause:** the canonical s6 frontend repository has no `default` bundle, while `/etc/s6/current/scripts/rc.init` always boots runlevel `default`.\n\nPackage transactions touching `/etc/s6/sv/*` automatically run:\n\n```sh\ns6 repository sync\ns6 set commit\ns6 live install\n```\n\nThat regenerates the database from the incomplete repository and removes the manually repaired `default` bundle. The current `/etc/s6/rc/compiled` is only a temporary pinned repair.\n\nAdditional corruption exists: package hooks report stale live service directories (`File exists`), and the old custom bundle was moved to:\n\n```text\n/etc/s6/sv.disabled/default-conflict-20260522/default\n```\n\nSo the next s6 service-package update can break boot again. No files were changed.\n\nConfirm and I’ll prepare the permanent s6 repository repair before diagnosing cognitive-mcp.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:\\n\\n- Pipes: |\\n- Logical operators: &&, ||\\n- Command separators: ;\\n- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)\\n\\nEach resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.\\n\\nExample:\\n\\ngit pull | tee output.txt\\n\\nThis is treated as two command segments:\\n\\n[\\\"git\\\", \\\"pull\\\"]\\n\\n[\\\"tee\\\", \\\"output.txt\\\"]\\n\\nCommands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.\\n\\n## How to request escalation\\n\\nIMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:\\n\\n- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `\\\"require_escalated\\\"`\\n- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. \\\"Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?\\\"\\n- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.\\n\\nIf you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with \\\"require_escalated\\\". {"timestamp":"2026-06-19T09:41:53.928Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call_output","call_id":"call_O3nf9UNaQuy559J0xkDetmFs","output":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.1 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"input_text","text":"#!/bin/sh\n# Safely compile and activate an s6-rc source tree.\n#\n# Never repoints /etc/s6/rc/compiled before s6-rc-update succeeds. Doing so\n# leaves /run/s6-rc/state from the old database paired with a new compiled DB,\n# which makes future s6-rc commands fail with \"unable to read valid state\".\nset -eu\n\nS6_SV=${S6_SV:-/etc/s6/sv}\nS6_ADMIN=${S6_ADMIN:-/etc/s6/adminsv}\nS6_COMPILED_LINK=${S6_COMPILED_LINK:-/etc/s6/rc/compiled}\nS6_DB_ROOT=${S6_DB_ROOT:-/etc/s6/rc}\nLABEL=${1:-local}\n\nif ! command -v s6-rc-compile >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"s6-rc-compile not found\" >&2\n    exit 127\nfi\n\nif ! command -v s6-rc-update >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"s6-rc-update not found\" >&2\n    exit 127\nfi\n\nif [ ! -d \"$S6_SV\" ]; then\n    echo \"service source directory not found: $S6_SV\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [ ! -d \"$S6_ADMIN\" ]; then\n    echo \"admin source directory not found: $S6_ADMIN\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nold_db=\"$(readlink -f \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\nnew_db=\"${S6_DB_ROOT}/compiled-${LABEL}-$(date +%s%N)\"\n\necho \"Compiling s6-rc database: $new_db\"\ns6-rc-compile \"$new_db\" \"$S6_SV\" \"$S6_ADMIN\"\ns6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" check\n\necho \"Updating live s6-rc state to: $new_db\"\nif ! s6-rc-update \"$new_db\"; then\n    echo \"s6-rc-update failed; leaving $S6_COMPILED_LINK unchanged\" >&2\n    [ -n \"$old_db\" ] && echo \"current compiled DB remains: $old_db\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nln -sfnT \"$new_db\" \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\"\necho \"Activated s6-rc database: $new_db\"\n\n    || true\nip route replace \"$GW\" dev \"$BR\" scope link 2>/dev/null || true\nip route replace default via \"$GW\" dev \"$BR\" onlink 2>/dev/null || true\necho \"ovsbr0-static: ${MGMT_ADDR}/${MGMT_PREFIX} on ${BR}, default via ${GW} onlink\"\nSHELL\nchmod +x /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-static/shell_up\n\n# ovsbr0-static must run after ovsbr0-netdev-verify.\ntouch /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-static/dependencies.d/ovsbr0-netdev-verify\n\n# ── 5. ovsbr0-afxdp must run after ovsbr0-static ─────────────────────────────\nlog \"adding ovsbr0-static → ovsbr0-afxdp dependency\"\nmkdir -p /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-afxdp/dependencies.d\ntouch /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-afxdp/dependencies.d/ovsbr0-static\n\n# ── 6. Add ovsbr0-netdev-verify and ovsbr0-static to ovs-stack bundle ─────────\nlog \"adding ovsbr0-netdev-verify to ovs-stack bundle\"\nmkdir -p /etc/s6/sv/ovs-stack/contents.d\ntouch /etc/s6/sv/ovs-stack/contents.d/ovsbr0-netdev-verify\nlog \"adding ovsbr0-static to ovs-stack bundle\"\ntouch /etc/s6/sv/ovs-stack/contents.d/ovsbr0-static\n\n# ── 7. Recompile s6-rc database ──────────────────────────────────────────────\nlog \"recompiling s6-rc database\"\ntmp=\"$(mktemp -d)\"\ns6-rc-compile \"$tmp/db\" /etc/s6/sv /etc/s6/adminsv\ns6-rc-db -c \"$tmp/db\" check && log \"database check passed\"\nstamp=\"$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)\"\n[ -e /etc/s6/rc/compiled ] && mv /etc/s6/rc/compiled \"/etc/s6/rc/compiled.prev-${stamp}\" || true\ncp -a \"$tmp/db\" /etc/s6/rc/compiled\nrm -rf \"$tmp\"\nlog \"s6-rc database updated\"\n\nlog \"\"\nlog \"===== Done =====\"\nlog \"Boot sequence after reboot:\"\nlog \"  ovsbr0-setup   — creates OVS bridge (ovs-vswitchd dependency)\"\nlog \"  ovsbr0-netdev-verify — confirms ovsbr0 stayed netdev\"\nlog \"  ovsbr0-static  — sets 148.113.204.83/32 on ovsbr0, default route onlink\"\nlog \"  ovsbr0-afxdp   — adds eth0 as AF_XDP (IP already on bridge, no gap)\"\nlog \"\"\nlog \"To test NOW without rebooting:\"\nlog \"  sh /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-static/shell_up\"\nlog \"  /usr/local/bin/op-ovsbr0-afxdp up\"\nlog \"  ip addr show ovsbr0 && ip route show\"\n\n# misc bundle\nmkdir -p \"$S6_SV/misc/contents.d\"\nprintf 'bundle\\n' > \"$S6_SV/misc/type\"\ntouch \"$S6_SV/misc/contents.d/op-xdp-final\"\ntouch \"$S6_SV/misc/contents.d/op-xdp-watch\"\ntouch \"$S6_SV/misc/contents.d/op-xdp-watch-log\"\ntouch \"$S6_SV/misc/contents.d/incus\"\ntouch \"$S6_SV/misc/contents.d/incus-log\"\n\n# ovs-stack bundle\nmkdir -p \"$S6_SV/ovs-stack/contents.d\"\ntouch \"$S6_SV/ovs-stack/contents.d/ovsbr0-afxdp\"\n\n# default runlevel\nmkdir -p \"$S6_SV/default\"\nprintf 'bundle\\n' > \"$S6_SV/default/type\"\nprintf '%s\\n' boot sshd fail2ban misc ovs-stack > \"$S6_SV/default/contents\"\n\n# ── 6. s6-rc compile ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nlog \"recompiling s6-rc database\"\ntmp=\"$(mktemp -d \"$S6_RC/compiled.new.XXXXXX\")\"\ns6-rc-compile \"$tmp/db\" \"$S6_SV\" /etc/s6/adminsv\ns6-rc-db -c \"$tmp/db\" check\ncp -a \"$tmp/db\" \"$S6_RC/compiled.new\"\nif [ -e \"$S6_RC/compiled\" ] || [ -L \"$S6_RC/compiled\" ]; then\n    mv \"$S6_RC/compiled\" \"$S6_RC/compiled.previous-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)\"\nfi\nmv \"$S6_RC/compiled.new\" \"$S6_RC/compiled\"\nrm -rf \"$tmp\"\n\n# ── 7. Apply ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nif incus info \"$CT\" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'Status: RUNNING'; then\n    log \"container running — applying hostside setup now\"\n    /usr/local/sbin/op-xdp-wg hostside || log \"warning: hostside returned non-zero\"\n    incus exec \"$CT\" -- systemctl daemon-reload 2>/dev/null || true\nelse\n    log \"container not running — hostside fires via LXC hook on next start\"\nfi\n\nlog \"done\"\n"}]}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-19T09:43:10.492Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call_output","call_id":"call_vjVI1znISP2CUTtPkhjTpODX","output":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.1 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"input_text","text":"#!/bin/sh\n# Safely compile and activate an s6-rc source tree.\n#\n# Never repoints /etc/s6/rc/compiled before s6-rc-update succeeds. Doing so\n# leaves /run/s6-rc/state from the old database paired with a new compiled DB,\n# which makes future s6-rc commands fail with \"unable to read valid state\".\nset -eu\n\nS6_SV=${S6_SV:-/etc/s6/sv}\nS6_ADMIN=${S6_ADMIN:-/etc/s6/adminsv}\nS6_COMPILED_LINK=${S6_COMPILED_LINK:-/etc/s6/rc/compiled}\nS6_DB_ROOT=${S6_DB_ROOT:-/etc/s6/rc}\nLABEL=${1:-local}\n\nif ! command -v s6-rc-compile >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"s6-rc-compile not found\" >&2\n    exit 127\nfi\n\nif ! command -v s6-rc-update >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"s6-rc-update not found\" >&2\n    exit 127\nfi\n\nif [ ! -d \"$S6_SV\" ]; then\n    echo \"service source directory not found: $S6_SV\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [ ! -d \"$S6_ADMIN\" ]; then\n    echo \"admin source directory not found: $S6_ADMIN\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nold_db=\"$(readlink -f \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\nnew_db=\"${S6_DB_ROOT}/compiled-${LABEL}-$(date +%s%N)\"\n\necho \"Compiling s6-rc database: $new_db\"\ns6-rc-compile \"$new_db\" \"$S6_SV\" \"$S6_ADMIN\"\ns6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" check\n\necho \"Updating live s6-rc state to: $new_db\"\nif ! s6-rc-update \"$new_db\"; then\n    echo \"s6-rc-update failed; leaving $S6_COMPILED_LINK unchanged\" >&2\n    [ -n \"$old_db\" ] && echo \"current compiled DB remains: $old_db\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nln -sfnT \"$new_db\" \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\"\necho \"Activated s6-rc database: $new_db\"\n\n"}]}}

-d \"$S6_ADMIN\" ]; then\n-    echo \"admin source directory not found: $S6_ADMIN\" >&2\n+new_db=\"$(readlink -f /etc/s6/repo/compiled/current)\"\n+if [ -z \"$new_db\" ] || [ ! -f \"$new_db/db\" ]; then\n+    echo \"s6 frontend did not produce a compiled database\" >&2\n     exit 1\n fi\n \n-old_db=\"$(readlink -f \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n-new_db=\"${S6_DB_ROOT}/compiled-${LABEL}-$(date +%s%N)\"\n-\n-echo \"Compiling s6-rc database: $new_db\"\n-s6-rc-compile \"$new_db\" \"$S6_SV\" \"$S6_ADMIN\"\n s6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" check\n+if ! s6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" list bundles | grep -Fxq \"$DEFAULT_BUNDLE\"; then\n+    echo \"refusing unsafe database: missing boot bundle '$DEFAULT_BUNDLE'\" >&2\n+    exit 1\n+fi\n \n echo \"Updating live s6-rc state to: $new_db\"\n-if ! Detect local WG IP for bind address resolution.\n    // 2. Write canonical IdentitySled to /dev/shm for Ghostbridge auth.\n    let wg_id = WireGuardIdentity::with_interface(&cli.wg_interface);\n    let wg_ip = wg_id.get_local_ip();\n\n    match wg_id.get_local_pubkey() {\n        Ok(pubkey) => {\n            info!(\n                interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n                pubkey = %pubkey,\n                wg_ip = ?wg_ip,\n                \"Writing WireGuard identity sled to /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat\"\n            );\n            if let Err(e) = write_sled_from_wg(&pubkey) {\n                warn!(\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"Failed to write identity sled — gRPC Ghostbridge auth will not work\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            warn!(\n                interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n                error = %e,\n                \"Could not read WireGuard public key — identity sled not written; \\\n                 set WG_PUBKEY env var to override\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Resolve bind addresses: promote 0.0.0.0 defaults to WG interface IP.\n    let http_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.http, wg_ip.as_deref());\n    let grpc_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.grpc, wg_ip.as_deref());\n\n    info!(\n        http = %http_addr,\n        grpc = %grpc_addr,\n        db = %cli.db,\n        wg_interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n        \"Starting Cognitive MCP Server\"\n    );\n\n    let server = CognitiveMcpServer::new(&cli.db).await?;\n\n    // D-Bus: start first, keep connection alive for the process lifetime.\n    let _dbus_conn = if !cli.no_dbus {\n        match server.start_dbus().await {\n            Ok(conn) => {\n                info!(\"D-Bus registered: org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp\");\n                Some(conn)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                warn!(\"D-Bus registration failed (continuing without it): {e}\");\n                None\n            }\n        }\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n\n    match (cli.no_grpc, cli.no_http) {\n        (true, true) => {\n            eprintln!(\"Error: both --no-grpc and --no-http specified. Nothing to run.\");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n        (true, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE only\");\n            server.start_http_server(&http_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, true) => {\n            info!(\"Running gRPC only\");\n            server.start_grpc_server(&grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE + gRPC\");\n            server.start_dual(&http_addr, &grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n    }\n\n    pub fn memory_store(&self) -> Arc<CognitiveMemoryStore> {\n        self.memory_store.clone()\n    }\n\n    pub fn cozo_shuttle(&self) -> Arc<CozoGraphShuttle> {\n        self.cozo_shuttle.clone()\n    }\n\n    pub fn tool_registry(&self) -> Arc<ToolRegistry> {\n        self.tool_registry.clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Register on the session D-Bus and serve until the connection drops.\n    /// Runs in the background — call this before start_http_server / start_dual.\n    pub async fn start_dbus(&self) -> Result<zbus::Connection, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n        use crate::dbus_interface::CognitiveMcpInterface;\n\n        let conn = zbus::Connection::session().await?;\n        conn.request_name(\"org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp\").await?;\n\n        let iface = CognitiveMcpInterface::new(self.tool_registry.clone());\n        conn.object_server()\n            .at(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/cognitive_mcp\", iface)\n            .await?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            \"Cognitive MCP D-Bus interface registered at /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/cognitive_mcp\"\n        );\n        Ok(conn)\n    }\n\n    pub fn qdrant_shuttle(&self) -> Option<Arc<QdrantSemanticShuttle>> {\n        self.qdrant_shuttle.clone()\n    }\n\n--- prior service log excerpts as root ---\n"}]}}

else {\n            return Ok(());\n        };\n\n        for document in store.list_documents().await? {\n            self.schema_catalog.write().register(document.schema);\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub async fn register(&self, plugin: Arc<dyn StatePlugin>) -> Result<()> {\n        let name = plugin.name().to_string();\n        let storage_path = self.plugin_storage_path(&name);\n        tokio::fs::create_dir_all(&storage_path).await?;\n\n        let dbus_path = Self::plugin_dbus_path(&name);\n\n        if let Some(schema) = plugin.schema() storage_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),\n                    source: \"plugin\".to_string(),\n                };\n                store.upsert_document(&document).await?;\n            }\n\n }\n\n        if let Some(connection) = &*self.dbus_connection.read().await {\n            let host = op_state::dbus_server::PluginDbusHost {\n                plugin: plugin.clone(),\n New (canonical): `org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.Plugins.Net`\n\n/// Root D-Bus object path for the op-dbus system\npub const DBUS_ROOT_PATH: &str = \"/org/opdbus/v1\";\n\n/// Canonical base path for all plugins\npub const PLUGIN_BASE_PATH: &str = \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins\";\n\n/// Base interface name for plugin-related interfaces\npub const PLUGIN_BASE_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.opdbus.v1.Plugin\";\n\n/// Interface for the plugins collection/manager\npub const PLUGINS_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.Plugins\";\n\n/// Base service name (bus name)\npub const BASE_SERVICE_NAME: &str = \"org.opdbus.v1\";\n\n/// Schema file directory for plugins\npub const PLUGIN_SCHEMA_DIR: &str = \"schemas/plugin\";\n\n/// Meta-schema file for plugin validation\npub const PLUGIN_META_SCHEMA: &str = \"schemas/plugin/org.opdbus.plugin.schema.json\";\n\n/// FreeDesktop plugin schema\npub const FREEDESKTOP_SCHEMA: &str = \"schemas/plugin/freedesktop.json\";\n\n/// ObjectManager interface (FreeDesktop standard)\npub const OBJECT_MANAGER_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager\";\n\n/// Properties interface (FreeDesktop standard)\npub const PROPERTIES_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties\";\n\n/// Introspectable interface (FreeDesktop standard)\npub const INTROSPECTABLE_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.freedesktop.DBus.Introspectable\";\n\n/// Peer interface (FreeDesktop standard)\npub const PEER_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.freedesktop.DBus.Peer\";\n\n/// Legacy path prefix - Cognitive MCP Server Binary\n//!\n//! Transports started in parallel:\n//! - HTTP/SSE  (MCP protocol, port 3003)\n//! - gRPC      (CognitiveToolService, port 50052)\n//! - D-Bus     (org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp / /org/opdbus/v1/cognitive)\n//!\n//! On startup the server reads the local WireGuard public key (from the\n//! interface named by $WG_INTERFACE, defaulting to \"netmaker\") and writes the\n//! canonical IdentitySled to /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat so the Ghostbridge\n//! interceptor and Qdrant shuttle can authenticate outbound gRPC calls.\n//!\n//! Bind address resolution order (highest priority first):\n//!   1. COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND / COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND env vars\n//!   2. --http / --grpc CLI flags\n//!   3. WireGuard interface IP detected at startup (if interface is up)\n//!   4. 0.0.0.0 fallback\n\nuse clap::Parser;\nuse op_cognitive_mcp::CognitiveMcpServer;\nuse op_identity::{write_sled_from_wg, WireGuardIdentity};\nuse tracing::{info, warn, Level};\nuse tracing_subscriber::FmtSubscriber;\n\n#[derive(Parser)]\n#[command(name = \"cognitive-mcp-server\")]\n#[command(about = \"Cognitive MCP Server with memory, NotebookLM bridge, gRPC, and D-Bus\")]\nstruct Cli {\n    /// HTTP/SSE server address (MCP protocol).\n    /// If left at 0.0.0.0 the WireGuard interface IP is used when available.\n    /// Override with COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND env var or this flag.\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND\", default_value = \"0.0.0.0:3003\")]\n    http: String,\n\n    /// gRPC server address (CognitiveToolService).\n    /// If left at 0.0.0.0 the WireGuard interface IP is used when available.\n    /// Override with COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND env var or this flag.\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND\", default_value = \"0.0.0.0:50052\")]\n    grpc: String,\n\n    /// CozoDB database path\n    #[arg(\n        long,\n        env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_DB_PATH\",\n        default_value = \"/var/lib/op-cognitive-mcp/memory.db\"\n    )]\n    db: String,\n\n    /// WireGuard interface to read identity from\n    #[arg(long, env = \"WG_INTERFACE\", default_value = \"netmaker\")]\n    wg_interface: String,\n\n    /// Log level\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_LOG_LEVEL\", default_value = \"info\")]\n    log_level: String,\n\n    /// Disable gRPC server\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_DISABLED\")]\n    no_grpc: bool,\n\n    /// Disable HTTP/SSE server\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_HTTP_DISABLED\")]\n    no_http: bool,\n\n    /// Disable D-Bus registration\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_DBUS_DISABLED\")]\n    no_dbus: bool,\n}\n\n/// Promote an `0.0.0.0:PORT` default address to `<wg_ip>:PORT` when the WG\n/// interface is up.  Explicit addresses (not starting with `0.0.0.0:`) are\n/// returned unchanged so env-var or flag overrides always win.\nfn resolve_bind(addr: &str, wg_ip: Option<&str>) -> String {\n    if let Some(rest) = addr.strip_prefix(\"0.0.0.0:\") {\n        if let Some(ip) = wg_ip {\n            return format!(\"{ip}:{rest}\");\n        }\n    }\n    addr.to_string()\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let cli = Cli::parse();\n\n    let level = match cli.log_level.as_str() {\n        \"trace\" => Level::TRACE,\n        \"debug\" => Level::DEBUG,\n        \"warn\" => Level::WARN,\n        \"error\" => Level::ERROR,\n        _ => Level::INFO,\n    };\n\n    let subscriber = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_max_level(level)\n        .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n        .finish();\n    tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(subscriber)?;\n\n    // ── WireGuard identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // 1. Detect local WG IP for bind address resolution.\n    // 2. Write canonical IdentitySled to /dev/shm for Ghostbridge auth.\n    let wg_id = WireGuardIdentity::with_interface(&cli.wg_interface);\n    let wg_ip = wg_id.get_local_ip();\n\n    match wg_id.get_local_pubkey() {\n        Ok(pubkey) => {\n            info!(\n                interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n                pubkey = %pubkey,\n                wg_ip = ?wg_ip,\n                \"Writing WireGuard identity sled to /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat\"\n            );\n            if let Err(e) = write_sled_from_wg(&pubkey) {\n                warn!(\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"Failed to write identity sled — gRPC Ghostbridge auth will not work\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            warn!(\n                interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n                error = %e,\n                \"Could not read WireGuard public key — identity sled not written; \\\n                 set WG_PUBKEY env var to override\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Resolve bind addresses: promote 0.0.0.0 defaults to WG interface IP.\n    let http_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.http, wg_ip.as_deref());\n    let grpc_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.grpc, wg_ip.as_deref());\n\n    info!(\n        http = %http_addr,\n        grpc = %grpc_addr,\n        db = %cli.db,\n        wg_interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n        \"Starting Cognitive MCP Server\"\n    );\n\n    let server = CognitiveMcpServer::new(&cli.db).await?;\n\n    // D-Bus: start first, keep connection alive for the process lifetime.\n    let _dbus_conn = if !cli.no_dbus {\n        match server.start_dbus().await {\n            Ok(conn) => {\n                info!(\"D-Bus registered: org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp\");\n                Some(conn)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                warn!(\"D-Bus registration failed (continuing without it): {e}\");\n                None\n            }\n        }\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n\n    match (cli.no_grpc, cli.no_http) {\n        (true, true) => {\n            eprintln!(\"Error: both --no-grpc and --no-http specified. Nothing to run.\");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n        (true, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE only\");\n            server.start_http_server(&http_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, true) => {\n            info!(\"Running gRPC only\");\n            server.start_grpc_server(&grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE + gRPC\");\n            server.start_dual(&http_addr, &grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n#!/bin/sh\nexec 2>&1\nexport COGNITIVE_MCP_DB_PATH=\"${COGNITIVE_MCP_DB_PATH:-/var/lib/op-dbus/cognitive.db}\"\nexport DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=\"${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS:-unix:path=/run/op-dbus/session-bus.sock}\"\nexport Features:\n//! - Plugin trait with desired state management\n//! - State plugins for network, LXC, systemd, OpenFlow, etc.\n//! - BTRFS subvolume storage per plugin\n//! - Automatic hash footprints for blockchain audit trail\n//! - Auto-creation of missing plugins\n//! - Lifecycle hooks\n//! - Canonical plugin-document persistence into the schema catalog\n\npub mod auto_create;\npub mod builtin;\npub mod canonical;\npub mod chat;\npub mod dynamic_loading;\npub mod plugin;\npub mod registry;\npub mod schema_loader;\npub mod service_def;\npub mod state;\n\n// State plugins - each manages a specific domain\npub mod default_registry;\npub mod state_plugins;\n\npub use auto_create::AutoPlugin;\npub use canonical as plugin_paths;\npub use default_registry::{DefaultPluginRegistry, PluginRegistryConfig};\npub use plugin::{Plugin, PluginCapabilities, PluginContext, PluginMetadata};\npub use registry::PluginRegistry as PluginCatalog;\npub use registry::{PluginRecord, PluginRegistry};\npub use schema_loader::SchemaLoader;\npub use state::{ChangeOperation, DesiredState, StateChange, ValidationResult};\n\n// ── Canonical PluginSchema authority surface ───────────────────────────────\n// \"The plugin is the schema.\" The schema *type* physically lives in the lowest\n// crate (op-state-store, zero workspace deps) to avoid dependency cycles, but\n// op-plugins is the single authoritative *import surface*: every consumer\n// (cognitive-mcp, projection, web, gRPC) imports schema types from `op_plugins`.\n// op-state-store is retired as a public schema surface — code that still (or\n// mistakenly) reaches for the old path can resolve through this alias instead.\npub use op_state_store::plugin_schema::{\n    PluginSchemaBuilder, ValidationResult as SchemaValidationResult,\n};\npub use op_state_store::{Constraint, FieldSchema, FieldType, PluginSchema, ReadOnlyCondition};\n\n/// Canonical input/contract schema for the cognitive-mcp gateway, including the\n/// `code_search` / `code_context` / `code_index` tool inputs (each carrying its\n/// OSCAL subid). This is the authoritative accessor; tools derive their\n/// `input_schema()` from this via `PluginSchema::field_input_schema(...)`.\npub fn cognitive_mcp_plugin_schema() -> PluginSchema {\n    state_plugins::cognitive_mcp::cognitive_mcp_schema()\n}\n\n// Re-export chat types\npub use chat::{\n    ChatMessage, ChatRequest, ChatResponse, ChatRole, ExecutionStatus, TokenUsage, ToolCall,\n};\n\n/// Prelude for convenient imports\npub mod prelude {\n    pub use super::auto_create::AutoPlugin;\n    pub use super::registry::PluginRegistry as PluginCatalog;\n    pub use super::registry::PluginRegistry;\n    pub use super::state::{ChangeOperation, DesiredState, StateChange, ValidationResult};\n\n    // Re-export state plugins\n    pub use super::dynamic_loading::DynamicLoadingPlugin;\n    pub use super::state_plugins::{\n        AdcPlugin, AgentConfigPlugin, AntigravityChatPlugin, AntigravityPlugin, BtrfsPlugin,\n        CognitiveMcpPlugin, CompactMcpPlugin, ConfigPlugin, CronPlugin, CtlPlaneChatbotPlugin,\n        DnsResolverPlugin, EndpointPlugin, ExecutionResult, FactoryPlugin, Fail2banPlugin,\n        FreeDesktopPlugin, FullSystemPlugin, GcloudAdcPlugin, HardwarePlugin, IncusPlugin,\n        KeypairPlugin, KeyringPlugin, KnowledgePlugin, Login1Plugin, LxcPlugin, MailServerPlugin,\n        McpStatePlugin, MemoryPlugin, NetStatePlugin, NetmakerConfig, NetmakerPlugin,\n        OpenFlowObfuscationPlugin, OpenFlowPlugin, OvsBridgePlugin, OvsdbDaemonPlugin,\n        PackageKitPlugin, PciDeclPlugin, PrivacyRouterPlugin, PrivacyRoutesPlugin, ProcfsPlugin,\n        ProxmoxPlugin, ProxyServerPlugin, RovsCommandsPlugin, RtnetlinkPlugin, S6StatePlugin,\n        SchemaRendererPlugin, ServicePlugin, SessDeclPlugin, SoftwarePlugin, ToolDefinition,\n        UnixSocketPlugin, UsersPlugin, WebUiPlugin, WireGuardPlugin, WorkflowsPlugin,\n        ZeroclawPlugin,\n    };\n}\npub mod state_publisher;\n"}]}}
