Verify 8081 listening (`incus exec netmaker -- ss -tlnp | grep 8081`).\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/GhostBridge-Netmaker-engineer-deck.html:6:<title>GhostBridge x Netmaker - Technical Platform Deck</title>\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/GhostBridge-Netmaker-engineer-deck.html:75:    <div class=\"eyebrow reveal\">GhostBridge x Netmaker</div>\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/GhostBridge-Netmaker-engineer-deck.html:77:    <p class=\"lead reveal d2\">Netmaker is the mesh and identity backbone of GhostBridge: a Rust control plane platform-as-a-service for governed AI, schema-authored state, no-NIC service hardening, gRPC over Unix domain sockets (UDS), semantic evidence, and immutable, tamper-evident accountability.</p>\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/GhostBridge-Netmaker-engineer-deck.html:79:      <span class=\"chip\">Netmaker</span><span class=\"chip\">WireGuard</span><span class=\"chip\">D-Bus</span><span class=\"chip\">PluginSchema</span><span class=\"chip\">Xray</span><span class=\"chip\">Incus</span><span class=\"chip\">Open vSwitch</span><span class=\"chip\">OpenFlow</span><span class=\"chip\">gRPC</span><span class=\"chip\">Tonic</span><span class=\"chip\">Gemma</span><span class=\"chip\">Unix domain sockets</span><span class=\"chip\">Qdrant</span><span class=\"chip\">Cozo</span><span class=\"chip\">Voyage</span><span class=\"chip\">OSCAL</span>\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/GhostBridge-Netmaker-engineer-deck.html:88:    <p class=\"lead reveal d2\" style=\"color:var(--mut)\">GhostBridge treats Netmaker/WireGuard identity as link zero. Every governed action carries identity, mutation, schema, policy authority, trace, footprint, and semantic meaning. AI can reason over the evidence, but only the governed layer can mutate state. gRPC is the service plane that moves these contracts between Rust components over Unix domain sockets and controlled bridge paths, and Tonic is the Rust implementation of that gRPC transport.</p>\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/GhostBridge-Netmaker-engineer-deck.html:90:    <div class=\"card reveal\"><h3><span class=\"dot\"></span>Transport</h3><p>Netmaker mesh carries the trusted path. No need to read it\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/cover-note.txt:5:Fair warning: it's a bit more involved than a typical setup — Netmaker ends up\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:1:# GhostBridge — System Overview (Netmaker spin)\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:2:### Pipelines · OSCAL · Vectors · Evidence chain — how it all fits, with Netmaker as the spine\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:4:> A plain-language tour of the whole machine. Each section ends with **\"The Netmaker\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:11:GhostBridge is a **zero-trust control plane** that sits on a **Netmaker mesh** and does three things at once:\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:17:Netmaker is the layer all three stand on: it's the transport *and* the root of identity.\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:27:Netmaker peer (WireGuard)\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:30:Decoy ingress (decoy-wg2)  ── public face is a honeypot; nothing of value here\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:42:Service container           ── netmaker-api / mail / qdrant / assistant …\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:59:### The Netmaker spin\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:60:The data-plane pipeline **starts at a Netmaker handshake** — no mesh, no front door. And the knowledge-plane pipeline ingests **mesh events as graph nodes** (peers, joins, posture changes), so Netmaker activity becomes queryable institutional memory, not just logs.\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:76:### The Netmaker spin\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:77:A Netmaker **peer's identity carries its OSCAL role**. Because identity is derived from the WireGuard relationship (next section), joining the mesh in the **compliance edition** means the peer is *already* an OSCAL principal — its role gates every hop, and its actions emit assessment evidence automatically. The mesh membership and the compliance posture are the same fact.\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:94:### The Netmaker spin\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:95:Mesh state gets embedded too: peer configs, topology changes, and posture snapshots become **semantic vectors**, so an operator (or an AI agent) can ask *\"show me peers that look like the one that misbehaved last month\"* — turning Netmaker telemetry into searchable knowledge.\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:115:### The Netmaker spin\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:116:The **root of the entire chain is the WireGuard PSK** Netmaker manages. The mesh credential is link #0. Every piece of evidence ultimately traces back to \"this Netmaker peer, with this key, at this time.\" Netmaker isn't just transporting the audited traffic — it's the **anchor the whole evidence chain hangs from.**\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:123:            ┌───────────────────────── NETMAKER MESH (WireGuard) ─────────────────────────┐\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:129:   decoy → sled → Xray(header) → A.N.N.A. → service          embed→Qdrant (semantic vectors)\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:137:**Read it as:** Netmaker roots identity → pipelines move and gate traffic → OSCAL vectors decide and document → semantic vectors remember → the evidence chain makes it all provable.\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/pitch/system-overview-netmaker-spin.md:143:> GhostBridge runs on a Netmaker mesh and turns it into a zero-trust, compliance-grade backbone. Traffic flows through a hardened pipeline — decoy ingress, identity sled, Xray header injection, and a per-hop interceptor — where every request is tagged with OSCAL/compliance *vectors* that decide permission and emit audit evidence. In parallel, a knowledge pipeline embeds everything into semantic *vectors* (Qdrant) and a learning graph (Cozo) so the system remembers and reasons. All of it is bound into a hash-linked *evidence chain* whose root is the WireGuard pre-shared key Netmaker already manages. Netmaker isn't a dependency we use — it's the spine: the transport, the root of identity, and link zero of the audit chain.\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/WISHLIST.md:26:| OD-08 | netmaker server down: resolve broker token timeout (stay on decoy `129.153.134.63` vs relocate) | `devops` | BLOCKED | egress works; server relocation decision open |\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/WISHLIST.md:37:| OD-24 | **Nail down registration + accountability loop** — reconcile provision script (CozoDB+Bearer+HTTP) with runtime (sled+header+gRPC); wire Netmaker peer reg | `general-purpose` | TODO | template: `deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh`; see SIGNALS concerns |\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/WISHLIST.md:74:| OD-00b | DNS host repoint → NextDNS (`127.0.0.1`); netmaker egress verified + persisted | `devops` | 2026-06-12 |\n/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/knowledge/transcripts/2026-06-02_ee39c8ab.md:1499:Now the full picture is clear. `op-cognitive-mcp` watches the `netmaker` WireGuard interface for handshakes and writes the identity sled to `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` when a peer connects. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.spawn_agent` without a configured namespace or `to=functions.agents.spawn_agent` with `tool_namespace = \"agents\"`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.\n\nThe goal is to correctly solve the problem in as little time as possible. Therefore, if at any point you can parallelize work by delegating tasks to another agent, you should do so to save time.\n\nAll agents share the same directory. In detail:\n- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.\n- All agents use the same current working directory.\n- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.\n\nThere are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.\n\nDo not spawn sub-agents unless the user explicitly asks for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work."}]}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-20</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

S6 state plugin — manages services via s6-rc on Artix/Chimera Linux.\n//!\n//! AGENTS.md §4 (D-Bus First): This plugin routes ALL control-plane calls\n//! through the `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl` D-Bus object instead of spawning\n//! s6-rc / s6-svc subprocesses directly.  The only exceptions are read-only\n//! enumeration queries (`s6-rc -a list`) which are considered observations.\n//!\n//! OSCAL subids:\n//!   obs.service.s6.list-units@v1    — query_current_state\n//!   mut.service.s6.start-unit@v1    — start via D-Bus\n//!   mut.service.s6.stop-unit@v1     — stop via D-Bus\n//!   mut.service.s6.restart-unit@v1  — restart via D-Bus\n//!   mut.service.s6.reload-unit@v1   — reload via D-Bus\n//!   mut.service.s6.enable-unit@v1   — enable via D-Bus\n//!   mut.service.s6.disable-unit@v1  — disable via D-Bus\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse async_trait::async_trait;\nuse op_state::{\n    ApplyResult, Checkpoint, DiffMetadata, PluginCapabilities, StateAction, StateDiff, StatePlugin,\n};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\n\n/// Path to the s6-rc live directory.\nconst desired_config.units {\n            for u in units.iter_mut() {\n                u.name = normalize_unit_name(&u.name).to_string();\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(current_config == desired_config)\n    }\n\n    async fn create_checkpoint(&self) -> Result<Checkpoint> {\n        let current = self.query_current_state().await?;\n        Ok(Checkpoint {\n            id: format!(\"s6-{}\", chrono::Utc::now().timestamp()),\n            plugin: self.name().to_string(),\n            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),\n            state_snapshot: current,\n            backend_checkpoint: None,\n        })\n    }\n\n    async fn rollback(&self, checkpoint: &Checkpoint) -> Result<()> {\n        let old: S6Config = simd_json::serde::from_owned_value(checkpoint.state_snapshot.clone())?;\n        if let Some(units) = old.units {\n            for unit in units {\n                let base = normalize_unit_name(&unit.name).to_string();\n                match unit.state.as_deref() {\n                    Some(\"active\") => {\n                        let _ = self.dbus.start(&base).await;\n                    }\n                    Some(\"inactive\") => {\n                        let _ = self.dbus.stop(&base).await;\n                    }\n                    _ => {}\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn capabilities(&self) -> PluginCapabilities {\n        PluginCapabilities {\n            supports_rollback: true,\n            supports_checkpoints: true,\n            supports_verification: true,\n            atomic_operations: false,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ── D-Bus client wrapper ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nuse op_state_store::{FieldSchema, FieldType, PluginSchema};\nuse simd_json::json;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tokio::sync::OnceCell;\nuse zbus::{proxy, Connection};\n\n/// D-Bus proxy for `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`.\n#[proxy(\n    default_service = \"org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl\",\n    default_path = \"/org/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl\",\n    interface = \"org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl\"\n)]\ntrait S6Systemctl {\n    /// Start a unit (resolves type at runtime).\n    async fn start(&self, unit: &str) -> zbus::Result<(bool, String)>;\n    /// Stop a unit (resolves type at runtime).\n    async fn stop(&self, unit: &str) -> zbus::Result<(bool, String)>;\n    /// Restart a unit.\n    async fn restart(&self, unit: &str) -> zbus::Result<(bool, String)>;\n    /// Reload a unit.\n    async fn reload(&self, unit: &str) -> zbus::Result<(bool, String)>;\n    /// Enable a unit.\n    async fn enable(&self, unit: &str) -> zbus::Result<(bool, String)>;\n    /// Disable a unit.\n    async fn disable(&self, unit: &str) -> zbus::Result<(bool, String)>;\n    /// Get full status JSON.\n    async fn status(&self, unit: &str) -> zbus::Result<String>;\n"}]}}

This module implements a reader for the `IdentitySled` struct\n//! located in shared memory, following the 3tched Architecture principles.\n\nuse crate::interfaces::{RawEntity, SourceReader};\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse op_identity::read_sled;\nuse simd_json::json;\nuse tracing::debug;\n\n/// Reader that extracts state from the Identity Sled in shared memory.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct IdentitySledReader {\n    /// Source identifier\n    source: String,\n}\n\nimpl IdentitySledReader {\n    /// Creates a new IdentitySledReader\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            source: \"identity-sled\".to_string(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for IdentitySledReader {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SourceReader for IdentitySledReader {\n    fn read_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<RawEntity>> {\n        let mut entities = Vec::new();\n\n        match self.read_sled_entity() {\n            Ok(entity) => entities.push(entity),\n            Err(e) => debug!(\"Sled not available: {}\", e),\n        }\n\n        Ok(entities)\n    }\n\n    fn read_entity(&self, entity_id: &str) -> Result<RawEntity> {\n        if entity_id == \"current\" {\n            self.read_sled_entity()\n        } else {\n            Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"Unknown sled entity: {}\", entity_id))\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn source_id(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.source\n    }\n\n    fn is_available(&self) -> bool {\n        std::path::Path::new(op_identity::SHM_SLED_PATH).exists()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl IdentitySledReader {\n    fn read_sled_entity(&self) -> Result<RawEntity> {\n        let (ptr, _mmap) =\n            read_sled().map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to read sled: {}\", e))?;\n        // SAFETY: `read_sled()` returns a pointer to a valid `IdentitySled` mapped\n        // into shared memory (`/dev/shm`). The `_mmap` guard owns the mapping and\n        // keeps it alive for the duration of this borrow, so the pointer is valid.\n        let sled = unsafe { &*ptr };\n\n        let footprint = hex::encode(sled.hashed_footprint);\n        let pubkey = hex::encode(sled.wireguard_pubkey);\n\n        Ok(RawEntity {\n            entity_type: \"identity.sled\".to_string(),\n            entity_id: \"current\".to_string(),\n            data: json!({\n                \"mutation_index\": sled.mutation_index,\n                \"hashed_footprint\": footprint,\n                \"wireguard_pubkey\": pubkey,\n            }),\n            source: self.source.clone(),\n        })\n    }\n}\n//! Projection Server: Main entry point for the projection system.\n//!\n//! This binary wires together all components of the projection system:\n//! SchemaEngine, ProjectionEngine, EventMaterializer, and SourceReaders.\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse op_projection::*;\nuse parking_lot::Mutex;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\nuse tracing_subscriber::{EnvFilter, FmtSubscriber};\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<()> {\n    // Initialize logging\n    let subscriber = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_env_filter(EnvFilter::from_default_env())\n        .finish();\n    tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(subscriber)?;\n\n    info!(\"Starting Operation-DBus Projection Server\");\n\n    // 1. Initialize Schema Engine\n    let mut schema_engine = SchemaEngine::new();\n\n    let plugin_reader = match SystemPluginReader::new().await {\n        Ok(reader) => reader,\n        Err(error) => {\n            warn!(\n                error = %error,\n                \"Failed to initialize plugin projection reader; continuing with non-plugin sources\"\n            );\n            SystemPluginReader::empty()\n        }\n    };\n\n    for schema in plugin_reader.projection_schemas() {\n        register_schema_if_missing(&mut schema_engine, schema)?;\n    }\n\n    info!(\n        \"Registered initial schemas ({} total)\",\n        schema_engine.list_schemas().len()\n    );\n\n    // 2. Initialize Projection Store and Engine\n    let store = ProjectionStore::new();\n    let validator = SchemaValidator::new(schema_engine.clone());\n    let engine = Arc::new(Mutex::new(ProjectionSystemEngine::new(\n        store.clone(),\n        validator,\n    )));\n\n    // 3. Initialize Access Controller\n    let mut access_controller = ProjectionAccessController::new();\n    access_controller.add_policy(AccessPolicy {\n        id: \"allow-all-read\".to_string(),\n        resource_pattern: \".*\".to_string(),\n        required_permissions: vec![],\n        action: \"read\".to_string(),\n        redact_sensitive: false,\n    });\n\n    info!(\"Projection Server is ready\");\n\n    // 7. D-Bus object server for projections.\n//!\n//! Serves every Projection through org.opdbus.v1.plugins at\n//! /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>. Nothing mounts outside the plugins root:\n//! no plugin means no schema means no object.\n\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tokio::sync::RwLock;\nuse tracing::{debug, info};\nuse zbus::{connection::Builder, interface, object_server::SignalEmitter, Connection};\n\nuse crate::data_models::Projection;\n\n/// A single projected object on the D-Bus object server.\npub struct ProjectedObject {\n    pub entity_type: String,\n    pub entity_id: String,\n    /// JSON-serialized projection data\n    pub data_json: Arc<RwLock<String>>,\n    pub state: Arc<RwLock<String>>,\n}\n\n#[interface(name = \"org.opdbus.v1.plugins.ProjectedObject\")]\nimpl ProjectedObject {\n    /// The schema/entity type for this object (e.g. \"system.memory\")\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn entity_type(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.entity_type\n    }\n\n    /// The unique entity ID within its type\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn entity_id(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.entity_id\n    }\n\n    /// Current projection state: Valid, Quarantined, Degraded, etc.\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn state(&self) -> String {\n        self.state.read().await.clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Full projection data as a JSON string\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn data(&self) -> String {\n        self.data_json.read().await.clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Signal emitted when this object's data changes\n    #[zbus(signal)]\n    async fn updated(emitter: &SignalEmitter<'_>, data_json: &str) -> zbus::Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Derives the D-Bus object path from a projection's entity_type and entity_id.\n///\n/// Every projected object lives under the single plugins root, and nested\n/// objects live under the plugin that produced them. No plugin means no schema\n/// means no object — nothing is ever mounted outside this path.\n///\n/// entity_type \"mail_server\", entity_id \"mail_server\"\n///   → /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/mail_server\n/// entity_type \"plugin.object\", entity_id \"wireguard:/interfaces/0\"\n///   → /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/wireguard/interfaces/0\npub fn projection_path(entity_type: &str, entity_id: &str) -> String {\n    if entity_type == \"plugin.object\" {\n        if let Some((plugin_id, object_path)) = entity_id.split_once(':') {\n            return plugin_object_path(plugin_id, object_path);\n        }\n    }\n\n    op_plugins::canonical::plugin_path(if entity_id.is_empty() {\n        entity_type\n    } else {\n        entity_id\n    })\n}\n\nfn plugin_object_path(plugin_id: &str, object_path: &str) -> String {\n    let mut path = op_plugins::canonical::plugin_path(plugin_id);\n\n    for segment in object_path.split('/').filter(|segment| !segment.is_empty()) {\n        path.push('/');\n        path.push_str(&sanitize_path_segment(segment));\n    }\n\n    path\n}\n\nfn sanitize_path_segment(segment: &str) -> String {\n    let sanitized: String = segment\n        .chars()\n        .filter_map(|c| {\n            if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' {\n                Some(c)\n            } else if c == '-' || c == '.' {\n                Some('_')\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        })\n        .take(255)\n        .collect();\n\n    if sanitized.is_empty() {\n        \"_\".to_string()\n    } else {\n        sanitized\n    }\n}\n\n/// Object state handles for updating in place\ntype ObjectHandles = (Arc<RwLock<String>>, Arc<RwLock<String>>);\n\n/// Manages the set of D-Bus objects served for all projections.\npub struct ProjectionDbusServer {\n    conn: Connection,\n    /// path → data/state handles so we can update in place\n    objects: HashMap<String, ObjectHandles>,\n"}]}}

Any unprivileged local attacker can execute `truncate -s 10 /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` or pre-create a truncated file, instantly causing a Denial of Service (DoS) of the entire high-privileged gRPC control plane by forcing a process crash whenever a new gRPC connection hits port 50051.\ncrates/audits/op-grpc-bridge/06_06_Async_Concurrency_Model.md:49:    The fields `is_valid` and `hashed_footprint` are read from shared memory via standard raw pointer dereferences without utilizing volatile reads (`core::ptr::read_volatile`) or atomic types (e.g., `AtomicBool`). Because the `SchemaEngine` or external processes can concurrently mutate `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` while the gRPC thread is executing the interceptor, this constitutes a data race.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:11:| `SledSnapshot::read()` maps `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` | `crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/sled.rs:35` | `ro` | **SIGBUS Crash**: Maps a file on `tmpfs`. If the file is truncated concurrently, accessing the mapped slice will trigger a SIGBUS and crash the process. Lacks validation of structural bounds. |\ncrates/audits/op-grpc-bridge/07_07_Security_Unsafe_Surface.md:19:* **Risk/Exploitability Assessment:** **CRITICAL**. This mapping reads `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`. There is no validation to ensure that the file's size on disk is equal to or greater than `std::mem::size_of::<IdentitySled>()` before mapping and casting. If a local attacker or a concurrent process truncates this file to 0 bytes or a size smaller than the struct, any subsequent dereference of the mapped pointer will immediately trigger a `SIGBUS` signal, crashing the entire gRPC ingress server (Denial of Service).\ncrates/audits/op-grpc-bridge/07_07_Security_Unsafe_Surface.md:141:| **01** | `interceptor.rs:49-58` | **Critical** | Zero-copy shared memory read is vulnerable to out-of-bounds panic and Denial of Service (SIGBUS) if `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` is truncated or modified. | Check the size of the mapped file against `std::mem::size_of::<IdentitySled>()` before dereferencing, and map the memory with read-only/copy-on-write protections. Add an explicit safety comment. |\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/07_07_Security_Unsafe_Surface.md:11:*   **Analysis**: Memory-mapping a file is inherently unsafe because the underlying file can be truncated or modified by other processes or threads, which violates Rust's memory aliasing and reference validity guarantees. There is no `// SAFETY:` block explaining why this operation is safe, how access to `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` is synchronized, or how the application prevents `SIGBUS` crashes if the file is truncated.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/07_07_Security_Unsafe_Surface.md:128:*   **Details**: The identity exchange between the background identity component and the proxy relies on reading a custom `#[repr(C)]` layout directly from shared memory `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/07_07_Security_Unsafe_Surface.md:165:*   **Impact**: The application memory-maps the file `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` which lives in shared memory (`/dev/shm`). If any other process on the host (including unprivileged local users, depending on file permissions) truncates this file while the proxy is running, any read access to the slice references (e.g. `bytes[..SLED_SIZE]`) will immediately trigger a `SIGBUS` signal. Because `op-mcp-proxy` does not register a custom signal handler to catch and recover from `SIGBUS`, this will cause an ungraceful, unlogged crash (Denial of Service).\ncrates/audits/op-grpc-bridge/16_16_Improvement_Suggestions.md:8:* **Description:** The `ghostbridge_interceptor` function opens the shared memory file `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` and maps it into the process address space using `mmap2`. It immediately casts the raw mapped pointer to `*const IdentitySled` and dereferences its fields:\ncrates/audits/op-grpc-bridge/16_16_Improvement_Suggestions.md:20:* **Exploitability:** Directly exploitable. If `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` is empty (0 bytes) or truncated (e.g., during a Btrfs mutation, system update, or local race condition), dereferencing `sled_ptr` accesses memory outside the mapped backing file pages. This triggers a hardware page fault that causes the OS to deliver an uncaught `SIGSEGV`, instantly terminating the entire multi-threaded Tonic gRPC server on port `50051`. This allows any local user or system state event to cause a complete Denial of Service.\ncrates/audits/op-mcp-proxy/10_10_Documentation_Completeness.md:133:*   **Impact**: The file mapping occurs over `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`. Because memory-mapping a file does not prevent truncation by other processes on the system, any local unprivileged process that can write to `/dev/shm` can truncate this file to 0 bytes. If the file is truncated while `op-mcp-proxy` reads from the `mmap` reference, the OS will raise a `SIGBUS` signal, resulting in an uncatchable immediate crash of the proxy.\ncrates/audits/op-grpc-bridge/17_17_DBus_IPC_Attack_Surface.md:26:  The gRPC middleware interceptor maps a raw database file from the memory-backed file system `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` via `memmap2::MmapOptions::new().map(&file)`. It then immediately casts the raw pointer to a shared memory structure:\ncrates/audits/op-grpc-bridge/17_17_DBus_IPC_Attack_Surface.md:32:  The interceptor **completely fails to validate the size of the mapped file** before casting and dereferencing the pointer. If `plugin_schema.dat` is empty (0 bytes) or smaller than `std::mem::size_of::<IdentitySled>()` (which is $\\ge 73$ bytes), dereferencing `(*sled_ptr)` triggers an immediate segmentation fault (`SIGSEGV`) or bus error (`SIGBUS`) on memory-access. \ncrates/audits/op-grpc-bridge/17_17_DBus_IPC_Attack_Surface.md:33:  Because `/dev/shm` is a world-writable partition on many default Linux systems, any unprivileged local user or compromised container/plugin can truncate `plugin_schema.dat` to 0 bytes. When the next gRPC request is intercepted on port `50051`, the entire gRPC server process crashes instantly, resulting in a persistent Denial of Service (DoS).\ncrates/audits/op-grpc-bridge/17_17_DBus_IPC_Attack_Surface.md:68:  While the global interceptor in `interceptor.rs` verifies that the client has a valid session footprint, **there are no fine-grained role or capability-based authorization checks** inside the gRPC methods themselves. The incoming `actor_id` and `capability_id` parameters are extracted but are purely log/state metadata; they are not evaluated against any access control list (ACL) or capability provider prior to triggering execution on the system bus. \n"}]}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-20T13:05:03.403Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call_output","call_id":"call_2BXSYKzkbrhIu5leeY8C3phd","output":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.1 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"input_text","text":"---\nname: backend-development-feature-development\ndescription: \"Orchestrate end-to-end backend feature development from requirements to deployment. Use when coordinating multi-phase feature delivery across teams and services.\"\nrisk: unknown\nsource: community\ndate_added: \"2026-02-27\"\n---\n\nOrchestrate end-to-end feature development from requirements to production deployment:\n\n[Extended thinking: This workflow orchestrates specialized agents through comprehensive feature development phases - from discovery and planning through implementation, testing, and deployment. Each phase builds on previous outputs, ensuring coherent feature delivery. The workflow supports multiple development methodologies (traditional, TDD/BDD, DDD), feature complexity levels, and modern deployment strategies including feature flags, gradual rollouts, and observability-first development. Agents receive detailed context from previous phases to maintain consistency and quality throughout the development lifecycle.]\n\n## Use this skill when\n\n- Coordinating end-to-end feature delivery across backend, frontend, and data\n- Managing requirements, architecture, implementation, testing, and rollout\n- Planning multi-service changes with deployment and monitoring needs\n- Aligning teams on scope, risks, and success metrics\n\n## Do not use this skill when\n\n- The task is a small, isolated backend change or bug fix\n- You only need a single specialist task, not a full workflow\n- There is no deployment or cross-team coordination involved\n\n## Instructions\n\n1. Confirm feature scope, success metrics, and constraints.\n2. Select a methodology and define phase outputs.\n3. Orchestrate implementation, testing, and security validation.\n4. Prepare rollout, monitoring, and documentation plans.\n\n## Safety\n\n- Avoid production changes without approvals and rollback plans.\n- Validate data migrations and feature flags in staging first.\n\n## Configuration Options\n\n### Development Methodology\n\n- **traditional**: Sequential development with testing after implementation\n- **tdd**: Test-Driven Development with red-green-refactor cycles\n- **bdd**: Behavior-Driven Development with scenario-based testing\n- **ddd**: Domain-Driven Design with bounded contexts and aggregates\n\n### Feature Complexity\n\n- **simple**: Single service, minimal integration (1-2 days)\n- **medium**: Multiple services, moderate integration (3-5 days)\n- **complex**: Cross-domain, extensive integration (1-2 weeks)\n- **epic**: Major architectural changes, multiple teams (2+ weeks)\n\n### Deployment Strategy\n\n- **direct**: Immediate rollout to all users\n- **canary**: Gradual rollout starting with 5% of traffic\n- **feature-flag**: Controlled activation via feature toggles\n- **blue-green**: Zero-downtime deployment with instant rollback\n- **a-b-test**: Split traffic for experimentation and metrics\n\n## Phase 1: Discovery & Requirements Planning\n\n1. **Business Analysis & Requirements**\n   - Use Task tool with subagent_type=\"business-analytics::business-analyst\"\n   - Prompt: \"Analyze feature requirements for: $ARGUMENTS. Define user stories, acceptance criteria, success metrics, and business value. Identify stakeholders, dependencies, and risks. Create feature specification document with clear scope boundaries.\"\n   - Expected output: Requirements document with user stories, success metrics, risk assessment\n   - Context: Initial feature request and business context\n\n2. **Technical Architecture Design**\n   - Use Task tool with subagent_type=\"comprehensive-review::architect-review\"\n   - Prompt: \"Design technical architecture for feature: $ARGUMENTS. Using requirements: [include business analysis from step 1]. Define service boundaries, API contracts, data models, integration points, and technology stack. Consider scalability, performance, and security requirements.\"\n   - Expected output: Technical design document with architecture diagrams, API specifications, data models\n   - Context: Business requirements, existing system architecture\n\n3. **Feasibility & Risk Assessment**\n   - Use Task tool with subagent_type=\"security-scanning::security-auditor\"\n   - Prompt: \"Assess security implications and risks for feature: $ARGUMENTS. Review architecture: [include technical design from step 2]. Identify security requirements, compliance needs, data privacy concerns, and potential vulnerabilities.\"\n   - Expected output: Security assessment with risk matrix, compliance checklist, mitigation strategies\n   - Context: Technical design, regulatory requirements\n\n## Phase 2: Implementation & Development\n\n4. **Backend Services Implementation**\n   - Use Task tool with subagent_type=\"backend-architect\"\n   - Prompt: \"Implement backend services for: $ARGUMENTS. Follow technical design: [include architecture from step 2]. Build RESTful/GraphQL APIs, implement business logic, integrate with data layer, add resilience patterns (circuit breakers, retries), implement caching strategies. Include feature flags for gradual rollout.\"\n   - Expected output: Backend services with APIs, business logic, database integration, feature flags\n   - Context: Technical design, API contracts, data models\n\n5. **Frontend Implementation**\n   - Use Task tool with subagent_type=\"frontend-mobile-development::frontend-developer\"\n   - Prompt: \"Build frontend components for: $ARGUMENTS. Integrate with backend APIs: [include API endpoints from step 4]. Implement responsive UI, state management, error handling, loading states, and analytics tracking. Add feature flag integration for A/B testing capabilities.\"\n   - Expected output: Frontend components with API integration, state management, analytics\n   - Context: Backend APIs, UI/UX designs, user stories\n\n6. **Data Pipeline & Integration**\n   - Use Task tool with subagent_type=\"data-engineering::data-engineer\"\n   - Prompt: \"Build data pipelines for: $ARGUMENTS. Design ETL/ELT processes, implement data validation, create analytics events, set up data quality monitoring. Integrate with product analytics platforms for feature usage tracking.\"\n   - Expected output: Data pipelines, analytics events, data quality checks\n   - Context: Data requirements, analytics needs, existing data infrastructure\n\n## Phase 3: Testing & Quality Assurance\n\n7. **Automated Test Suite**\n   - Use Task tool with subagent_type=\"unit-testing::test-automator\"\n   - Prompt: \"Create comprehensive test suite for: $ARGUMENTS. Write unit tests for backend: [from step 4] and frontend: [from step 5]. Add integration tests for API endpoints, E2E tests for critical user journeys, performance tests for scalability validation. Ensure minimum 80% code coverage.\"\n   - Expected output: Test suites with unit, integration, E2E, and performance tests\n   - Context: Implementation code, acceptance criteria, test requirements\n\n8. **Security Validation**\n   - Use Task tool with subagent_type=\"security-scanning::security-auditor\"\n   - Prompt: \"Perform security testing for: $ARGUMENTS. Review implementation: [include backend and frontend from steps 4-5]. Run OWASP checks, penetration testing, dependency scanning, and compliance validation. Verify data encryption, authentication, and authorization.\"\n   - Expected output: Security test results, vulnerability report, remediation actions\n   - Context: Implementation code, security requirements\n\n9. **Performance Optimization**\n   - Use Task tool with subagent_type=\"application-performance::performance-engineer\"\n   - Prompt: \"Optimize performance for: $ARGUMENTS. Analyze backend services: [from step 4] and frontend: [from step 5]. Profile code, optimize queries, implement caching, reduce bundle sizes, improve load times. Set up performance budgets and monitoring.\"\n   - Expected output: Performance improvements, optimization report, performance metrics\n   - Context: Implementation code, performance requirements\n\n## Phase 4: Deployment & Monitoring\n\n10. **Deployment Strategy & Pipeline**\n    - Use Task tool with subagent_type=\"deployment-strategies::deployment-engineer\"\n    - Prompt: \"Prepare deployment for: $ARGUMENTS. Create CI/CD pipeline with automated tests: [from step 7]. Configure feature flags for gradual rollout, implement blue-green deployment, set up rollback procedures. Create deployment runbook and rollback plan.\"\n    - Expected output: CI/CD pipeline, deployment configuration, rollback procedures\n    - Context: Test suites, infrastructure requirements, deployment strategy\n\n11. **Observability & Monitoring**\n    - Use Task tool with subagent_type=\"observability-monitoring::observability-engineer\"\n    - Prompt: \"Set up observability for: $ARGUMENTS. Implement distributed tracing, custom metrics, error tracking, and alerting. Create dashboards for feature usage, performance metrics, error rates, and business KPIs. Set up SLOs/SLIs with automated alerts.\"\n    - Expected output: Monitoring dashboards, alerts, SLO definitions, observability infrastructure\n    - Context: Feature implementation, success metrics, operational requirements\n\n12. **Documentation & Knowledge Transfer**\n    - Use Task tool with subagent_type=\"documentation-generation::docs-architect\"\n    - Prompt: \"Generate comprehensive documentation for: $ARGUMENTS. Create API documentation, user guides, deployment guides, troubleshooting runbooks. Include architecture diagrams, data flow diagrams, and integration guides. Generate automated changelog from commits.\"\n    - Expected output: API docs, user guides, runbooks, architecture documentation\n    - Context: All previous phases' outputs\n\n## Execution Parameters\n\n### Required Parameters\n\n- **--feature**: Feature name and description\n- **--methodology**: Development approach (traditional|tdd|bdd|ddd)\n- **--complexity**: Feature complexity level (simple|medium|complex|epic)\n\n### Optional Parameters\n\n- **--deployment-strategy**: Deployment approach (direct|canary|feature-flag|blue-green|a-b-test)\n- **--test-coverage-min**: Minimum test coverage threshold (default: 80%)\n- **--performance-budget**: Performance requirements (e.g., <200ms response time)\n- **--rollout-percentage**: Initial rollout percentage for gradual deployment (default: 5%)\n- **--feature-flag-service**: Feature flag provider (launchdarkly|split|unleash|custom)\n- **--analytics-platform**: Analytics integration (segment|amplitude|mixpanel|custom)\n- **--monitoring-stack**: Observability tools (datadog|newrelic|grafana|custom)\n\n## Success Criteria\n\n- All acceptance criteria from business requirements are met\n- Test coverage exceeds minimum threshold (80% default)\n- Security scan shows no critical vulnerabilities\n- Performance meets defined budgets and SLOs\n- Feature flags configured for controlled rollout\n- Monitoring and alerting fully operational\n- Documentation complete and approved\n- Successful deployment to production with rollback capability\n- Product analytics tracking feature usage\n- A/B test metrics configured (if applicable)\n\n## Rollback Strategy\n\nIf issues arise during or after deployment:\n\n1. Immediate feature flag disable (< 1 minute)\n2. Blue-green traffic switch (< 5 minutes)\n3. Full deployment rollback via CI/CD (< 15 minutes)\n4. Database migration rollback if needed (coordinate with data team)\n5. Incident post-mortem and fixes before re-deployment\n\nFeature description: $ARGUMENTS\n\n## Limitations\n- Use this skill only when the task clearly matches the scope described above.\n- Do not treat the output as a substitute for environment-specific validation, testing, or expert review.\n- Stop and ask for clarification if required inputs, permissions, safety boundaries, or success criteria are missing.\n"}]}}

Plugin Reader: Reading from plugins.\n//!\n//! This module implements the `PluginReader` trait by loading the default\n//! runtime plugins, querying their live state, and emitting both top-level\n//! plugin state entities and nested object projections.\n\nuse crate::data_models::{FieldSchema, FieldType, PluginSchema};\nuse crate::interfaces::{PluginLifecycleEvent, PluginReader, RawEntity, SourceReader};\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse op_plugins::DefaultPluginRegistry;\nuse op_state::StatePlugin;\nuse op_state_store::{MemoryStore, StateStore};\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};\nuse std::future::Future;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::{debug, info, warn};\n\nstruct LoadedPlugin {\n    name: String,\n    schema: Option<PluginSchema>,\n    plugin: Arc<dyn StatePlugin>,\n}\n\n/// Reader that extracts live state from runtime plugins.\npub struct SystemPluginReader {\n    /// Source identifier\n    source: String,\n    /// Loaded runtime plugins and their resolved schemas\n    plugins: Vec<LoadedPlugin>,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Debug for SystemPluginReader {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        let plugin_names: Vec<&str> = self\n            .plugins\n            .iter()\n            .map(|plugin| plugin.name.as_str())\n            .collect();\n        f.debug_struct(\"SystemPluginReader\")\n            .field(\"source\", &self.source)\n            .field(\"plugins\", &plugin_names)\n            .finish()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SystemPluginReader {\n    /// Creates an empty reader when plugin bootstrap is unavailable.\n    pub fn empty() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            source: \"plugin\".to_string(),\n            plugins: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Creates a new SystemPluginReader backed by the default runtime plugins.\n    /// Uses MemoryStore — no SQLite, zero drift. Current state = desired state.\n    pub async fn new() -> Result<Self> {\n        let state_store: Arc<dyn StateStore> = Arc::new(MemoryStore::new());\n\n        let registry = DefaultPluginRegistry::new(state_store);\n        let plugins = registry.load_all_plugins().await?;\n        let plugins = plugins\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|plugin| {\n                let name = plugin.name().to_string();\n                let schema = Self::plugin_owned_schema(&name, plugin.schema());\n\n                if schema.is_none() {\n                    warn!(\n                        plugin_id = %name,\n                        \"Plugin has no PluginSchema; top-level state will be projected without plugin-specific validation\"\n                    );\n                }\n\n                LoadedPlugin { name, schema, plugin }\n            })\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n\n        info!(\n            plugin_count = plugins.len(),\n            \"Initialized plugin projection reader\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(Self {\n            source: \"plugin\".to_string(),\n            plugins,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// The schema used to validate nested plugin object projections.\n    pub fn nested_object_projection_schema() -> PluginSchema {\n        let read_only_string = |description: &str| FieldSchema {\n            field_type: FieldType::String,\n            required: true,\n            description: description.to_string(),\n            default: None,\n            example: None,\n            constraints: Vec::new(),\n            read_only: true,\n            read_only_when: None,\n        };\n\n        PluginSchema::builder(\"plugin.object\")\n            .version(\"1.0.0\")\n            .category(\"plugin\")\n            .field(\"plugin_id\", read_only_string(\"Owning plugin identifier\"))\n            .field(\"parent_id\", read_only_string(\"Parent projection entity ID\"))\n            .field(\n                \"object_path\",\n                read_only_string(\"JSON pointer-like path to the nested object\"),\n            )\n            .field(\n                \"value\",\n                FieldSchema {\n                    field_type: FieldType::Any,\n                    required: true,\n                    description: \"Nested object value mirrored from plugin state\".to_string(),\n                    default: None,\n                    example: None,\n                    constraints: Vec::new(),\n                    read_only: true,\n                    read_only_when: None,\n                },\n            )\n            .build()\n    }\n\n    /// Returns all schemas required for plugin state projection.\n    ///\n    /// Plugin schemas are the canonical `PluginSchema` directly — no conversion:\n    /// the plugin is the schema.\n    pub fn projection_schemas(&self) -> Vec<PluginSchema> {\n        let mut schemas = self\n            .plugins\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|plugin| plugin.schema.clone())\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n        schemas.push(Self::nested_object_projection_schema());\n        schemas\n    }\n\n    /// Reads all plugin-backed projection entities asynchronously.\n    pub async fn read_all_async(&self) -> Result<Vec<RawEntity>> {\n        let mut entities = Vec::new();\n\n        for plugin in &self.plugins {\n            entities.extend(self.read_loaded_plugin(plugin).await?);\n        }\n\n        debug!(\n            entity_count = entities.len(),\n            \"Read plugin projection entities\"\n        );\n        Ok(entities)\n    }\n\n    /// Reads all projection entities for a single plugin asynchronously.\n    pub async fn read_plugin_objects_async(&self, plugin_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<RawEntity>> {\n        let requested_id = DefaultPluginRegistry::resolve_requested_plugin_name(plugin_id)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid plugin request '{}'\", plugin_id))?;\n        let requested_plugin;\n        let plugin = match self\n            .plugins\n            .iter()\n            .find(|plugin| plugin.name == requested_id)\n        {\n            Some(plugin) => plugin,\n            None => {\n                requested_plugin = Self::load_requested_plugin(&requested_id).await?;\n                &requested_plugin\n            }\n        };\n\n        self.read_loaded_plugin(plugin).await\n    }\n\n    async fn load_requested_plugin(plugin_id: &str) -> Result<LoadedPlugin> {\n        let state_store: Arc<dyn StateStore> = Arc::new(MemoryStore::new());\n        let registry = DefaultPluginRegistry::new(state_store);\n        let plugin = registry\n            .load_plugin(plugin_id)\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to auto-load requested plugin '{}'\", plugin_id))?;\n        let name = plugin.name().to_string();\n        let schema = Self::plugin_owned_schema(&name, plugin.schema());\n\n        Ok(LoadedPlugin {\n            name,\n            schema,\n            plugin,\n        })\n    }\n\n    fn plugin_owned_schema(plugin_id: &str, schema: Option<PluginSchema>) -> Option<PluginSchema> {\n        match schema {\n            Some(schema) if schema.name == plugin_id => Some(schema),\n            Some(schema) => {\n                warn!(\n                    plugin_id,\n                    schema_name = %schema.name,\n                    \"Ignoring schema whose name does not match the owning plugin\"\n                );\n                None\n            }\n            None => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Reads nested object projections for a single plugin asynchronously.\n    pub async fn read_nested_objects_async(\n        &self,\n        plugin_id: &str,\n        parent_id: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<RawEntity>> {\n        let entities = self.read_plugin_objects_async(plugin_id).await?;\n\n        Ok(entities\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter(|entity| {\n                entity.entity_type == \"plugin.object\"\n                    && entity\n                        .data\n                        .get(\"parent_id\")\n                        .and_then(|value| value.as_str())\n                        == Some(parent_id)\n            })\n            .collect())\n    }\n\n    async fn read_loaded_plugin(&self, plugin: &LoadedPlugin) -> Result<Vec<RawEntity>> {\n        let state = match plugin.plugin.query_current_state().await {\n            Ok(state) => state,\n            Err(error) => {\n                warn!(\n                    plugin_id = %plugin.name,\n                    error = %error,\n                    \"Skipping plugin projection because state query failed\"\n                );\n                return Ok(Vec::new());\n            }\n        };\n\n        let mut entities = vec![RawEntity {\n            entity_type: plugin.name.clone(),\n            entity_id: plugin.name.clone(),\n            data: state.clone(),\n            source: self.source.clone(),\n        }];\n\n        entities.extend(Self::collect_nested_entities(\n            &plugin.name,\n            &state,\n            &self.source,\n        ));\n\n        Ok(entities)\n    }\n\n    fn collect_nested_entities(plugin_id: &str, state: &Value, source: &str) -> Vec<RawEntity> {\n/// persist their canonical plugin documents during registration.\npub struct DefaultPluginRegistry {\n    config: PluginRegistryConfig,\n    state_store: Arc<dyn StateStore>,\n    schema_loader: SchemaLoader,\n}\n\nimpl DefaultPluginRegistry {\n    /// Create a new plugin loader\n    pub fn new(state_store: Arc<dyn StateStore>) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            config: PluginRegistryConfig::default(),\n            state_store,\n            schema_loader: SchemaLoader::new(\"schemas/plugin\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create with custom schema directory\n    pub fn with_schema_dir(\n        state_store: Arc<dyn StateStore>,\n        schema_dir: impl Into<std::path::PathBuf>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            config: PluginRegistryConfig::default(),\n            state_store,\n            schema_loader: SchemaLoader::new(schema_dir),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Validate a plugin has a valid schema file\n    ///\n    /// Returns Ok(()) if schema exists and is valid\n    /// Returns Err if schema is missing or invalid (in strict mode)\n    pub async fn validate_plugin_schema(&self, plugin_name: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        match self.schema_loader.load_schema(plugin_name).await? {\n            Some(_) => Ok(()),\n            None => Err(anyhow!(\n                \"Plugin '{}' has no valid schema file. Expected: schemas/plugin/{}.json\",\n                plugin_name,\n                plugin_name\n            )),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Check if a schema file exists for a plugin\n    pub async fn schema_exists(&self, plugin_name: &str) -> bool {\n        self.schema_loader.schema_exists(plugin_name).await\n    }\n\n    /// Create with custom configuration\n    pub fn with_config(state_store: Arc<dyn StateStore>, config: PluginRegistryConfig) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            config,\n            state_store,\n            schema_loader: SchemaLoader::new(\"schemas/plugin\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create with custom configuration and schema directory\n    pub fn with_config_and_schema_dir(\n        state_store: Arc<dyn StateStore>,\n        config: PluginRegistryConfig,\n        schema_dir: impl Into<std::path::PathBuf>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            config,\n            state_store,\n            schema_loader: SchemaLoader::new(schema_dir),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Resolve user/request-facing plugin references into canonical loader names.\n    ///\n    /// Supports direct names, aliases, and projection paths like\n    /// `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>/...`.\n    ///\n    /// The old `/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/...` spelling is accepted as a\n    /// compatibility alias and normalized to the canonical plural base path.\n    pub fn resolve_requested_plugin_name(requested: &str) -> Result<String> {\n        let trimmed = requested.trim();\n        if trimmed.is_empty() {\n            return Err(anyhow!(\"Plugin identifier cannot be empty\"));\n        }\n\n        let extracted = Self::extract_plugin_name_from_projection_path(trimmed);\n        let from_path = extracted.as_deref().unwrap_or(trimmed);\n        let normalized = from_path\n            .trim()\n            .trim_matches('/')\n            .replace('-', \"_\")\n            .to_lowercase();\n\n        let canonical = match normalized.as_str() {\n            \"network\" => \"net\",\n            \"systemd\" | \"dinit\" | \"service_s6\" => \"s6\",\n            \"web_ui\" | \"webui\" => \"web_ui\",\n            \"mail\" | \"mailserver\" => \"mail_server\",\n            \"privacyroutes\" => \"privacy_routes\",\n            \"privacyrouter\" => \"privacy_router\",\n            \"ovsbridge\" => \"ovsdb_bridge\",\n            \"rtnet\" => \"rtnetlink\",\n            \"sessdecl\" => \"sess_decl\",\n            other => other,\n        };\n\n        Ok(canonical.to_string())\n    }\n\n    fn extract_plugin_name_from_projection_path(requested: &str) -> Option<String> {\n        // Normalize aliases first, then extract the top-level plugin name.\n        let normalized = crate::canonical::normalize_plugin_path(requested)?;\n        normalized\n            .strip_prefix(crate::canonical::PLUGIN_BASE_PATH)?\n            .trim_start_matches('/')\n            .split('/')\n            .find(|segment| !segment.is_empty())\n            .map(|segment| segment.to_string())\n    }\n\n    /// Compatibility shim for older callers. Registration is discovery-based:\n    /// if a state plugin exists, it is loaded.\n    pub async fn load_default_plugins(&self) -> Result<Vec<Arc<dyn op_state::StatePlugin>>> {\n        self.load_all_plugins().await\n    }\n\n    /// Load every built-in plugin implementation so the schema catalog can\n    /// publish the full plugin contract set, not just runtime autoload state.\n    pub async fn load_all_plugins(&self) -> Result<Vec<Arc<dyn op_state::StatePlugin>>> {\n        let mut plugins: Vec<Arc<dyn op_state::StatePlugin>> = Vec::new();\n        let mut plugin_names = Self::available_plugins();\n\n        plugin_names.sort();\n        plugin_names.dedup();\n\n        for plugin_name in plugin_names {\n            match self.load_plugin(&plugin_name).await {\n                Ok(plugin) => {\n                    if !plugin.is_available() {\n                        tracing::info!(\n                            \"Loaded unavailable plugin schema {}: {}\",\n                            plugin_name,\n                            plugin.unavailable_reason()\n                        );\n                    } else {\n                        tracing::info!(\"Loaded plugin schema: {}\", plugin_name);\n                    }\n                    plugins.push(plugin);\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\"Failed to load plugin schema {}: {}\", plugin_name, e);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\"Loaded {} built-in plugin schemas\", plugins.len());\n        Ok(plugins)\n    }\n\n    /// Load a specific plugin by name\n    pub async fn load_plugin(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Arc<dyn op_state::StatePlugin>> {\n        let resolved_name = Self::resolve_requested_plugin_name(name)?;\n        let plugin: Arc<dyn op_state::StatePlugin> = match resolved_name.as_str() {\n            \"mcp\" => {\n                let config_path =\n                    self.get_plugin_config_path(\"mcp\", \"/etc/op-dbus/mcp-config.json\");\n                Arc::new(McpStatePlugin::new(self.state_store.clone(), config_path))\n            }\n            \"zeroclaw\" => Arc::new(ZeroclawPlugin::new()),\n            \"factory\" => Arc::new(FactoryPlugin::new()),\n            \"fail2ban\" => Arc::new(Fail2banPlugin::new()),\n            \"cron\" => Arc::new(CronPlugin::new()),\n//! Runtime plugin catalog.\n//!\n//! The catalog indexes live plugin instances and mirrors plugin-owned\n//! `PluginSchema` documents into the shared schema catalog. Runtime truth stays\n//! with the plugin schema; persisted catalog documents are compatibility\n//! snapshots for consumers that still hydrate from disk.\n\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse op_core::state_publisher::{ChangeType, StatePublisher};\nuse op_dbus_model::{CatalogDocument, SqlitePluginCatalog};\nuse op_state::StatePlugin;\nuse op_state_store::SchemaCatalog;\nuse PluginRegistry {\n    plugins: AsyncRwLock<HashMap<String, PluginRecord>>,\n    base_path: PathBuf,\n    schema_catalog: Arc<RwLock<SchemaCatalog>>,\n    schema_catalog_store: Option<Arc<SqlitePluginCatalog>>,\n    publisher: AsyncRwLock<Option<Arc<dyn StatePublisher>>>,\n    dbus_connection: AsyncRwLock<Option<zbus::Connection>>,\n}\n\nimpl PluginRegistry {\n    pub fn new(base_path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Self {\n        Self::with_schema_catalog_and_store(\n            base_path,\n            Arc::new(RwLock::new(SchemaCatalog::empty())),\n            None,\n        )\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_schema_catalog_and_store(\n        base_path: impl AsRef<Path>,\n        schema_catalog: Arc<RwLock<SchemaCatalog>>,\n        schema_catalog_store: Option<Arc<SqlitePluginCatalog>>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            plugins: AsyncRwLock::new(HashMap::new()),\n            base_path: base_path.as_ref().to_path_buf(),\n            schema_catalog,\n            schema_catalog_store,\n            publisher: AsyncRwLock::new(None),\n            dbus_connection: AsyncRwLock::new(None),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub async fn set_publisher(&self, publisher: Arc<dyn StatePublisher>) {\n        *self.publisher.write().await = Some(publisher);\n    }\n\n    pub async fn set_dbus_connection(&self, connection: zbus::Connection) {\n        *self.dbus_connection.write().await = Some(connection);\n    }\n\n    pub async fn hydrate_catalog_from_store(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let Some(store) = &self.schema_catalog_store else {\n            return Ok(());\n        };\n\n        for document in store.list_documents().await? {\n            self.schema_catalog.write().register(document.schema);\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub async fn register(&self, plugin: Arc<dyn StatePlugin>) -> Result<()> {\n        let name = plugin.name().to_string();\n        let storage_path = self.plugin_storage_path(&name);\n        tokio::fs::create_dir_all(&storage_path).await?;\n\n        let dbus_path = Self::plugin_dbus_path(&name);\n\n        if let Some(schema) = plugin.schema() {\n            self.schema_catalog.write().register(schema.clone());\n\n            if let Some(store) = &self.schema_catalog_store {\n                let document = CatalogDocument {\n                    schema: schema.clone(),\n                    dbus_path: dbus_path.clone(),\n                    service_name: crate::canonical::BASE_SERVICE_NAME.to_string(),\n                    storage_path: storage_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),\n                    source: \"plugin\".to_string(),\n                };\n                store.upsert_document(&document).await?;\n            }\n\n            if let Some(publisher) = &*self.publisher.read().await {\n                let _ = publisher\n                    .publish_change(\n                        name.clone(),\n                        format!(\"schema/{}\", name),\n                        ChangeType::PropertySet,\n                        Some(\"definition\".to_string()),\n                        None,\n                        schema.to_json_schema(),\n                        vec![\"schema\".to_string(), \"plugin\".to_string()],\n                        \"PluginSchema\".to_string(),\n                    )\n                    .await;\n            }\n        } else {\n            warn!(\n                \"Plugin {} has no PluginSchema; it will not enter the schema catalog\",\n                name\n            );\n        }\n\n        if let Some(connection) = &*self.dbus_connection.read().await {\n            let host = op_state::dbus_server::PluginDbusHost {\n                plugin: plugin.clone(),\n                schema_registry: self.schema_catalog.clone(),\n            };\n            if let Err(error) = connection\n                .object_server()\n                .at(dbus_path.as_str(), host)\n                .await\n            {\n                debug!(\"Plugin {} D-Bus host export skipped: {}\", name, error);\n            }\n        }\n\n        self.plugins.write().await.insert(\n            name.clone(),\n            PluginRecord {\n                name,\n                plugin,\n                storage_path,\n                dbus_path,\n            },\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub async fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn StatePlugin>> {\n        self.plugins\n            .read()\n            .await\n            .get(name)\n            .map(|record| record.plugin.clone())\n    }\n\n    pub async fn records(&self) -> Vec<PluginRecord> {\n        self.plugins.read().await.values().cloned().collect()\n    }\n\n    fn plugin_storage_path(&self, name: &str) -> PathBuf {\n        self.base_path.join(Self::sanitize_path_segment(name))\n    }\n\n    fn plugin_dbus_path(name: &str) -> String {\n        crate::canonical::plugin_path(name)\n    }\n\n    fn sanitize_path_segment(segment: &str) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(segment.len());\n        for ch in segment.chars() {\n            if ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || ch == '_' {\n                out.push(ch);\n            } else {\n                out.push('_');\n            }\n        }\n\n        if out.is_empty() {\n            \"_\".to_string()\n        } else {\n            out\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for PluginRegistry {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new(\"/var/lib/op-dbus/plugins\")\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n enforce\n    /// the Absolute Base rule: without a valid schema, no entity exists.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let engine = Self {\n            schemas: HashMap::new(),\n consumers\n        // can immediately detect whether the projection system is alive.\n        let _ = engine.write_schemas_to_shm();\n        engine\n    }\n\n    /// Creates a new SchemaEngine with the given actor and trace ID\n    pub fn with_context(_actor: &str, _trace_id: &str) -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n\n    /// Generates a footprint hash for audit trail using Blake3 (Strike/Etch).\n    fn generate_footprint(&self, schema_name: &str, version: SchemaVersion) -> String {\n        let timestamp = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_nanos_opt().unwrap_or(0);\n        let data = format!(\"{}:{}:{}\", schema_name, version, timestamp);\n        let hash = blake3::hash(data.as_bytes());\n        hash.to_hex().to_string()\n    }\n\n    /// Write the entire schema catalog to shared memory as JSON.\n    /// This is the single source of truth: UI, blockchain, gRPC reflection,\n    /// and all downstream consumers read from this file.\n    pub fn write_schemas_to_shm(&self) -> Result<String> {\n        let catalog: std::collections::HashMap<String, Vec<&PluginSchema>> = self\n            .schemas\n            .iter()\n            .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.iter().collect()))\n            .collect();\n\n        let json_bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&catalog)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to serialize schema catalog: {}\", e))?;\n\n        let mut file = std::fs::File::create(SHM_SCHEMA_PATH)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot write schema SHM: {}\", e))?;\n        file.write_all(&json_bytes)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to write schema SHM: {}\", e))?;\n        file.sync_all()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to sync schema SHM: {}\", e))?;\n\n        let hash = blake3::hash(&json_bytes);\n        let hex = hash.to_hex().to_string();\n        info!(path = SHM_SCHEMA_PATH, footprint = %hex, \"Schema catalog written to shared memory\");\n        Ok(hex)\n    }\n\n    /// Read the Blake3 footprint of the current schema catalog on disk.\n    pub fn read_schema_footprint(&self) -> Result<String> {\n        let bytes = std::fs::read(SHM_SCHEMA_PATH)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot read schema SHM: {}\", e))?;\n        let hash = blake3::hash(&bytes);\n        Ok(hash.to_hex().to_string())\n    }\n\n    /// Generates a trace ID for audit trail\n    fn generate_trace_id(&self) -> String {\n        // In production, use a proper UUID or distributed tracing ID\n        let timestamp = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_nanos_opt().unwrap_or(0);\n        format!(\"trace-{}\", timestamp)\n    }\n\n    /// Records an audit entry for schema changes\n    fn record_audit(&mut self, schema_name: &str, change_type: SchemaChangeType, reason: &str) {\n        let footprint = self.generate_footprint(schema_name, 0);\n        let trace_id = self.generate_trace_id();\n        let change_type_clone = change_type.clone();\n\n        let entry = SchemaAuditEntry {\n            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),\n            actor: \"system\".to_string(),\n            schema_name: schema_name.to_string(),\n            change_type,\n            reason: reason.to_string(),\n            footprint,\n            trace_id,\n        };\n\n        self.audit_trail.push(entry);\n        debug!(\n            schema_name = schema_name,\n            change_type = ?change_type_clone,\n            \"Schema audit entry recorded\"\n//! Projection System: Schema-validated state transformation engine\n//!\n//! The Projection System transforms live authoritative state from diverse sources\n//! (D-Bus, gRPC, procfs, plugin-defined objects) into schema-validated derived\n//! projections for dashboards, orchestration context, audit/compliance, topology,\n//! AI context, and historical replay.\n//!\n//! # Core Principles\n//!\n//! - **Schema-as-Code Authority**: `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth\n//! - **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy)**: Reads from The Sled (`/dev/shm`)\n//! - **Zero-Btrfs Overhead**: Identity extraction uses in-memory environment variables\n//! - **The Accountability Loop**: `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`\n//!\n//! # Modules\n//!\n//! - `data_models`: Core data structures for projections\n//! - `interfaces`: Trait interfaces for projection components\n//! - `schema_engine`: Schema registry and validation\n//! - `schema_validator`: Entity validation services\n//! - `projection_engine`: State transformation engine\n//! - `event_materializer`: Event-driven projection updates\n//! - `json_stream`: Real-time UI delivery\n//! - `access_control`: Access control and redaction\n\npub mod access_control;\npub mod data_models;\npub mod dbus_reader;\npub mod dbus_server;\npub mod event_materializer;\npub mod grpc_reader;\npub mod interfaces;\npub mod json_stream;\npub mod ovsdb_mirror;\npub mod plugin_reader;\npub mod procfs_reader;\npub mod projection_engine;\npub mod projection_store;\npub mod schema_engine;\npub mod schema_validator;\n\n// Re-export core types\npub mod sled_reader;\n\npub use DashboardProjection, EventType, FieldSchema, FieldType,\n    HealthStatus, HistoricalProjection, Link, Node, OrchestrationProjection, PluginSchema,\n    Projection, ProjectionEvent, ProjectionState, dbus_reader::SystemDbusReader;\npub use dbus_server::ProjectionDbusServer;\npub use event_materializer::ProjectionMaterializer;\npub use grpc_reader::SystemGrpcReader;\npub use interfaces::{\n    AccessController, AuditTrail, DbusReader, EventMaterializer, GrpcReader, HistoricalStore,\n    JsonStreamServer, JsonStreamStatus, OvsdbMirrorProjection, PluginLifecycleEvent, PluginReader,\n    ProcfsReader, ProjectionEngine, RawEntity, SchemaRegistry, SourceReader,\n};\npub use json_stream::ProjectionStreamServer;\npub use ovsdb_mirror::OvsdbMirrorProjectionImpl;\npub use
