ChangeSource,\n    ) -> Result<StateChange, String> {\n        if tags.is_empty() {\n            tags = self.compute_tags(&plugin_id, &object_path);\n        }\n\n        let event = {\n            let mut chain = self.event_chain.write().await;\n            let op = match change_type {\n                ChangeType::PropertySet => OperationType::PropertySet,\n                ChangeType::ObjectRemoved => OperationType::Custom(\"delete\".to_string()),\n                _ => OperationType::EmitSignal,\n            };\n            let event = chain.record(\n                actor_id.clone(),\n                plugin_id.clone(),\n                \"1.0.0\".to_string(),\n                op,\n                object_path.clone(),\n                tags.clone(),\n                Decision::Allow,\n                &new_value,\n            );\n            event.clone()\n        };\n\n        self.update_cached_plugin_state(\n            &plugin_id,\n            &object_path,\n            change_type,\n            member_name.as_deref(),\n            &new_value,\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        // Write the plugin's state to the shm projection layer.\n        //\n        // The projection IS the state — `/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/<plugin>.json`\n        // is the single source of truth that the D-Bus tree derives from.\n        // We write a composite object: `data` holds the mutation value, and\n        // `_introspection` holds the D-Bus tree crawl result. The projection\n        // server reads `data` for the `ProjectedObject.Data` property and\n        // derives child paths from it. The `_introspection` field (underscore-\n        // prefixed) is skipped by path derivation so it doesn't create child\n        // objects (no recursive echo).\n        if change_type != ChangeType::ObjectRemoved {\n            let crawl_result = self.crawl_plugin_dbus_tree(&plugin_id).await;\n\n            let projection_value = if let Some(crawl) = crawl_result {\n                simd_json::json!({\n                    \"data\": new_value,\n                    \"_introspection\": crawl,\n                })\n            } else {\n                new_value.clone()\n            };\n\n            match simd_json::to_string(&projection_value) {\n                Ok(json) => {\n                    if let Err(e) =\n                        op_core::projection_shm::write_projection(&plugin_id, json.as_bytes())\n                    {\n                        tracing::warn!(plugin_id = %plugin_id, error = %e, \"Failed to write shm projection\");\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        plugin_id = %plugin_id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"Failed to serialize plugin state for shm projection\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let change = StateChange {\n            change_id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),\n            event_id: event.event_id,\n            plugin_id,\n            object_path,\n            change_type,\n            member_name,\n            old_value,\n            new_value,\n            tags_touched: tags,\n            event_hash: event.event_hash.clone(),\n            timestamp: event.timestamp,\n            actor_id,\n            source,\n        };\n\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-24T11:13:35.870Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_kBDh9GnwzojwZqD0jBSWqxBf","output":"Chunk ID: 5e3d01\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1202\nOutput:\n//! Shared-memory projection layer for the projected plugin tree.\n//!\n//! The projected plugin tree lives in tmpfs (`/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/`).\n//! The MutationEngine writes one file per plugin on every mutation (atomic\n//! temp+rename). The projection D-Bus server reads 1:1 from these files on\n//! every property access — zero-copy, memory-speed, no held cache.\n//!\n//! This module is the shared contract between the **writer** (op-grpc-bridge\n//! MutationEngine, the single write door) and the **reader** (op-projection\n//! D-Bus server). Both depend on op-core, so the path constants and I/O\n//! helpers live here.\n\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io::Write;\n\n/// Directory for per-plugin projection files (one JSON file per plugin).\npub const SHM_PROJECTION_DIR: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/projections\";\n\n/// Manifest carrying the monotonic `generation` counter. Written LAST as the\n/// atomic commit point after each projection write. Consumers read it to\n/// detect staleness (compare generation before/after a read).\npub const SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/.manifest.json\";\n\n/// Atomically publish `bytes` to a `/dev/shm` path via a sibling temp file +\n/// rename, so readers see either the old or new content, never a torn write.\npub fn atomic_write_shm(path: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    let tmp = format!(\"{}.tmp\", path);\n    {\n        let mut file = fs::File::create(&tmp)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot create {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n        file.write_all(bytes)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to write {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n        file.sync_all()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to sync {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n    }\n    fs::rename(&tmp, path)\n        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to rename {} -> {}: {}\", tmp, path, e))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Sanitize a plugin id into a safe flat filename (no path separators or NUL).\nfn safe_filename(plugin_id: &str) -> String {\n    plugin_id\n        .chars()\n        .map(|c| if c == '/' || c == '\\\\' || c == '\\0' { '_' } else { c })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// File path for a specific plugin's projection.\npub fn projection_file_path(plugin_id: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"{}/{}.json\", SHM_PROJECTION_DIR, safe_filename(plugin_id))\n}\n\n/// Write a plugin's full projected state to shm and bump the manifest\n/// generation.\n///\n/// Called by the MutationEngine on every mutation that changes a plugin's\n/// state. `json_bytes` is the JSON serialization of the plugin's current state\n/// (the mutation fold from `state_cache`).\npub fn write_projection(plugin_id: &str, json_bytes: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    fs::create_dir_all(SHM_PROJECTION_DIR).map_err(|e| {\n        anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot create projection dir {}: {}\", SHM_PROJECTION_DIR, e)\n    })?;\n\n    let path = projection_file_path(plugin_id);\n    atomic_write_shm(&path, json_bytes)?;\n\n    // Bump manifest generation (atomic commit point, written last).\n    let generation = read_manifest_generation().wrapping_add(1);\n    let manifest = format!(\"{{\\\"generation\\\":{}}}\", generation);\n    atomic_write_shm(SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST, manifest.as_bytes())?;\n\n    tracing::debug!(plugin_id, generation, \"Projection written to shm\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Read the raw bytes of a plugin's projection from shm.\npub fn read_projection_bytes(plugin_id: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n    fs::read(projection_file_path(plugin_id)).ok()\n}\n\n/// Read the current manifest `generation`, or 0 if no manifest exists yet.\npub fn read_manifest_generation() -> u64 {\n    let mut bytes = match fs::read(SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST) {\n        Ok(b) => b,\n        Err(_) => return 0,\n    };\n    let value = match simd_json::from_slice::<simd_json::OwnedValue>(&mut bytes) {\n        Ok(v) => v,\n        Err(_) => return 0,\n    };\n    match value.get(\"generation\") {\n        Some(g) => g.as_u64().unwrap_or(0),\n        None => 0,\n    }\n}\n\n/// List all plugin ids that currently have projection files in shm.\n///\n/// The manifest file (`.manifest.json`) is excluded. Plugin filenames are\n/// unsanitized back to their original form (the safe-filename transform is\n/// lossless for valid plugin ids).\npub fn list_projected_plugins() -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut plugins = Vec::new();\n    if let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(SHM_PROJECTION_DIR) {\n        for entry in entries.flatten() {\n            if let Some(name) = entry.file_name().to_str() {\n                if let Some(plugin) = name.strip_suffix(\".json\") {\n                    // Skip the manifest (`.manifest.json` → `.manifest`)\n                    if !plugin.starts_with('.') {\n                        plugins.push(plugin.to_string());\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    plugins.sort();\n    plugins\n}\n"}}

The mutation argument is not state; the state is\n+/// the registered service list under the single shared container socket.\n+fn unix_socket_state_after_registration(name: &str, ports: &[u16]) -> simd_json::OwnedValue {\n+    let mut sockets = existing_unix_socket_sockets();\n+    sockets.retain(|socket| {\n+        socket\n+            .get(\"name\")\n+            .and_then(|value| value.as_str())\n+            .map(|existing_name| existing_name != name)\n+            .unwrap_or(true)\n+    });\n+\n+    sockets.push(simd_json::json!({\n+        \"name\": name,\n+        \"path\": op_plugins::state_plugins::unix_socket::SHARED_CONTAINER_SOCKET,\n+        \"ports\": ports,\n+        \"protocol\": \"grpc\",\n+        \"label\": \"\",\n+    }));\n+\n+    simd_json::json!({ \"sockets\": sockets })\n+}\n+\n+fn existing_unix_socket_sockets() -> Vec<simd_json::OwnedValue> {\n+    let Some(mut bytes) = op_core::projection_shm::read_projection_bytes(\"unix_socket\") else {\n+        return Vec::new();\n+    };\n+    let Ok(state) = simd_json::to_owned_value(&mut bytes) else {\n+        return Vec::new();\n+    };\n+\n+    let sockets = state\n+        .get(\"sockets\")\n+        .and_then(|value| value.as_array())\n+        .or_else(|| {\n+            state\n+                .get(\"data\")\n+                .and_then(|data| data.get(\"sockets\"))\n+                .and_then(|value| value.as_array())\n+        });\n+\n+    sockets\n+        .into_iter()\n+        .flatten()\n+        .filter(|socket| {\n+            socket\n+                .get(\"path\")\n+                .and_then(|value| value.as_str())\n+                .is_some()\n+        })\n+        .cloned()\n+        .collect()\n+}\n+\n /// Parse createunixsocket arguments. Accepts either a JSON array\n /// `[name, [ports...]]` or an object `{ \"name\": \"...\", \"ports\": [...] }`.\n /// `ports` may be a JSON array of numbers or a CSV string (\"6334\" / \"6334,8080\").\n"}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * {"timestamp":"2026-06-24T11:41:30.313Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_MyMDF4BUILQrhPFxZvPFY8Xn","output":"Chunk ID: 0a605c\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 871\nOutput:\n//! op-dbus: gRPC server for all Operation services\n//!\n//! Binds to the ovsbr0 interface IPv4 address (discovered at runtime via\n//! rtnetlink) so all Incus containers can reach it through the single OVS\n//! choke point. No hardcoded IP — the address follows whatever ovsbr0 is\n//! assigned.\n//!\n//! Listen address override: `OP_DBUS_GRPC_LISTEN` (e.g. \"0.0.0.0:50051\" for\n//! dev, or an explicit `ip:port`). When unset, op-dbus resolves the first\n//! IPv4 on `OP_DBUS_GRPC_IFACE` (default `ovsbr0`) and binds `<that-ip>:50051`;\n//! if the interface has no IPv4 it falls back to `0.0.0.0:50051`.\n\nuse std::net::SocketAddr;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\nuse tracing_subscriber::{EnvFilter, FmtSubscriber};\n\nuse op_grpc_bridge::run_grpc_server;\nuse op_grpc_bridge::MutationEngine;\nuse op_jsonrpc::nonnet::NonNetDb;\nuse op_network::rovs_proxy::OvsdbDbusClient;\nuse op_network::rtnetlink::list_interfaces;\nuse op_state_store::{ChainConfig, EventChain};\nuse tokio::sync::RwLock;\n\n/// Default port when no explicit listen address is supplied.\nconst DEFAULT_GRPC_PORT: u16 = 50051;\n/// Interface whose IPv4 is used for the default bind address.\nconst DEFAULT_GRPC_IFACE: &str = \"ovsbr0\";\n\n/// Resolve the bind address: explicit `OP_DBUS_GRPC_LISTEN` wins; otherwise\n/// discover the first IPv4 on the configured interface and append the port;\n/// otherwise bind all interfaces.\nasync fn resolve_listen_addr() -> SocketAddr {\n    if let Ok(listen) = std::env::var(\"OP_DBUS_GRPC_LISTEN\") {\n        if let Ok(addr) = listen.parse::<SocketAddr>() {\n            return addr;\n        }\n        warn!(%listen, \"OP_DBUS_GRPC_LISTEN did not parse as SocketAddr; falling back to discovery\");\n    }\n\n    let port: u16 = std::env::var(\"OP_DBUS_GRPC_PORT\")\n        .ok()\n        .and_then(|p| p.parse().ok())\n        .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_GRPC_PORT);\n    let iface = std::env::var(\"OP_DBUS_GRPC_IFACE\")\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| DEFAULT_GRPC_IFACE.to_string());\n\n    if let Ok(interfaces) = list_interfaces().await {\n        if let Some(ni) = interfaces.iter().find(|i| i.name == iface) {\n            if let Some(ip) = ni\n                .addresses\n                .iter()\n                .find(|a| a.family == \"AF_INET\" || a.address.parse::<std::net::Ipv4Addr>().is_ok())\n                .and_then(|a| a.address.split('/').next().map(|s| s.to_string()))\n            {\n                if let Ok(addr) = format!(\"{}:{}\", ip, port).parse::<SocketAddr>() {\n                    info!(iface = %iface, %ip, port, \"discovered ovsbr0 bind address\");\n                    return addr;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    warn!(iface = %iface, \"no IPv4 on interface; binding 0.0.0.0\");\n    format!(\"0.0.0.0:{}\", port)\n        .parse()\n        .expect(\"0.0.0.0:port always parses\")\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    let filter = EnvFilter::try_from_default_env().unwrap_or_else(|_| EnvFilter::new(\"info\"));\n    let _ = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_env_filter(filter)\n        .with_target(false)\n        .compact()\n        .try_init();\n\n    let addr = resolve_listen_addr().await;\n\n    let chain = Arc::new(RwLock::new(EventChain::new(ChainConfig::default())));\n    let ovsdb = Arc::new(OvsdbDbusClient::new());\n    let nonnet = Arc::new(NonNetDb::new());\n    let engine = Arc::new(MutationEngine::new(chain, ovsdb, nonnet));\n\n    info!(addr = %addr, \"op-dbus starting\");\n    run_grpc_server(addr, engine, None, None).await?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-24T11:41:43.153Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_52Pn4eM3DqDe792dRH0XM1CL","output":"Chunk ID: 607b20\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 672\nOutput:\n    /// Live listeners keyed by socket path. Holding the `UnixListener` keeps the\n    /// socket bound for the lifetime of the plugin; dropping it tears it down.\n    active: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, UnixListener>>>,\n}\n\nimpl UnixSocketPlugin {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            active: Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Read this plugin's desired socket set straight from the single active\n    /// schema catalog in shared memory (zero-copy 1:1). The catalog is keyed by\n    /// plugin name and each entry carries the schema-declared state.\n    fn read_desired() -> UnixSocketState {\n        let Ok(mut bytes) = std::fs::read(SHM_SCHEMA_PATH) else {\n            return UnixSocketState::default();\n        };\n        let Ok(catalog) = simd_json::to_owned_value(&mut bytes) else {\n            return UnixSocketState::default();\n        };\n        let Some(state) = catalog\n            .get(\"unix_socket\")\n            .and_then(|versions| versions.as_array())\n            .and_then(|versions| versions.last())\n            .and_then(|schema| schema.get(\"example\"))\n        else {\n            return UnixSocketState::default();\n        };\n        simd_json::serde::from_owned_value::<UnixSocketState>(state.clone()).unwrap_or_default()\n    }\n\n    /// Bind a single endpoint, replacing any stale socket file. Returns `true`\n    /// when a new listener was created.\n    fn ensure_bound(\n        active: &mut HashMap<String, UnixListener>,\n        endpoint: &SocketEndpoint,\n    ) -> Result<bool> {\n        if active.contains_key(&endpoint.path) {\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n        if let Some(parent) = Path::new(&endpoint.path).parent() {\n            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;\n        }\n        if Path::new(&endpoint.path).exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&endpoint.path)?;\n        }\n        let listener = UnixListener::bind(&endpoint.path)?;\n        listener.set_nonblocking(true)?;\n        active.insert(endpoint.path.clone(), listener);\n        info!(\n            socket = %endpoint.path,\n            name = %endpoint.name,\n            ports = ?endpoint.ports,\n            protocol = %endpoint.protocol,\n            \"bound unix socket endpoint\"\n        );\n        Ok(true)\n    }\n\n    /// Drop a listener and unlink its socket file. Returns `true` when removed.\n    fn unbind(active: &mut HashMap<String, UnixListener>, path: &str) -> bool {\n        if active.remove(path).is_some() {\n            if let Err(error) = std::fs::remove_file(path) {\n                warn!(socket = %path, %error, \"failed to unlink unix socket file\");\n            }\n            true\n        } else {\n            false\n        }\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-24T18:05:54.162Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-24</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n"}}

Cognitive MCP Server Binary\n//!\n//! Transports started in parallel:\n//! - HTTP/SSE  (MCP protocol, port 3003)\n//! - gRPC      (CognitiveToolService, port 50052)\n//! - D-Bus state is owned by the canonical plugin projection at\n//!   org.opdbus.v1.plugins / /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/cognitive_mcp\n//!\n//! On startup the server reads the local WireGuard public key (from the\n//! interface named by $WG_INTERFACE, defaulting to \"netmaker\") and writes the\n//! canonical IdentitySled to /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat so the Ghostbridge\n//! interceptor and Qdrant shuttle can authenticate outbound gRPC calls.\n//!\n//! Bind address resolution order (highest priority first):\n//!   1. COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND / COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND env vars\n//!   2. --http / --grpc CLI flags\n//!   3. WireGuard interface IP detected at startup (if interface is up)\n//!   4. 0.0.0.0 fallback\n\nuse clap::Parser;\nuse op_cognitive_mcp::CognitiveMcpServer;\nuse op_identity::{write_sled_from_wg, WireGuardIdentity};\nuse tracing::{info, warn, Level};\nuse tracing_subscriber::FmtSubscriber;\n\n#[derive(Parser)]\n#[command(name = \"cognitive-mcp-server\")]\n#[command(about = \"Cognitive MCP Server with memory, NotebookLM bridge, HTTP, and gRPC\")]\nstruct Cli {\n    /// HTTP/SSE server address (MCP protocol).\n    /// If left at 0.0.0.0 the WireGuard interface IP is used when available.\n    /// Override with COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND env var or this flag.\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND\", default_value = \"0.0.0.0:3003\")]\n    http: String,\n\n    /// gRPC server address (CognitiveToolService).\n    /// If left at 0.0.0.0 the WireGuard interface IP is used when available.\n    /// Override with COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND env var or this flag.\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND\", default_value = \"0.0.0.0:50052\")]\n    grpc: String,\n\n    /// CozoDB database path\n    #[arg(\n        long,\n        env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_DB_PATH\",\n        default_value = \"/var/lib/op-cognitive-mcp/memory.db\"\n    )]\n    db: String,\n\n    /// WireGuard interface to read identity from\n    #[arg(long, env = \"WG_INTERFACE\", default_value = \"netmaker\")]\n    wg_interface: String,\n\n    /// Log level\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_LOG_LEVEL\", default_value = \"info\")]\n    log_level: String,\n\n    /// Disable gRPC server\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_DISABLED\")]\n    no_grpc: bool,\n\n    /// Disable HTTP/SSE server\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_HTTP_DISABLED\")]\n    no_http: bool,\n\n    /// Run stdio transport only (for local MCP clients — direct, no network)\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_STDIO\")]\n    stdio: bool,\n}\n\n/// Promote an `0.0.0.0:PORT` default address to `<wg_ip>:PORT` when the WG\n/// interface is up.  Explicit addresses (not starting with `0.0.0.0:`) are\n/// returned unchanged so env-var or flag overrides always win.\nfn resolve_bind(addr: &str, wg_ip: Option<&str>) -> String {\n    if let Some(rest) = addr.strip_prefix(\"0.0.0.0:\") {\n        if let Some(ip) = wg_ip {\n            return format!(\"{ip}:{rest}\");\n        }\n    }\n    addr.to_string()\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let cli = Cli::parse();\n\n    let level = match cli.log_level.as_str() {\n        \"trace\" => Level::TRACE,\n        \"debug\" => Level::DEBUG,\n        \"warn\" => Level::WARN,\n        \"error\" => Level::ERROR,\n        _ => Level::INFO,\n    };\n\n    let subscriber = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_max_level(level)\n        .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n        .finish();\n    tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(subscriber)?;\n\n    // ── WireGuard identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // 1. Detect local WG IP for bind address resolution.\n    // 2. Write canonical IdentitySled to /dev/shm for Ghostbridge auth.\n    let wg_id = WireGuardIdentity::with_interface(&cli.wg_interface);\n    let wg_ip = wg_id.get_local_ip();\n\n    match wg_id.get_local_pubkey() {\n        Ok(pubkey) => {\n            info!(\n                interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n                pubkey = %pubkey,\n                wg_ip = ?wg_ip,\n                \"Writing WireGuard identity sled to /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat\"\n            );\n            if let Err(e) = write_sled_from_wg(&pubkey) {\n                warn!(\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"Failed to write identity sled — gRPC Ghostbridge auth will not work\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            warn!(\n                interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n                error = %e,\n                \"Could not read WireGuard public key — identity sled not written; \\\n                 set WG_PUBKEY env var to override\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Resolve bind addresses: promote 0.0.0.0 defaults to WG interface IP.\n    let http_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.http, wg_ip.as_deref());\n    let grpc_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.grpc, wg_ip.as_deref());\n\n    info!(\n        http = %http_addr,\n        grpc = %grpc_addr,\n        db = %cli.db,\n        wg_interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n        \"Starting Cognitive MCP Server\"\n    );\n\n    let server = CognitiveMcpServer::new(&cli.db).await?;\n\n    if cli.stdio {\n        info!(\"Running stdio only (local MCP transport)\");\n        server.start_stdio().await?;\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    match (cli.no_grpc, cli.no_http) {\n        (true, true) => {\n            eprintln!(\"Error: both --no-grpc and --no-http specified. Nothing to run.\");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n        (true, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE only\");\n            server.start_http_server(&http_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, true) => {\n            info!(\"Running gRPC only\");\n            server.start_grpc_server(&grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE + gRPC\");\n            server.start_dual(&http_addr, &grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n"}}

Arc<ContextAwarenessEngine>,\n    memory_store: Arc<CognitiveMemoryStore>,\n    session_manager: Arc<SessionManager>,\n) -> Router {\n    let activity_tx = engine.activity_sender();\n\n    let state = ContextServerState {\n        context_engine: engine,\n        activity_tx,\n        memory_store,\n        session_manager,\n    };\n\n    let router = Router::new()\n .route(\"/request_push\", post(request_knowledge_push))\n        .route(\"/health\", get(context_health))\n        .with_state(state);\n\n    info!(\"Context-aware server endpoints registered\");\n state\n        .activity_tx\n        .send(ActivityEvent {\n            session_id: session_id.clone(),\n            activity_type: ActivityType::ToolCall,\n            content: \"Subscribed to context push stream\".to_string(),\n            metadata: serde_json::json!({ \"endpoint\": \"/context/stream\" }),\n        })\n        .await;\n\n    // Subscribe to push notifications\n    let mut push_rx = state.context_engine.subscribe_pushes();\n\n    // Create filtered stream for this session only\n    let stream = async_stream::stream! {\n        // Send initial connection event\n        yield Ok(Event::default()\n            .event(\"connected\")\n            .data(serde_json::json!({\n                \"session_id\": &session_id,\n                \"message\": \"Connected to context Ok(Event::default()\n            .event(\"disconnected\")\n            .data(serde_json::json!({\n                \"session_id\": &session_id,\n                \"message\": \"Context stream ended\",\n                \"timestamp\": chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339()\n            }).to_string()));\n    };\n\n    Sse::new(stream).keep_alive(\n        axum::response::sse::KeepAlive::new()\n            .interval(Duration::from_secs(30))\n            .text(\"keep-alive\"),\n    )\n}\n\n/// Get session context status\nasync fn get_session_status(\n    State(state): State<ContextServerState>,\n }\n            \"--help\" | \"-h\" => {\n                print_help();\n                std::process::exit(0);\n            }\n            other => anyhow::bail!(\"unknown argument: {other}\"),\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(Args { env_file })\n}\n\nfn print_help() {\n    println!(\n        \"op-identity-shuttle\\n\\n\\\nUsage:\\n  op-identity-shuttle [--env-file PATH]\\n\\n\\\nOptions:\\n  --env-file {"timestamp":"2026-06-24T18:12:42.897Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_IBTsfM3iCUrVaGbPdQg7rbmG","output":"Chunk ID: 727fb0\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 639\nOutput:\n#!/bin/sh\n# 🟢 🛷 Safely build, commit and activate the canonical Artix s6 service set.\n#\n# The s6 frontend generates the boot bundle during `s6 set commit`. Compiling\n# /etc/s6/sv directly bypasses that step and can produce a database without the\n# `default` runlevel, which makes the next boot fail in rc.init.\nset -eu\n\nPROJECT_ROOT=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/../..\" && pwd)\nS6_COMPILED_LINK=${S6_COMPILED_LINK:-/etc/s6/rc/compiled}\nDEFAULT_BUNDLE=${DEFAULT_BUNDLE:-default}\n\n# Build the Rust workspace as the unprivileged user who owns the source tree,\n# then install every binary target to /usr/local/bin. This keeps the cargo\n# cache and target directory owned by the developer while allowing the final\n# install and s6 activation to run as root.\nBUILD_USER=${BUILD_USER:-$(logname 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' \"${SUDO_USER:-$USER}\")}\n\nbuild_workspace() {\n    echo \"Building workspace binaries as $BUILD_USER...\"\n    cd \"$PROJECT_ROOT\"\n    sudo -u \"$BUILD_USER\" cargo build --workspace --release\n}\n\ninstall_binaries() {\n    echo \"Installing built binaries to /usr/local/bin...\"\n    cd \"$PROJECT_ROOT\"\n    find target/release -maxdepth 1 -type f -executable -print0 |\n        while IFS= read -r -d '' bin; do\n            install -Dm755 \"$bin\" \"/usr/local/bin/$(basename \"$bin\")\"\n        done\n}\n\nif ! command -v s6 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v s6-rc-db >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"s6 frontend or s6-rc-db not found\" >&2\n    exit 127\nfi\n\nif [ \"${SKIP_BUILD:-}\" != \"1\" ]; then\n    build_workspace\nfi\ninstall_binaries\n\nold_db=\"$(readlink -f \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n\necho \"Synchronizing the canonical s6 repository\"\ns6 repository sync\ns6 set check -F -u\ns6 set commit -f -D \"$DEFAULT_BUNDLE\"\n\nnew_db=\"$(readlink -f /etc/s6/repo/compiled/current)\"\nif [ -z \"$new_db\" ] || [ ! -f \"$new_db/db\" ]; then\n    echo \"s6 frontend did not produce a compiled database\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\ns6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" check\nif ! s6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" list bundles | grep -Fxq \"$DEFAULT_BUNDLE\"; then\n    echo \"refusing unsafe database: missing boot bundle '$DEFAULT_BUNDLE'\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"Updating live s6-rc state to: $new_db\"\nif ! s6 live install -b; then\n    echo \"s6 live install failed; leaving $S6_COMPILED_LINK unchanged\" >&2\n    [ -n \"$old_db\" ] && echo \"current compiled DB remains: $old_db\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nln -sfnT \"$new_db\" \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\"\nif [ \"$(readlink -f \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\")\" != \"$new_db\" ]; then\n    echo \"failed to point bootdb at the committed database\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"Activated s6-rc database: $new_db\"\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-24T18:14:15.330Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_qY5LwkY1GSfmSFVcaW5xDmBm","output":"Chunk ID: e094f2\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 810\nOutput:\n//! D-Bus Projection Client — reads live plugin projections from the /org/opdbus/v1/plugins tree.\n//!\n//! Plugin paths are derived at runtime from /dev/shm/live-schema.json.\n//! Every key in the schema catalog maps to /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin_id>.\n//! No hardcoded paths — if it's not in the schema, it doesn't exist.\n\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tokio::sync::RwLock;\nuse tracing::{debug, info, warn};\nuse zbus::Connection;\n\npub type ProjectionCache = Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, Value>>>;\n\nconst DBUS_SERVICE: &str = op_core::config::OPDBUS_BUS_NAME;\nconst PLUGIN_ROOT: &str = op_core::config::PLUGIN_BASE_PATH;\nconst PROJECTED_OBJECT_IFACE: &str = \"org.opdbus.ProjectedObjectV1\";\nconst SHM_SCHEMA_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/live-schema.json\";\n\nfn plugin_ids_from_schema() -> Vec<String> {\n    let bytes = match std::fs::read(SHM_SCHEMA_PATH) {\n        Ok(b) => b,\n        Err(e) => {\n            warn!(error = %e, \"Could not read live schema; no projections will be cached\");\n            return vec![];\n        }\n    };\n    let mut bytes = bytes;\n    match simd_json::to_owned_value(&mut bytes) {\n        Ok(Value::Object(map)) => map\n            .keys()\n            .filter(|k| *k != \"schema_renderer\")\n            .map(|k| k.to_string())\n            .collect(),\n        _ => {\n            warn!(\"Live schema is not a JSON object; no projections will be cached\");\n            vec![]\n        }\n    }\n}\n\npub async fn start_projection_monitor(cache: ProjectionCache) {\n    let conn = match Connection::system().await {\n        Ok(c) => c,\n        Err(e) => {\n            warn!(error = %e, \"Failed to connect to system D-Bus; projection monitor disabled\");\n            return;\n        }\n    };\n\n    info!(\n        \"Connected to system D-Bus; starting projection monitor for {}\",\n        PLUGIN_ROOT\n    );\n\n    let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5));\n    loop {\n        interval.tick().await;\n        let plugin_ids = plugin_ids_from_schema();\n        for id in &plugin_ids {\n            let path = format!(\"{}/{}\", PLUGIN_ROOT, id);\n            if let Err(e) = refresh_projection(&conn, cache.clone(), id, &path).await {\n                debug!(path = %path, error = %e, \"Projection not available\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn refresh_projection(\n    conn: &Connection,\n    cache: ProjectionCache,\n    plugin_id: &str,\n    path: &str,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let proxy = zbus::Proxy::new(conn, DBUS_SERVICE, path, PROJECTED_OBJECT_IFACE).await?;\n    let data_json: String = proxy.get_property(\"JsonData\").await?;\n    let mut bytes = data_json.into_bytes();\n    let value = simd_json::to_owned_value(&mut bytes)\n        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to parse projection JSON: {}\", e))?;\n    cache.write().await.insert(plugin_id.to_string(), value);\n    debug!(plugin_id = %plugin_id, path = %path, \"Projection cached\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\npub async fn get_projection(cache: &ProjectionCache, entity_type: &str) -> Option<Value> {\n    cache.read().await.get(entity_type).cloned()\n}\n\npub async fn get_all_projections(cache: &ProjectionCache) -> HashMap<String, Value> {\n    cache.read().await.clone()\n}\n"}}

Environment Configuration Loader\n//!\n//! Loads environment variables from the canonical location: `/etc/op-dbus/environment`\n//! This ensures all op-dbus components share the same configuration.\n//!\n//! ## Usage\n//!\n//! Call `load_environment()` early in main() before accessing any config:\n//!\n//! ```rust\n//! use op_core::config::load_environment;\n//!\n//! fn main() {\n//!     load_environment();\n//!     // Now all env vars from /etc/op-dbus/environment are available\n//! }\n//! ```\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse tracing::{debug, info, warn};\n\n/// Canonical D-Bus well-known bus name for the op-dbus system.\n///\n/// All components (op-dbus-mirror, projection_server, rovs_proxy, etc.)\n/// must use this constant instead of hardcoding the string.\npub const OPDBUS_BUS_NAME: &str = \"org.opdbus.v1.plugins\";\n\n/// Canonical base object path for the projected plugin tree.\n///\n/// This is the single stable root anchor; plugin leaves live at\n/// `{PLUGIN_BASE_PATH}/<plugin_id>` and must be derived from it (or discovered\n/// by introspection), never hardcoded with a different spelling. Consumers of the mirror's surfaces (OVSDB JSON-RPC,\n/// ObjectManager) dial this name instead.\npub const MIRROR_BUS_NAME: &str = \"org.opdbus.v1.mirror\";\n\n/// Canonical session bus socket path.  No dash — consistent with `opdbus`\n/// used in D-Bus names, object paths, and shm directories.\npub const SESSION_BUS_SOCKET_PATH: &str = \"/run/opdbus/session-bus.sock\";\n\n/// Canonical session bus address string (for `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`).\npub const SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS: &str = \"unix:path=/run/opdbus/session-bus.sock\";\n\n/// Default path for the environment file\npub const DEFAULT_ENV_FILE: &str = \"/etc/op-dbus/environment\";\n\n/// Alternative paths to check (in order of priority)\npub const ENV_FILE_PATHS: &[&str] = &[\"/etc/op-dbus/environment\", \"/etc/op-dbus.env\", \".env\"];\n\n/// Load environment variables from the canonical configuration file.\n///\n/// This function:\n/// 1. Checks `/etc/op-dbus/environment` first (system-wide)\n/// 2. Falls back to `.env` in current directory (development)\n/// 3. Does NOT override existing environment variables\n///\n/// Returns the path that was loaded, or None if no file was found.\npub fn load_environment() -> Option<String> {\n    // Check if a custom path is specified\n    if let Ok(custom_path) = std::env::var(\"OP_ENV_FILE\") {\n        if let Some(path) = try_load_env_file(&custom_path) {\n            return Some(path);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Try each path in order\n    for path in ENV_FILE_PATHS {\n        if let Some(loaded_path) = try_load_env_file(path) {\n            return Some(loaded_path);\n        }\n    }\n\n    debug!(\"No environment file found, using existing environment\");\n    None\n}\n\n/// Try to load an environment file from the given path.\nfn try_load_env_file(path: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let path_obj = Path::new(path);\n\n    if !path_obj.exists() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    match fs::read_to_string(path_obj) {\n        Ok(content) => {\n            let mut loaded_count = 0;\n            let mut skipped_count = 0;\n\n            for line in content.lines() {\n                let line = line.trim();\n\n                // Skip comments and empty lines\n                if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with('#') {\n                    continue;\n                }\n\n                // Parse KEY=VALUE\n                if let Some((key, value)) = parse_env_line(line) {\n                    // Don't override existing environment variables\n                    if std::env::var(&key).is_err() {\n                        std::env::set_var(&key, &value);\n                        loaded_count += 1;\n                        debug!(\n                            \"Loaded: {}={}\",\n                            key,\n                            if key.contains(\"KEY\")\n                                || key.contains(\"TOKEN\")\n                                || key.contains(\"SECRET\")\n                            {\n                                \"***\"\n                            } else {\n                                &value\n                            }\n                        );\n                    } else {\n                        skipped_count += 1;\n                        debug!(\"Skipped (already set): {}\", key);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            info!(\n                \"Loaded {} environment variables from {} ({} skipped - already set)\",\n                loaded_count, path, skipped_count\n            );\n\n            Some(path.to_string())\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            warn!(\"Failed to read environment file {}: {}\", path, e);\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse a single environment line into key-value pair.\nfn parse_env_line(line: &str) -> Option<(String, String)> {\n    // Handle: KEY=VALUE, KEY=\"VALUE\", KEY='VALUE'\n    let mut parts = line.splitn(2, '=');\n    let key = parts.next()?.trim();\n    let value = parts.next()?.trim();\n\n    if key.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    // Remove surrounding quotes\n    let value = value\n        .strip_prefix('\"')\n        .and_then(|v| v.strip_suffix('\"'))\n        .or_else(|| value.strip_prefix('\\'').and_then(|v| v.strip_suffix('\\'')))\n        .unwrap_or(value);\n\n    Some((key.to_string(), value.to_string()))\n}\n\n/// Get a configuration value with a default.\npub fn get_config(key: &str, default: &str) -> String {\n    std::env::var(key).unwrap_or_else(|_| default.to_string())\n}\n\n/// Get an optional configuration value.\npub fn get_config_opt(key: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    std::env::var(key).ok().filter(|v| !v.is_empty())\n}\n\n/// Get a boolean configuration value.\npub fn get_config_bool(key: &str, default: bool) -> bool {\n    std::env::var(key)\n        .map(|v| matches!(v.to_lowercase().as_str(), \"true\" | \"1\" | \"yes\" | \"on\"))\n        .unwrap_or(default)\n}\n\n/// Get an integer configuration value.\npub fn get_config_int(key: &str, default: i64) -> i64 {\n    std::env::var(key)\n        .ok()\n        .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())\n        .unwrap_or(default)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_parse_env_line_simple() {\n        let (k, v) = parse_env_line(\"FOO=bar\").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(k, \"FOO\");\n        assert_eq!(v, \"bar\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_parse_env_line_quoted() {\n        let (k, v) = parse_env_line(\"FOO=\\\"bar baz\\\"\").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(k, \"FOO\");\n        assert_eq!(v, \"bar baz\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_parse_env_line_single_quoted() {\n        let (k, v) = parse_env_line(\"FOO='bar'\").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(k, \"FOO\");\n        assert_eq!(v, \"bar\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_parse_env_line_empty() {\n        assert!(parse_env_line(\"\").is_none());\n        assert!(parse_env_line(\"=value\").is_none());\n"}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * plugin_state_from_dbus_passthrough(ZEROCLAW_PLUGIN_ID).await\n}\n\npub async fn routes(_cache: &ProjectionCache) -> Option<Vec<ZeroclawRoute>> {\n    let zeroclaw = plugin_state().await?;\n    let model)\n}\n\npub async fn ensure_model_available(cache: &ProjectionCache, model: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    if let Some(route) = route_for_model(cache, model).await {\n        if !route.available {\n
